Still picked, owed: the macOS list watcher's 250 ms look where `daemon.pid` names no live
daemon, which has no event to wait for. `UNWATCHED` is gone (runs-11, below).

**runs-11, built (2026-11-14): no follower and no slot waits on a clock.**
- *`UNWATCHED` (250 ms, picked)*, how often what could not make a file watch looked instead,
  is gone: where no watch can be made, the follower refuses, typed (`daemon::WatchRefused`,
  made by `daemon::watch`), as control-08's log lanes do (27fa453ad). ROOT's ruling, 2026-11-14:
  refuse; no clock fallback, no handle-only mode. A watch needs a descriptor (two on macOS,
  kqueue(2) and its directory's) and on Linux a watch of the process's one inotify instance
  (`max_user_watches`) or an instance of its own (`max_user_instances`, inotify(7); PM M257):
  a host out of them is out of resources the follower could not wait for, and a look's
  interval has no cost to be derived from. Each user:
  - *The listener* makes its three watches (the home, `images/`, `contexts/`) before the
    daemon says it serves (`home_watches`, in `serve`): a daemon that cannot make one does not
    start, its starter told as of any start it cannot make. `listen` takes `[FileWatch; 3]`,
    no `Option`.
  - *`logs -f`* makes each log's watch before any of it is shown, and *`watch processes`*
    its record's: one refused answers `shards: NAME: …: its watch could not be made, so it is
    not followed: …`, status 1, its run's end waiter never asked for. `wait_readable` takes
    no timeout.
  - *A log driver's shipper* makes its watch as it begins to follow: refused, it ends with
    `WatchRefused` (its cause in the daemon's log, as a driver that cannot be made ends it),
    its waiter forgotten and its place kept, so that the shipper its run's next start or the
    daemon's next start makes sends from there.
  Red, each by mutation restoring the fallback or swallowing the refusal:
  `a_follow_no_watch_can_be_made_for_is_refused_before_anything_is_shown` (`logs -f` and
  `watch processes`: before, each followed its run to its end and said nothing),
  `a_shipper_no_watch_can_be_made_for_ends_typed`, and
  `a_daemon_that_cannot_watch_its_home_is_not_started` (each of the three directories). A
  test makes a directory's watch fail by the name `unwatchable` in it (`cfg(test)` only).
- *`SWEEP` (60 s, picked)*, after which a slot taken with no request was marked, and at the
  second removed, is gone (ROOT's ruling, 2026-11-14: the taker names its process and the
  daemon follows its end; a `shards_ipc::slots` protocol change). On Unix:
  - A client names itself as it takes a slot: before it opens anything else of it, it writes
    `PID START` (`this_process`, `Named`) in one write to the slot's sixth FIFO, `N.taker`
    (32 bytes at most: a `u32`'s digits, a space, a `u64`'s, a newline; far under
    `PIPE_BUF`, read whole, POSIX write(2)).
  - `Slot::wait` waits on `say`, its stop and `taker`; once the name comes it tells its
    caller (`Event::Named`) and follows that process: a kqueue of its `EVFILT_PROC`
    `NOTE_EXIT` on macOS, its pidfd on Linux (pidfd_open(2), 5.3), its start checked once its
    end is watched. A taker that ends before its first byte leaves the slot `Gone`, which its
    maker replaces at once; what it wrote before it ended goes first.
  - The gap between a client's read of its record and its name's write is closed by the take
    lock, `requests/taking`: a client holds it shared (flock(2)) from before it reads a record
    until it has named itself, let go of before its file closes (M244); a lock goes with its
    holder's end. Where more slots of a list are taken than have named takers, the maker tries
    it exclusive, never waiting (`Requests::quiet`): held, no client is taking a slot, so a
    slot taken whose name is neither there to read (`Probe`) nor read (its wait says so before
    it reads, drained then) is a taker's that ended in the gap, let go of and another offered.
    Not held, a client is taking one, and its name or its request is an event that brings the
    maker back. A slot left so holds no client's place nor the daemon's quiet; one whose taker
    died in the gap waits for the maker's next event with no client taking.
  - Windows' slots needed none of it: a client takes an instance by opening it, and its end
    ends the instance's reads (M340), so `Slot::wait` is `Gone` already; `probe` is always
    named and `quiet` never held.
  - The take lock is required (legacy4, 2026-11-14). A daemon makes `requests/taking`
    before its lists, under `.taking.new` renamed into place, and makes it again so as it
    makes its lists again (`Requests::renew`), so that every list a client opens has one
    beside it and its name never names nothing. A client that finds a list with none, the
    list's name still naming the FIFO it opened, is refused typed (`Taken::NoTakeLock`,
    "a daemon of a shards from before slots' takers named themselves serves this home ...
    end that daemon's process") and asks nothing; where the list was made again or went
    since it opened it, it looks again. Its hold is `Taking(File)`: the `Option` whose
    `None` took a slot with no hold, "a build's before takers named themselves", is gone,
    as is a client's naming of nothing where a slot has no `N.taker` (`name_taker`'s
    NotFound, now passed over as a slot removed since its offer, as ENXIO is). No release
    made either: the lock and the taker came in 65bf5db0d (2026-11-13), which
    `git tag --contains` names no `v*` for, and v0.7.0's slots have neither; a client and
    its daemon are one build (D36), and such a daemon was served only to step aside, which
    the client now refuses, as it does a daemon from before slots
    (`shards_ipc::PreSlotsDaemon`). Red/green: `a_list_with_no_take_lock_beside_it_is_refused`
    (the slot was taken unheld before), whose rows also hold the lock's file made before
    the lists and anew at a renewal.
  Red, each by mutation: the taker's end not followed (the wait never ends), in
  `slots::fifo::tests::a_slot_whose_taker_ends_before_its_request_is_gone`; the lock not
  asked, and names not looked at, in
  `daemon::slots::tests::a_slot_whose_taker_ended_taking_it_is_let_go_of_while_none_takes`.
  Also `the_daemon_holds_the_take_lock_only_while_no_client_takes_a_slot`.
  Owed to ROOT: a client killed between take and request on HVF, KVM and WHP hosts, its slot
  re-offered as it ends (`cargo test -p shards --profile test-release --test daemon`); the
  client path's added cost (an flock pair, a FIFO's open and write) by
  `docs/research/measurements/build-ab/ab.py` against e0e21e89b.

- *`TAKEOVER` (20 s, picked)*, after which a daemon waiting for its home's lock stepped aside
  as if another served, is gone: it waits while the lock's holder lives (`take_lock`). A lock
  held is a holder that lives: flock(2) and LockFileEx are let go of by the OS as their
  holder's last descriptor closes, at its end, so the lock is the holder's life with no ID to
  misread and no gap. Its identity is the home's `daemon.pid` (`Named`, `PID START`), which a
  daemon writes right after it takes the lock and before it makes its slots' lists; not the
  lock's own file, as the runs-fixes design first had it: std's `File::try_lock` on Windows is
  LockFileEx over the whole file (offset 0, length `u64::MAX`), and a region locked so "denies
  all other processes both read and write access" (LockFileEx's documentation), so no waiter
  could read a name there. A `daemon.pid` that names no living process (one a crashed daemon
  left, or none) while the lock is held is a holder between its lock and its name: followed by
  its lock alone, and judged anew once named.
  - Judged by D215's judge once the host has shown a start: each daemon keeps, as it makes its
    slots' lists, how long it took from its lock (`ends::End::Start`, the home's `ends`
    record's `start MS`, the slowest kept, as `ends.rs` keeps its other ends). A waiter looks
    at the named holder one slice (that slowest start) after it first sees it named, and each
    slice after while it goes on (`ends::Followed::goes_on`: any CPU, memory its host frees,
    or its host holding it); one that has gone on with nothing for a whole slice is refused,
    typed (`HolderStalled`: its process and the slice), the waiter's starter and so its client
    told. Cold, a home with no start kept: the lock alone, however long. A holder ending its
    runs (`shards_ipc::exiting`) is not judged: its runs' stop timeouts bound it, as before.
  - No home is taken, and no wait given up, on a clock. A waiter that gives up takes nothing:
    its client then waits on the holder itself (`ask_slot`, while `daemon.pid` lives), as
    before.
  Red: `a_daemon_waits_for_its_homes_lock_while_its_holder_lives` by mutation restoring the
  20 s (it stepped aside at 20 s while its holder lived; green, it took the home as the lock
  was let go, after 21 s); `a_starting_holder_that_goes_on_with_nothing_for_the_hosts_slowest_start_is_refused`
  by mutation never refusing (a sleep named as the holder was waited for on). Still picked,
  owed: the 10 ms between the waiter's looks at the lock and the lists (D222's row: a blocking
  `File::lock` on a helper thread and a watch of `requests/`). Owed to ROOT: a start's lock to
  lists on HVF, KVM and WHP hosts, loaded and quiet, from the `start` lines the home's `ends`
  keeps, and two daemons started at once on each (`cargo test -p shards --profile test-release
  --test daemon`).

Held by unit tests: `a_request_cut_tells_its_client_to_ask_again` (red before: its slot ended
unanswered), `a_requests_wait_is_learned_from_its_clients`,
`a_client_no_descriptor_is_left_for_is_refused_with_the_spare`,
`a_closed_daemon_is_not_held_by_a_slot_whose_answer_is_said`,
`no_collection_starts_while_the_listener_is_starved` (now woken by `wake_listener`; red
before), the closed daemon's slot tests at their new wait, and shards_ipc's
`a_daemon_whose_id_another_process_has_now_does_not_live`,
`a_daemon_is_exiting_while_its_process_lives`,
`a_list_without_a_live_pid_still_ends_with_its_writer` (a reused ID among its cases). Owed:
the daemon E2E suite (its slots, `daemon stop`, a stepping-aside daemon), an E2E of a daemon
out of descriptors (RLIMIT_NOFILE lowered for it alone), the Windows named pipe refusal on a
Windows host, the 8-target lint, and CI.

### D186. How much of the disk shards keeps is its user's to set (`shards configure disk`, built)

**Found.** The audit of defaults taken from Docker (docs/audit/2026-10-16_docker-framing.md):
the build cache's collection kept dockerd's default policy, 10% of the disk reserved, 80%
the most, 20% kept free (D114), and nothing changed it; a run's log kept Docker's `local`
driver's 5 segments of 20 MiB (D27), which only the daemon's environment changed, read once
as the daemon started.

**The user's calls (2026-10-18).** The build cache: dockerd's 10% to 80% kept, "but this
NEEDS to be user configurable". A log: 1 GiB, "but again, I expect this to be user
configurable".

**Decided.**
- `shards configure disk`, beside `configure guest` in shards' grammar (`disk configure`
  as the command it runs): `--build-cache-reserve`, `--build-cache-max` and
  `--build-cache-free`, each `N%` of the disk the image store is on (0 to 100) or a size
  (`50g`, `512m`: binary units, as `--memory` reads them); `--log-history SIZE`;
  `--events-history SIZE`, the home's events' journal's (D187); `--reset`.
  Alone, each setting and whether it is its default. Every flag is checked before any is
  kept, so a command that fails changes nothing; a reset sets aside what was there,
  whether it reads or not.
- **Files, as shards' own interfaces are.** The settings are the home's `disk`, a line a
  setting (`NAME VALUE`), written whole as a new file renamed over the last, so a reader
  finds the one or the other. They are read where they are used: as each run starts, by
  the daemon, and by each build's collection. A read where nothing is set costs what a
  stat does, and one with settings 7 to 12 µs at p50 on a loaded host (PM M252), so there
  is no cache, which a change could find stale; a change takes at the next run or build,
  whether the daemon runs or not.
- **A log's history** is the most of the disk a run's log takes, records' framing
  included (13 bytes a record), as written: equal segments, two at least, so that it holds
  at most its history and, once its oldest segment has gone, its history less two segments
  at least (one gone, and what a whole number of segments leaves). A history in one segment
  would keep nothing just after each rotation. The segments' size is derived (runs-11,
  below; it was 20 MiB, Docker's `local` driver's, copied). A run's own `--log-opt max-size` and
  `max-file` still bound its log (D161), and the daemon's environment
  (`SHARDS_LOG_MAX_SIZE`, `SHARDS_LOG_MAX_FILE`), where it is set, wins over the file.
- **The build cache's bounds.** A share is that much of the disk's bytes, exactly, 0% none,
  and a size is taken as it is; a reserve is at most the most. The defaults are the shares
  the user chose, and are now what they say: dockerd counts a share's whole GiB and one
  more in decimal gigabytes, which keeps 9.3%, 74.5% and 18.6% of a 2 TiB disk where it
  says 10%, 80% and 20%; shards took that from it (D114), and reserved 188.1 GiB of a
  2,014 GiB disk where its 10% is 201.4 GiB. Where the disk's
  size cannot be read, the sizes set apply, and a share is nothing to reckon (with none
  set, nothing goes since D212, where dockerd's 2 GB reserve held before). A changed cache
  setting is the next build's collection's, grown or not: `configure disk` removes the
  home's `buildcache-gc` (D212).
- **Concurrent commands (runs-09, 2026-11-14).** Two `configure disk` commands had shared
  one staging name, `.disk.new`, and read, changed and written the file unlocked: a command
  whose read was older wrote over another's update, and one's rename could publish the
  other's staging file as it truncated it, then write into the published file and fail.
  A command now rereads, changes and writes the file holding the home's `disk.lock` alone
  (flock(2), LockFileEx: the image store's `Locked`, let go before it closes, PM M244): a
  lock of its own, as the settings' file is replaced by each write. It writes through
  `platform::write_in`, a staging file of the writer's own (`O_EXCL`), synced, renamed
  over the file; on Windows that lands a version beside it (PM M345), and readers open
  the newest (`open_newest_in`). Readers take no lock: each finds a whole file, the old or
  the new. No literal: the lock and staging names are names. Unit tests (disk.rs):
  `concurrent_settings_updates_keep_each_others_fields` (an update waits for another
  command's held lock, then keeps both fields) and
  `settings_publication_leaves_another_writers_staging_file_alone`; with the lock and the
  owned staging removed, the base's transaction, both fail (the later snapshot drops
  `log-history`; another writer's `.disk.new` is published).
  [runs-fixes record](../research/measurements/runs-fixes/README.md#runs-09).
- **A segment's size, derived (runs-11 `LOG_SEGMENT`, 2026-11-14).** ROOT's objective: a
  reader resuming from a cursor reads at most one segment to find its place, while rotation
  keeps a run's log cap whole; the size from the cap and the file system's allocation unit.
  A cursor (`Pos`: its segment's number, its record's, its byte) names its segment, which a
  reader opens by name and enters by its index (8 bytes a record) and, packed, its seek
  table's one frame (D162); `--since` reads from the newest segment that begins no later
  than it, that one whole (D187): either way one segment is the most a resuming reader reads
  to find its place, so its cost grows with the size `S`. So does what a rotation takes from
  the cap: one segment. Each segment also costs its own making and going, whatever its size:
  a warm VM's `LOG_SEGMENT` ask, two files made, two removed, a pack, and a name every reader
  lists (`LogFile::segments`): `H / S` of them for a history `H`. Counted in the file
  system's own unit `U` (an allocation unit read or written each per-segment step, one per
  unit of a segment), `H / S + S / U` is least at `S = √(H · U)` (its derivative
  `−H / S² + 1 / U` is zero there), taken in whole units, since each file takes whole units
  of its disk, at least one unit and at most `H / 2`, the two segments a cap needs; then
  `H / S` segments, whole, so that they hold no more than `H` (`disk::log_retention`). `U`
  is the home's (`platform::allocation_unit`: statvfs(3)'s `f_frsize`, "file system fragment
  size"; Windows' sectors per cluster times bytes per sector, GetDiskFreeSpaceW), read as
  each run starts, beside the settings; a unit that cannot be read refuses the run, typed as
  the settings' own failures are. Its cold start, where no unit is known (a log's flags read
  without a log written, `--log-driver none`'s run head, the record of processes when the
  settings fail, the events' journal whose home's unit is unread): the cap's two halves, the
  bound the cap alone sets. 1 GiB on 4 KiB units: 512 segments of 2 MiB (was 52 of
  20,648,881 bytes); on 64 KiB clusters, 128 of 8 MiB; 64 KiB on 4 KiB, 4 of 16 KiB (was 2
  of 32 KiB). The events' journal (D187) keeps its history so too.
- **Every run's log held to its bound in bytes at each rotation (runs-11, ROOT's ruling).** A
  writer's retention lets go of one segment a rotation, `seq − files` (segments.rs): a log
  continued under segments of another size (one a daemon of 20 MiB segments began) or a
  smaller `--log-history` kept the segments it held past its new bound, until as many
  rotations had passed them, or for ever below `seq − files`. Now, as the daemon makes a
  run's next segment (files.rs), the run's logs are held to their bound by D240's rule
  (`managed/cap.rs` `hold`): a run whose members' logs are kept, all together within its one
  cap, as before; any other, its command's log alone within `size × files` bytes of output,
  its oldest let go first, never its newest, each loss in its `log.capped` (which `logs`
  says), as D240's are. One rule for every run, and no migration: a home's logs from before
  are held as any log is. Each hold weighs every segment from what the log records (its
  index's time, its log's length, a packed one's seek table), an open and a read each: O(files)
  a rotation, files at most `H / U` (`H / S` with `S ≥ U`); 512 for the default on 4 KiB
  units. In steady state, segments of the log's own size within its own count, it lets go
  of nothing. Red: `disk::tests::settings_read_back_and_come_to_their_amounts`, by mutation
  putting back 20 MiB segments; `daemon::tests::a_runs_log_is_held_to_its_bound_whatever_its_segments`
  by mutation holding runs without members' logs by their count alone (three segments of 64
  bytes kept past a 128-byte bound). The cost model's weighting (a per-segment step and a
  unit's read alike) is the model's; owed to ROOT: `logs -f` resume latency and rotation
  cost against segment size, sizes from one allocation unit to the cap's half, n, p50, p90,
  p99 and max per size, on APFS, ext4 or btrfs, and NTFS, by a harness under
  `docs/research/measurements/`, which confirms the balance or gives the weights their
  measured ratio; and
  `cargo test -p shards --profile test-release --test containers a_logs_history_is_what_its_user_set`
  (its segments now the derivation's) on HVF, KVM and WHP.
- **A file that does not read**, edited by hand: a run is refused, saying the file and its
  line; a build's collection collects nothing and says so at every build (`WARNING: the
  build cache was not collected: ...`), the build itself done; `--reset` mends it.
- With a context (D180), `configure disk` runs on the context's machine, whose disk it is.

**Tested.** On real microVMs: tests/containers.rs `a_logs_history_is_what_its_user_set`:
the default said; at 64k, a run's log is two segments on disk, 32 KiB (less a record's
head) to 64 KiB, the output's newest bytes; set to 128k as the daemon runs, the next run's is
128k's; a flag that does not read, before a reset, keeps nothing; a broken file refuses a
run, saying its file and line, and `--reset` mends it. tests/build.rs
`a_builds_cache_is_kept_as_its_user_set`: a broken file is said and collects nothing;
after `--reset --build-cache-max 1`, the next build's collection leaves no record, and the
step runs again. Unit tests: the settings read back as written; a history's segments; the
policy's bounds, set and unset. Mutation-checked, each caught: the daemon's logs ignoring
the settings; a short history in one segment; a reset reading what it resets; flags before
a reset unchecked; a run admitted past settings that do not read; a reserve past the most;
settings that do not read collected by the default policy; a set policy waiting out the
last collection; a failed collection unsaid; the collection ignoring the settings.
On every host the daemon runs on: both E2E tests are every host's, and pass on Windows'
real WHP microVMs too, where the disk's size is GetDiskFreeSpaceExW's
(`platform::disk_space`): CI 42329593544 at 51a709e9, windows-2025 (job 128272814009, no
test of it skipped) and windows-2022 (job 128272814036, whose skips are snapshot restores
alone, PM M345), as on macOS and Linux.

### D187. The home's events, kept for `--since` past their daemon (built)

**Found.** The audit of what was taken from Docker (docs/audit/2026-10-16_docker-framing.md):
a home's events for `events --since` were the last 256, dockerd's `eventsLimit` (moby
daemon/events/events.go), in the daemon's memory and gone with it. A shards daemon exits
once idle (`SHARDS_DAEMON_IDLE`, 900 s), and `--since` then said nothing of what had
happened before, where Docker's daemon, which runs on, says its last 256.

**Decided.**
- **A journal in the home**, `events/`: segments of an event a line, each as `--format
  json` prints it (Docker's events.Message, the API's from 1.52), named by number. The
  daemon appends each event as it logs it, under the lock it tells its listeners under, so
  that a listener has each event once: read from the journal up to where it was written
  as the listener came, then heard. A segment that ends in a line cut short, by a crash
  mid-write, is let be and the next begun past it; a line that does not read is passed by.
- **Its history is a log's** (D186): `configure disk --events-history SIZE`, at most that
  many bytes of the newest events, in equal segments, two at least, their size a log's
  (D186's runs-11 derivation, from the history and the home's allocation unit), the
  oldest removed as the newest begins; by default a log's 1 GiB, the user's call for a log
  (2026-10-18), the home's events being the home's log. The setting is read as each
  segment begins, so a change takes at the next.
- **`--since` reads from the newest segment that begins no later than it**, each segment
  read whole, one at a time, its events filtered as before.
- An event costs a write(2) of its line to a file opened for appending, unsynced: a host
  that crashes may lose its last, as its page cache does a log's.

**Tested.** Unit (daemon/events.rs): events kept for the next daemon, read back whole; the
history kept and the oldest gone (two segments, at most the history's bytes); a line cut
short passed by; a listener reads what came before and hears what comes after, none
twice. Mutation-checked, each caught: no trimming; a line cut short written on. E2E
(tests/containers.rs): `events_outlive_their_daemon`, a run's life read back by the next
daemon after `daemon stop` (failed with the journal taken out); `events_tell_a_microvms_life`.

### D212. The build cache goes only as its user's shares say, collected where a build grew it (built)

**Found.** The audit of what was taken from Docker (docs/audit/2026-10-16_docker-framing.md):
past the shares D186 made the user's, the build cache's collection kept dockerd's other
rules (moby docker-v29.3.1 daemon/internal/builder-next/worker/gc.go `DefaultGCPolicy`):
records easy to make again (`source.local`, `exec.cachemount`, `source.git.checkout`)
unused for two days went past a temporary share of the reserve (e·π·φ %, 512 MB at least),
any record unused for 60 days went past the shares, and where the disk's size could not
be read, 2 GB were reserved; and a build collected at most once a minute, as BuildKit's
controller throttles its GC (control/control.go `throttledGC`). Of the three types, a
shards store has cache mounts alone (D114): the first rule took every cache mount unused
for two days, its downloads and compilers' caches, whatever room the disk had.

**Decided.**
- **No record goes for its age.** What a collection protects is the disk, and the user's
  shares (D186) say how much of it the cache may hold, how much it may always keep and how
  much stays free: a record kept within them costs no disk the user asked back, and one
  removed costs its next build the step it saved, a cache mount's every download again.
  An age protects nothing the shares do not. The policy is the shares' two rules: the
  records no image shares, then all of them, the least recently and least often used
  first (cache/manager.go `sortDeleteRecords`, as `builder prune` ranks them).
- **A disk whose size cannot be read** bounds the cache by the sizes the user set alone,
  and where none is set, nothing goes: a share of a disk of unknown size is no size, and
  a rule with no bound would take every record. The store's own room check still keeps
  every write within the disk's free space (audit A10).
- **Collected where a build grew the cache**, not on a timer: the cache passes its bounds
  only as it grows, by a record put or a cache mount's content kept
  (`shards_image::store::cache_grew`, this process's), and a collection reads every
  record, 1.3 ms for 100 records and 86 ms for 10,000 at p50, 172 ms at p99, on a loaded
  host (PM M426): a build answered whole from the cache, the edit-and-rebuild loop's most
  common, would pay that for nothing, and a build that ran a step has run a microVM. A
  changed policy is the next build's to collect, grown or not (`configure disk` removes
  the home's `buildcache-gc`, as since D186). A free space that falls by other programs'
  writes is the next growing build's to answer.
- **One collection at a time** among the home's processes: the stamp `buildcache-gc`,
  locked while it collects, tried; where another holds it, that one collects. Two at once
  would each count the other's removals as their own still to make, and take past the
  bounds. The stamp's time says when the last ran.

**Tested.** Unit tests: the default policy is the shares' two rules, no age, and none at
all where neither the disk nor a size is known; a user's settings as D186's. On real
microVMs, tests/build.rs `run_caches_are_kept_across_builds`: a build that grew the cache
collected it; the same build again, answered whole from the cache, collected nothing;
builds that ran steps did. `a_builds_cache_is_kept_as_its_user_set` (D186): a changed
policy collected at the next build, which grew nothing. Measured: PM M426's harness,
`build::gc::tests::a_collections_cost_by_records`.

### D217. A kill waits as long as its microVM goes on ending, by what its host has shown; a freeze, to its end (built)

**Concurrent record writers** (runs-07). A daemon and each API host hold the
stable `ends.lock` exclusively across reread, maximum merge and publication. The
existing store `Locked` wrapper unlocks before closing (M244); locking the replaced
record's inode would not serialize the next reader. Publication uses the existing
platform `write_in`: a uniquely owned temporary file, synced and renamed whole.
A failed write retains this process's learned maximum, and its next observation
can persist that retained maximum even when it is faster. The focused race test
holds the stable lock while another writer learns a helper end, publishes its own
teardown snapshot and releases the lock: both maxima must survive. Existing cold
liveness behavior and the record's millisecond format are unchanged; no new wait,
cache, runtime number or platform adapter. See the [runs fix evidence](../research/measurements/runs-fixes/README.md).

**The record read as written** (runs-12). `heard` publishes through `platform::write_in`,
which on Windows replaces no file (PM M345): each write lands a version, `ends.~N`, and
removes the plain name. The record was read as the plain name (`fs::read_to_string`), so
on Windows every reader after the first write found none, and each host's slices were
lost to the next process. Every reader now opens the newest version (`ends::newest`,
`platform::open_newest_in`), on Unix the name itself. Unit test
`each_published_record_is_read_back_by_the_next_process` (three publications, each read
back by a new process's `Ends`), red on Windows with the plain read put back; Unix has
no versions, so only Windows can show it red. The E2E reader
(`a_kills_end_is_kept_as_this_hosts_in_its_home`) reads the newest version too.

**A stop keeps its ends once** (flake-harden, 2026-11-16). A stop's one loop (`end_all`,
which `stop`, `kill`, `rm -f` and `restart` end their targets from) kept each end it heard
in the home as it heard it: `heard`'s reread under the record's lock and `write_in`, which
syncs the file and then its directory, two F_FULLFSYNCs on macOS (PM M46: 8.5 ms at p50 on
a quiet host; M313: 100 to 614 ms each on a loaded one). Each keep held up every end after
it, and each end was timed only once the ends before it were taken, the keeps with them, so
that on a loaded host an end of a burst was the slowest yet, and kept, in turn.
`daemon::tests::stop_ends_every_container_at_once` (sixty, a 10 s grace) took 25.9 s in a
loaded full run at 6f5755ae1 (lane shards-green), where three other runs passed: the cause
read from the code, with no trace kept, and its loaded reproduction owed (R09). Now the loop
learns each end in memory as it hears it (`Ends::learn`, the slices from then on), timed as
its poll woke, and keeps the record once, after the last (`Ends::keep`): no end waits on a
flush, nor counts one in its time. `keep` holds the memory's lock
only to merge, not over the record's lock and flush, which every slice asked meanwhile (a
stop's escalation, the followers' loop's helper slice) waited on. `heard`, the two together,
stays for those that keep one end in a wait of their own (`netproc::reap`). Guard:
`a_stop_answers_each_end_while_its_homes_record_is_held`, a kill of two with the record's
lock held, both answered (red with a keep per end); the stop test's failure says when its
SIGKILLs came, so the next red tells a late escalation from late ends. Unchanged and
unreproduced: the followers' loop keeps a network process's end as it hears it
(`follow.rs` `process_ended`), on the loop that takes every run's messages.

**Found.** The audit of what was taken from Docker (docs/audit/2026-10-16_docker-framing.md):
a microVM whose command outlived its SIGKILL had its VM killed 10 s later and its end given
up 2 s after that (moby daemon/kill.go), a signal that could not be sent waited out 2 s
(daemon/stop.go), a daemon's shutdown killed a VM whose command outlived its stop timeout
by 5 s (daemon.go `ShutdownTimeout`), and a joiner's freeze (D119) gave up after 10 s
(runc libcontainer cgroups/fs2/freezer.go `waitFrozen`). Each is a clock on work that ends
as it ends: a SIGKILLed command ends as its guest's kernel frees what it held, which grows
with it, 0.3 s for 16 GiB at p50 and 5.6 s beside a host's every CPU busy (PM M480), so
that a microVM holding a few tens of GiB on a busy host outlives 10 s with nothing wrong;
and a VM ended first loses what its guest had yet to write back (D119's joiner layers, a
writable layer's metadata). A figure measured on shards' machines is as arbitrary on a
user's host as Docker's.

**Decided.**
- **A teardown is followed, not timed** (daemon/ends.rs), on D215's judge (the person's
  rule for waits, 2026-11-13): once SIGKILL is sent, by `stop`, `kill`, `rm -f`, `restart`
  or the daemon's own stop, its VM process is looked at after a slice and each slice after,
  and waited on while it goes on with its end: it ran any CPU at all, held less than it did
  (its host freeing it), or its host held it from running (D215's readers,
  `shards_api::Watch`: a thread runnable or waiting on memory, its threads' run-queue wait
  or its own cgroup's pressure grown),
  which is no stall of its own. Its VM is killed only once it did none of these for a whole
  slice, or is stopped or frozen. It was PM M357's idle CPU (`Progress`, 63 ms in 10 s),
  which ended a teardown that ran slower than an idle microVM (red at 2b89e8504:
  `an_end_goes_on_at_any_rate_and_not_asleep_or_stopped`, a fiftieth of a CPU). A killed VM
  process is followed the same way, its host freeing it, before its end is given up on. A
  joiner's VM is its provider's, which runs the provider's command too: a joiner is held to
  one slice, then sent SIGKILL again, as before.
- **A network or share process is followed the same way** (2026-11-13, PM M546; the
  person's ruling: a wait follows the party's liveness and progress, then the slowest
  answer seen). Once its VM has gone and its spawner holds nothing of it, it goes as its
  VM's links close, which wakes its reaper (`netproc::reap`; for a daemon's run, the
  followers' loop). It is looked at once a slice has passed, waited on for another while it
  runs or frees what it holds, and ended only once it has done neither for a slice. Its own
  end is kept as the host's; one its reaper made is not. It was `netproc::GRACE`, a second,
  picked, and the daemon's port check (`in_use`) waited twice that for an ended run's
  network process; it now waits one slice. The cost: a network process stuck on nothing of
  its own is ended 10 s or more after its VM, where it was 1 s; one that exits as its links
  close, as each does, ends the wait at once. The waits that took that second as their
  basis no longer keep it: init's relay drain (hostbind.rs `DRAIN`) follows its relays' peers
  (D124, PM M556), and the VM process's waits follow their parties (below).
- **The VM process's waits follow their parties' liveness, and the daemon judges** (ROOT's
  (A), 2026-11-13; each was a second, picked): confined, it sees nothing of its network
  process's or its daemon's progress, so its run's end waits for the guest's frames to be in
  the ring (`TxFlush::flush(None)`, whose worker answers every flush as it ends), for its
  ports' closing (`UNPUBLISH`) while its network process lives, and for a port of the host's
  let go (`HOST_RELEASE`) while its daemon's connection lives. It tells the daemon it waits on
  its network process (`UNPUBLISHING`), which follows that process from then on its helper
  slice, as one whose VM has gone (`follow_unpublish`), ends it where it goes on with nothing
  for a slice, which ends the VM's wait, and follows it no more once it answered
  (`PORTS_FREE`). Red at 6c3cb7137, each with the second: a flush answered 1.5 s on, an
  unpublish and a host port's release answered 1.5 s on, each given up on; and a network
  process its VM waited on, doing nothing, never ended.
- **The daemon's asks of a network process are followed too** (ROOT, 2026-11-13; it was
  `PUBLISH_PATIENCE`, the same second, picked): a published port, a peer, a network's names
  (`networks::ask_net`, `Asks`), and a run's on the host's network (`HostNet`), each wait for
  room and for its answer judged by D215's judge (`netproc::until_ready`) on the daemon's
  record of its network processes' answers (`netproc::NET_ANSWERS`, one for the process, W*
  its slowest answer), its network process followed by its pid (`NetLink`, carried with its
  control from its start): before the record's first answer, the process's liveness alone,
  its socket's end; past W*, looked at each W*, and refused where a whole W* shows it ran
  no CPU and its host was not the reason. Each answer teaches the record, its wall and the
  process's CPU. A wait for room is one for poll(2)'s POLLOUT (WSAPoll's POLLWRNORM), so no
  write is cut part-way. Red at 07adbbc8b (`ask_red_tests`, adas-mac-studio.local): an answer
  1.5 s on was refused at 1.002 s; green: `netproc::ask_tests`, a busy stand-in's answers 1.5
  s on taken, cold and past W*, and a sleeping one's ask refused past a taught W*.
- **The slice is the host's own, W*.** Each end heard is kept in the home (`ends`:
  `teardown MS`, `exit MS` and `helper MS`, the slowest of each this home's processes have
  heard: its daemon and its runs' hosts keep one record, each end put with what it holds
  then, written whole and renamed over), and a slice is the slowest of its kind there, so
  that a host whose guests stall on its disk for 9 s before they end (PM M419) gives its
  teardowns that long. A home with none of a kind yet has no slice (`Ends::slice` is
  `None`): its end is followed by its process's liveness alone, to the end that teaches
  it, as the person's rule has a cold wait. `LEAST_SLICE` (`IDLE_VM_CPU`'s 10 s, the floor
  a home with no record took alone) is gone: D215's readers read CPU to the nanosecond, so
  no tick of a clock reads as a run, and a pause of the host's is its hold, not a stall
  (red at 2b89e8504: `a_hosts_ends_are_learned_and_kept_in_its_home`, 10 s of shards' own
  for a home with no record). Its gap: the first end of a kind a home ever hears, a
  teardown its guest cannot finish among them, is waited for as long as its process lives;
  the daemon's own stop and `rm -f` on such a home wait so too. The daemon's tests teach a
  helper's slice where their stand-ins never end (`heard`), as a home that has heard one.
- **A signal that cannot be sent kills its VM at once:** the run's connection to its VM
  is gone, the one its guest says its end on, so nothing it could wait for can come.
- **A joiner's freeze has no deadline** (init's `freeze`): once `cgroup.freeze` is
  written no process of the cgroup runs another instruction of its own, and `frozen 1`
  comes as each leaves the kernel work it was in (cgroup-v2.rst), a volume's write as its
  host's share server answers. A freeze given up on left the cgroup freezing while its
  pause said it had failed. One whose work cannot end is ended by the joiner's own kill.
  Measured, every freeze came within 0.23 s (PM M482).
- **Kept: the stop timeout of 10 s** where a run sets none. It is the input's meaning, not
  a wait on work: a Compose file's `stop_grace_period` left out is "10 seconds for the
  container to exit before sending SIGKILL" (the Compose file reference), and a run's
  `--stop-timeout` left out is read the same, the time its author gave its command to end
  on its own.

**Tested.** Unit tests (daemon/ends.rs): a home with no record gives no end a slice (it
gave each the least); each slower end heard is kept, in the home too, and read back by the
next daemon; a record it cannot read is none; a home's processes keep one record, neither's
slower end lost to the other's write, and a record that cannot be kept is said; an end is
followed while its VM process runs, a joiner's never; and one goes on at a fiftieth of a CPU,
not asleep or stopped (`an_end_goes_on_at_any_rate_and_not_asleep_or_stopped`). netproc.rs
`a_helper_is_waited_on_while_it_goes_on_with_its_end`: a busy helper is waited on past five
slices and its end kept, a sleeping one ended at its first look and nothing kept; the
daemon's `a_network_process_is_ended_once_it_goes_on_no_more_and_the_ports_freed`. On real microVMs, tests/containers.rs `a_kills_end_is_kept_as_this_hosts_in_its_home`:
a kill's end kept in the home, its VM not killed under it; the stop, kill, pause and
daemon-stop tests as before. Measured: PM M480 to M482, which validate the method (every
teardown and freeze measured ends while it is followed) and are no figure of it. On D215's
judge, at main 68baef2d0 (adas-mac-studio.local, macOS 26.2 arm64, kiln r276): shards-api's
judge, progress and client tests (53 passed, 3 ignored), the shards bin's ends, reap, network
process, stop, health, metrics and commands tests (41 passed); clippy -D warnings on macOS,
x86_64 Linux (shards-api) and x86_64 Windows (cargo-xwin, shards-api and shards). Owed: the
real-VM kill and stop tests on HVF, KVM and WHP (ROOT's).

### D188. A host short of memory gets back what its microVMs hold cold of their files (built)

**Amended: a told line says what its host has available** (2026-11-16, ROOT's decision; lane
charge-seam).
- *Why.* D252's charges are held to the host's available memory (daemon/managed.rs
  `Charge::grow`), which no unprivileged process can set. So no real-VM test could give a run
  room for its link but not for its first lanes (lane phase6-v). ROOT's decision: tell it
  through this channel (R12), with one reader for the daemon and the run host, and no channel
  of its own.
- *The words.* Each told line, its newline apart, is one of two:
  - empty: the host is short of memory, as before;
  - `available BYTES`, BYTES in decimal digits alone: the host has BYTES of memory available,
    in place of its kernel's count (`shards_ipc::host_available`: Linux's `MemAvailable`,
    macOS's `kern.memorystatus_level`, Windows' `ullAvailPhys`). Every charge is held to it
    from then on, until a line says another.

  Any other line is refused `InvalidData`: a sign, a CR, a space, a number past a u64, or a
  line past the longest word. The longest word is 30 bytes (`available ` and the 20 digits of
  `u64::MAX`); a longer line is refused as it reaches that length rather than held. A line its
  pipe's end cuts off is `UnexpectedEof`. Before, any line was a short word. Every line
  written so far was empty (`common::Told::say`, build.rs's and build_windows.rs's), so no
  writer changes.
- *One reader* (pressure.rs).
  - `read_word` reads a line a byte at a time, as before, so that it never takes the next
    line's bytes.
  - `heard` keeps an `available` word's bytes as the process's own (`TOLD_AVAILABLE`).
  - `available()` answers the told bytes where a line has told some, else the kernel's count.
  - `Charge::grow` measures every charge against `available()`, the daemon's runs' and a run
    host's alike.
- *Where it is read.*
  - The daemon: its watcher, through `Pressure::wait`, which now returns the word
    (`Word::Short` for every word of its kernel's). It hears an `available` word as it hears a
    short one, while a microVM runs, since it listens only then (above). It says each in its
    log: `told the host has N bytes of memory available: every run's charge is held to that`.
    A test keeps a microVM running and waits for that line before it starts a run.
  - A run host (`shards api-run`, D231, which shards-api's boot starts): the first line of
    what `SHARDS_PRESSURE` names in its environment (`ImageSpec::env`), a FIFO, a named pipe
    or a file. It is read once its request is read and before its run is made
    (`pressure::first`, in `host`), so that every charge its run makes as it starts is held to
    it. A pipe no line has reached yet is waited on. The run host says the word in its
    diagnostics; one it cannot read refuses its run `Cause::Boot`. Later lines are not read: a
    run host is told once, as its run is made.
  - A build (`SHARDS_BUILD_PRESSURE`): its watcher reads the word and asks its builders
    nothing at it, as no builder is charged to a budget.
- *Literals* (R03): the word's name, `available`; its longest line, 30 bytes, derived from the
  name and `u64::MAX` (`u64::MAX.ilog10() + 1` digits). No number is chosen.
- *Tested* (unit, written, not run: the person's rule of 2026-11-16).
  - `pressure::words::a_told_line_is_short_or_what_its_host_has_available`: both words, one
    after another from one pipe; each refused line; a line cut off. It reads only and tells
    nothing, since the told bytes are the process's, which other unit tests' charges read.
  - `pressure::tests::a_fifo_tells_its_pressure_a_line_at_a_time`: its words are `Word::Short`.
  - Real VM: D252's two tests (its amendment of this date).
- *Owed* (ROOT).
  - `cargo test --profile test-release -p shards --bin shards -- pressure::`
  - The told pipe's real-VM tests, whose words are unchanged, on HVF, KVM and WHP:
    `--test containers -- --exact what_a_microvm_holds_cold_is_given_back_at_its_hosts_word`,
    `--test engine_ring -- --exact a_give_back_lets_an_idle_slot_go`,
    `--test build -- --exact a_builder_gives_back_what_it_holds_cold_at_its_builds_word`
    (Unix), and `--test build_windows` (WHP).

**R03 review memory-06..08, 10 (2026-11-14, implemented; PM M581):** no fixed time
or level is left in how the host hears its pressure and paces what follows it:
- *What a pressure is* (memory-07): a PSI trigger's window's stall is pressure once
  it is as long as the act it brings took last, the daemon's (or a build's) latest
  give-back from its ask to its answer (`platform::pressure::stall_of`): rent or buy,
  act once waiting has lost what acting costs, at most twice the best choice in
  hindsight (Karlin, Manasse, Rudolph and Sleator, "Competitive snoopy caching",
  Algorithmica 3, 1988). Cold start: no act yet, the kernel's least threshold, 1 µs
  (`psi_trigger_create`: more than none, at most the window); the first stall is
  heard and its act teaches the next. Its triggers are armed again as it changes;
  one that cannot be stays as it was. Replaced lmkd's 140 ms in 2 s (an upstream
  default, which R03 refuses).
- *The window* (memory-06): 2 s on Linux is the kernel's bound, the least an
  unprivileged writer may arm (`psi_trigger_create`: a multiple of 2 s, checked in
  the averaging work with no real-time thread of its own; Linux 6.4, d82caa273565;
  read in 7.2-rc4's kernel/sched/psi.c), shards running as its user; it is kept in
  the Linux adapter alone (`WINDOW_US`). `shards_abi::PRESSURE_WINDOW_US` and
  `platform::PRESSURE_WINDOW` are gone: nothing else paces itself by it.
- *A kernel that arms no trigger* (memory-08): the same trigger kept by the daemon,
  `some total` (the kernel's stall so far, brought up to date as it is read,
  `psi_show`) read at once as the watch starts and then each window, a window's
  growth past the learned stall a word. It was avg10 read each 10 s, at 7%. A file
  that cannot be read ends the watch with its error, never zero pressure.
- *macOS and Windows* (memory-06): a raised pressure is said again on D215's pace
  (`shards_abi::pace`, `sqrt(2 c w)`), `c` the last act's cost and `w` how long it
  has been raised; before any act, the watcher's own look's cost. It was 2 s.
- *What follows a word* (memory-06): a microVM held short of its budget is told its
  room again `sqrt(2 c w)` after its last word, `c` what telling it took, `w` how
  long it had been short (`budget::Held::told_again`); a group's pass, `c` the last
  pass's time and `w` how long its groups had gone unchanged (members, budget read,
  short or not: `groups::Paced`); a build's look for late answers and its budget's
  room, `c` its last look and `w` how long it had one out or was held
  (`give::watch_words`). A build's patience for its builders' answers is the slowest
  they have given (W*, `give::Unsaid::patience`), none waited for and none judged
  before the first; it was a pressure window. The log's pacing (`pressure::Saying`)
  follows its source's repeat (`Pressure::repeat`), a told pipe's each line a
  pressure of its own.
- *A guest's recent growth* (memory-06, PM M466): memory is cold only if it stayed
  plugged through a whole period of the run's peak, from one give-back to the next,
  unused; a give-back that finds more plugged than as its period began keeps all
  (init `came_within`, `begin_period`). It was a mark within 2 s.
- *A share's budget room* (memory-10): looked at on D215's pace (below).
- Owed to ROOT (R09/R14, real hosts): the budget E2E
  `cargo test -p shards --test budget` on a Linux host with cgroup v2 delegation;
  `cargo test -p shards moves_live --test moved`; `update_under_pressure_stress`
  (tests/containers.rs, ignored) for PM M466's rounds under the period rule; the
  PSI threshold's word count and give-backs on a loaded Linux host against lmkd's
  140 ms; macOS's and Windows' repeat counts under a raised pressure
  (`SHARDS_PRESSURE` cannot raise the system's: Windows'
  `each_low_memory_signal_is_a_word_and_one_that_lasts_is_said_again` and a
  memory-pressure tool's run on a Mac). The DAX crossover (memory-09) stays owed below.

**Review memory-04 (2026-11-13):** the builder's giver retains the latest ROOM
word while a prior GIVE_BACK or ROOM reply is outstanding, including the explicit
unbudgeted word. It transmits that word as the reply is consumed and coalesces a
value already in flight, whose acknowledgment remains consumable. Desired room
and request/reply state have one owner; budget removal cannot disappear behind
a late answer. Red and light-check evidence: `docs/research/measurements/memory-fixes-v1/README.md`.

**Review memory-15 (2026-11-14):** a builder booted cold, with all it may have and nothing
to plug (D133), answers `GIVE_BACK` and `ROOM` as one with memory to plug: its build has
its cgroup from its start (`plug::hold_build`), which it had only where it plugged, so it
gave nothing back; it gives back its files' cold pages, and unplugs nothing, having none
plugged (D133's "Every builder's build has its cgroup").


**Found.** The user's plan, item 4: memory that tracks the working set, reclaimed at the
host's pressure, not on a timer. A run's guest keeps what its workload reads in its page
cache, guest memory the host cannot drop, only swap: a 1 GiB file read from a volume left
944 MiB of page cache in the guest and 1,003 MiB more of the VM process's memory on the
host (PM M267), where a container's page cache is its host's to drop. Free page reporting
(D151) gives back what a guest frees, and nothing asked a guest to free.

**Decided.**
- **The daemon watches the host's memory pressure** (`platform::MemoryPressure`). On
  Linux, PSI triggers (Documentation/accounting/psi.rst): some task stalled on memory as
  long as its last give-back took, over the shortest window an unprivileged process may
  watch (Linux 6.4, d82caa273565; memory-07 above, which replaced lmkd's 140 ms); on
  the host's memory, on the daemon's own cgroup, where its microVMs are made, and on each
  scope it makes microVMs in under a user's slice (D183), which may hold them to a budget:
  a cgroup's stall counts in the host's figure against every CPU busy elsewhere, so a
  budget is reached before the host says so. A kernel that arms none of its user's has
  the same trigger kept from its `some total`, read each window (memory-08). On macOS,
  libdispatch's memory pressure source, said again on D215's pace while the pressure
  stays raised (memory-06). On Windows, the system's low memory notification
  (CreateMemoryResourceNotification, `LowMemoryResourceNotification`), signalled while
  its available memory is low (by default 32 MB of each 4 GB, 64 MB at most: its
  documentation), said again on the same pace while it stays so. On macOS and
  Windows a group shards keeps holds microVMs to a budget (D183's slice 3), whose files
  the daemon reads on its passes' pace (memory-06). Where `SHARDS_PRESSURE` names a FIFO (on Windows,
  a named pipe), each line written to it is the host's word in place of its kernel's, as
  `SHARDS_BUILD_PRESSURE` tells a build: a test's, as no unprivileged process may raise
  macOS's or Windows' pressure. A line may say what the host has available instead (the
  amendment of 2026-11-16, above).
- **Each time, every running microVM gives back what it holds cold of its files.** Its
  init (builtin `RECLAIM`) reclaims as much of its run's file pages as its memory.stat
  counts inactive, of its file pages alone (`memory.reclaim` with `swappiness=0`, Linux
  6.11, 68cd9050d871; a kernel without the key takes the amount alone), then reports what
  that freed at once (`page_reporting.flush`, D151's patch 0005), so that the host has it
  back before init answers. Each microVM through one of its runs, its own or else a
  joiner's (D119), each on a thread of its own, and one still giving back since a pass
  before asked nothing more until it has answered or been ended: passes that asked one
  microVM after another, each waiting up to 10 s for an answer and then for its end,
  waited on a guest whose own memory its host had taken for minutes, and gave back 3 times
  in 600 s (PM M308). Each is waited for while its microVM's process runs, and ended, said
  to have had no answer, only once that process stalls (below): a microVM over its
  budget's `memory.high` is slowed by its host for as long as it is over it, and the
  answers of one asked to give back what would bring it under, and to hear its room after,
  came past a 10 s deadline as its host let it run, which ended them, its budget's word
  never said or saying nothing given back (PM M467). A group's give-backs and rooms,
  macOS's and Windows' among them, are waited for the same way.
- **What a microVM's own answers are waited for by is learned, not set**
  (`health::Wait::WhileRuns`; R03, the person's rule of 2026-11-13). It was PM M357's idle
  microVM, 63 ms of CPU in 10 s (`shards_vmm::platform::IDLE_VM_CPU`), judged each 10 s
  (`TAKE_TIMEOUT`): two figures of our machines, which ended any microVM that ran slower
  than an idle one over a slice, its answer however near (red at e0cc059c7, below). It is
  now D215's judge, shared, not copied (R12):
  - *Records*: each kind of answer apart, in the daemon's memory (`health::Answers`): a
    give-back (`RECLAIM`, at its host's pressure, a budget's or a group's), a room told
    (`ROOM`), metrics read (`METRICS`), and each of init's builtins its quiet work asks
    (`exec_answered`, a record per builtin: `STAT`, `TOP`, `STATS`, a member's ports, a
    network's switch, a layer's size, an update), which were each `TAKE_TIMEOUT`'s 10 s
    (ROOT's (3), 2026-11-13). A network's switch keeps one record for each verb asked of it
    (D215, 2026-11-17: a `make`'s answers had judged a `connect`). Each keeps W*, the slowest answer seen from a
    wait's start to its exec's end, and R*, the least CPU rate a microVM still answered at
    (`shards_api::Record`). Only an exec's own end teaches: one the daemon ended teaches
    nothing. Each wait takes its clock before its exec is asked (amended below), so every answer of
    the microVM's came within it and teaches.
  - *Amended (ci-fixes, 2026-11-16, kiln goal fb3528f9): the wait begins before its ask.*
    - *Before.* `exec_followed` began its wait (`await_exit`) after `send_exec` and after
      spawning its output's reader. An answer already there as the wait began taught nothing,
      read as D185's `Asked::waited` is: it was waited for not at all (D222's wait of
      nothing), and its W* of next to nothing would have had its kind's next asks looked at
      each microsecond. A microVM that answers faster than a thread is spawned so taught
      nothing, ever. On CI's Windows arm64 (CI 43968984258, job 133659472771, fe83503c2) the
      daemon test `a_microvm_that_does_not_give_back_keeps_no_other_waiting` never ended: its
      stand-in answers as it reads the ask, and its give-back was never learned in ~24k passes
      ("gave back 24165 MiB … in 24165 passes"), until the step's limit.
    - *Decided.* The wait begins before its exec is asked, in `exec_followed` and `exec_on`
      alike (health.rs `Begun::now`, then `send_exec`, then `await_exit`): its judge's follow
      of the microVM's process begun, or its `Cut::Unread`, which ends the exec once asked.
      No answer can come before it, so the check of one there as the wait begins is gone,
      and W* runs from the wait's start, before the ask, as D215 counts a wait. A W* of mere
      microseconds no longer has looks made each microsecond: a judge looks each W* or each
      least window its counters resolve, whichever is longer (shards-api `Judge::window`, b26,
      `a_wait_is_never_refused_within_what_its_reading_resolves`).
      Not changed: the waits on what the daemon does not ask (a VM's READY, a client's
      requests) keep D222's wait of nothing, as their party may speak before they begin. A
      visit's hold, which answers the daemon's RUN, was among them until D222's amendment of
      2026-11-17: one there before its wait's first look now teaches its time from its RUN,
      its slowest alone, with no read of its VM process before RUN.
    - No literal; no cache touched; the wait's start moved before its ask.
    - *Tests* (written, not run: the person's rule of 2026-11-16). health.rs
      `an_answer_there_before_its_waiter_reads_teaches_from_its_ask` (replaces
      `an_exit_said_before_its_wait_teaches_nothing`: the answer said 1 ms past the wait's
      start, before its waiter reads, teaches a W* no shorter);
      `a_cold_wait_follows_its_microvm_while_it_lives` (its W* holds the answer's whole 0.8 s);
      the daemon's `a_microvm_that_does_not_give_back_keeps_no_other_waiting` (one answered
      give-back teaches, where it looped until one did). Owed (ROOT): the daemon's bin tests on
      Linux and macOS, and that test on Windows arm64 (CI's windows-11-arm), red at fe83503c2.
  - *Amended (own-35-ci-green, 2026-11-17, kiln goal fb3528f9; ROOT's ruling): the clock
    alone before the ask.*
    - *Before.* `Begun::now` followed the microVM's process before `send_exec`
      (shards-api `Follow::begin`), and every exec's ask waited for that read. On Windows it
      is a ToolHelp snapshot of every process (progress.rs `grow`) and the system's records
      of every process and thread (`records`), each read of which took 13.1 to 13.8 ms on
      jupiter (PM M606); on Linux and macOS, the process's own files and records.
    - *Decided.* `Begun::now` takes the time alone, a clock read, before `exec_followed` and
      `exec_on` ask (health.rs): no read of the microVM's process before the ask, on any OS.
      `await_exit` follows the process from its first look that finds nothing to read, once
      asked, as it did before 2026-11-16, and ends the exec there where it cannot be read
      (`Cut::Unread`). Each answer teaches its kind its time from the ask (`teach_answer`,
      `Record::teach_unrated`), so W* runs from the ask as the amendment above decided; where
      a look followed the process before the answer, the answer also teaches the work read
      from then, with its rate (D215: only work read through an answer teaches R* and C*). An
      answer there at the first look teaches its slowest alone, as a visit's hold does (D222,
      amended 2026-11-17). The read's cost is gone from before the ask; a process read after
      it runs while the microVM runs its exec, and an answer that comes during the read is
      taken once the read ends.
    - No literal; no cache touched.
    - *Tests* (written, not built or run: the lane's no-test rule). health.rs
      `an_answer_there_before_its_waiter_reads_teaches_from_its_ask` now also asks that such
      an answer teach no rate (its process read before its waiter first looked: red at
      0c54ac6239, where this busy test process's CPU was read from before the ask);
      `a_cold_wait_follows_its_microvm_while_it_lives` keeps its W* of the answer's whole
      0.8 s from the ask; the daemon's `a_microvm_that_does_not_give_back_keeps_no_other_waiting`
      learns from one pass. Owed (ROOT): those tests on Linux, macOS and Windows.
  - *Amended again the same day (own-35-ci-green, kiln goal fb3528f9; ROOT's ruling): the read
    waits for W\*, by D215's rule.*
    - *Before.* `await_exit` read the microVM's process at its first look that found nothing
      to read, right after the ask, which almost no answer comes before; and the answer read
      it again (`Follow::answered`, whose look on Windows takes another ToolHelp snapshot).
    - *Decided.* An exec's wait keeps the rule D215 gave its judged waits the same day ("the
      read waits for W*"; health.rs `read_at`, the one rule of every judged wait: an exec's,
      a visit's hold, a judged exchange's). It waits on its answer alone until it has lasted
      W*, its kind's slowest answer timed from the ask, and reads the process only past W*,
      following it from then, or ending the exec there where it cannot be read
      (`Cut::Unread`); a kind with no answer yet waits on its answer, or its connection's end,
      alone, as before. Its answer reads the process only where that read began
      (`teach_answer`). The trade-off is D215's: before W* its judge could refuse nothing, so
      a microVM that runs nothing is refused, and a group told (`Wait::GroupWord`), about one
      W* later, its first judged window beginning at W* instead of at the ask; answers within
      W* teach W* alone, and R* and C* come from the waits that needed a read.
    - No literal; no cache touched.
    - *Tests* (written, not built or run: the lane's no-test rule). health.rs
      `an_exec_answered_within_w_star_reads_no_process`: red at 2fe4947fba, where its first
      look read this busy test process and its answer taught that CPU as a rate; green here,
      W* alone. Owed (ROOT): the health tests and the daemon's exec tests
      (`metrics_whose_microvm_runs_nothing_are_ended`, now refused one W* later) on Linux,
      macOS and Windows.
  - *Cold start*: before its kind's first answer, a wait follows its microVM's liveness
    alone, to its exec's end or its microVM's.
  - *The judge*: past W* from its start, the wait looks at the microVM's process once each
    W*. A look that finds it ran no CPU at all since the look before ends the exec (SIGKILL,
    its end waited for) and says so, typed (`health::Cut::Stalled`: how far into the wait,
    the time looked over, R* and W*), where the client of a metrics read and the daemon's
    log are told it. R* is diagnosis, never a bound. A process that cannot be read while it
    lives ends its exec at once (`Cut::Unread`), never taken for one that ran nothing; one
    gone is its exec's end.
  - *Readers*: D215's (`shards_api::Followed::of_pid`): Linux's CPU clock, macOS's
    proc_pid_rusage, Windows' QueryProcessCycleTime over the process and what descends from
    it, each read with the start that tells it from a process given its pid later. The
    judge's schedule and verdict moved into `crates/api/src/judge.rs` (`Record`, `Judge`,
    `Found`), apart from the CPU it reads, for waits that follow something else.
  - *Literals*: none. W*, R* and every window are this daemon's own; their durations
    saturate at u64's nanoseconds (D215); a look due now is made, never a read with a zero
    timeout.
  - *A cold kind follows liveness* (ROOT's ruling, 2026-11-13). Before its kind's first
    answer, a wait on a microVM whose init never answers holds its thread, and a metrics
    read its client, until that microVM ends: audit-fix-host-v1's finding 4, now only
    before the kind's first answer (`metrics_whose_microvm_runs_nothing_are_ended` teaches
    its record first). Its progress is shown typed meanwhile: a client's wait by the
    listener's word of what its microVM runs (D209), and an end by its `Cut`.
  - *A microVM its host holds is live* (ROOT's ruling, 2026-11-13; D215's judge, `Found::Held`).
    Linux puts a task over its cgroup's `memory.high` to sleep up to
    `MEMCG_MAX_HIGH_DELAY_JIFFIES` (2 s) at each return to user space (mm/memcontrol.c,
    `mem_cgroup_handle_over_high`), and a loaded host's scheduler can keep a runnable
    process off its CPUs for longer than a short W*: a microVM all of whose threads so wait
    for a whole W* ran nothing of its own fault. A look that finds no CPU refuses now only
    where its host was not the reason: none of its threads runnable or waiting on its host's
    memory, nor (Linux) its cgroup's CPU or memory pressure grown; and a microVM stopped or
    frozen is refused whatever else shows. The evidence is D215's readers'. Not measured
    here: the budget E2E under a `memory.high` (tests/budget.rs, tests/containers.rs) holds it.
  - Tested (light), health.rs: `a_cold_wait_follows_its_microvm_while_it_lives`,
    `a_microvm_that_runs_at_any_rate_is_waited_for` (a fiftieth of a CPU, below the idle
    rate), `an_exec_is_ended_once_its_microvm_runs_nothing_for_a_whole_w_star`,
    `an_unread_microvm_process_ends_its_exec_typed` (macOS) and
    `a_timed_wait_ends_its_exec_and_an_untimed_one_waits`; reclaim.rs's
    `a_give_back_says_what_it_gave_or_why_it_gave_nothing`; daemon.rs's
    `metrics_whose_microvm_runs_nothing_are_ended`; shards-api's judge.rs and progress.rs

    Green on the merged tree (origin/main 5bc134861 with 6fc62c231 and 005dce1da; same host,
    rustc 1.98.1): health.rs 11 of 11, reclaim.rs 1, daemon.rs's `metrics_` 4, budget.rs 7,

    Not run: these tests on Linux or Windows, real microVMs (the budget E2E above among

- **A budget falling short waits for its host's give-back** (PM M467): where a give-back
  of the host's pressure is under way in the microVM, the budget's own asks once it has
  ended, its room read again; and its word says what its host's pressure had it give back
  and ask to unplug since the word before, which the host's own word says only as its
  pressure begins and as it doubles (below): a budget set just after the host had taken
  what it held cold found nothing to give back, and its word said nothing given back.
- **Ring pins come out of the room** (kiln plan 01a1cd8e862e7169a074db3d5fa33f3d:
  "Everything a VM holds, ring pins included, comes out of that room"). An engine ring's
  slots are guest RAM its guest's kernel pins for the host to reach (D230). Init's relay
  makes a slot only where the budget's hold leaves room past what the run holds and its
  working room, counts its slots in the run's cgroup, and lets idle ones go as a told room
  shrinks or a give-back asks; a live stream keeps its ring, grown no further (D230's
  "Supply is the run's room";
  [ring-pins-v1](../research/measurements/ring-pins-v1/README.md) r13 and r16, on KVM
  x86_64 and arm64 and HVF). Budgets per fleet are Hex's to set (plan step 14, Hex's
  `docs/design/learned-charge.md` C7). A run booted for an orchestrator is told no room
  yet: shards-api carries `STATS` and no `ROOM` (D231), so Hex refuses a guest's room typed
  (`Awaits(GuestRoom)`). Owed to step 14, on shards-api's wire.
- **Held within what its budget leaves it** (PM M309). Where the cgroup a microVM's VM
  process is in, or one above it, holds it to a budget (`memory.high` or `memory.max`, a
  slice's `MemoryHigh` or `MemoryMax`, D183), the host can take back only page cache from
  it with no swap, and a guest's page cache is guest RAM, the host's anonymous memory: a
  guest that read past its budget filled it, and the host took back the one thing it
  could, the guest's own RAM as a template's file pages, which the guest read back as it
  ran, 400 to 600 s for a gigabyte its run read in 3 to 5 s with no budget, on CI's AMD
  and Intel runners alike. So each microVM's guest is told the room its budget leaves it,
  the least any cgroup over it may still take before its host must take back memory its
  processes map or hold: its budget less their anonymous, shared and kernel memory
  (memory.stat's `anon`, `shmem`, `kernel`, `sock`, `zswap`) and the file pages they map,
  wherever those are charged (each process's `Pss_File`, a page shared among them counted
  once), a restored guest's own RAM among them, which comes back charged to the budget as
  the guest reads it again once evicted; no less than its `memory.current` less its page
  cache no process maps, and of what is charged to it no more than its `memory.current`,
  which its kernel counts at once where its statistics may be behind it (just after a
  microVM ended they still counted it, a budget short by 577 MiB told the next); less the
  inactive page cache its kernel keeps beside the file pages the budget's processes map
  before it takes those (mm/vmscan.c, `inactive_is_low`: as many as the mapped under a GiB
  of them). A room of all its page cache no process mapped let one guest fill the budget
  to its last file page and read its own RAM back for 2,100 s, until its job was ended;
  statistics read just after the kernel reclaimed a gigabyte, still counting it, once gave
  a room of all the budget (PM M309). It is told as its run begins, each time a budget
  over it is set or changed (inotify on each cgroup's `memory.high` and `memory.max`) or
  met (its `memory.events`), and as another microVM the budget held ends. Init holds its
  run within it (builtin `ROOM`): the run's `memory.high` never past what it uses and that
  room, and its grower lifting no hold past it, nor plugging more than lets the run reach
  it beside its kernel's memory (with the page structures of what it plugs, a 64th of it:
  a grower that doubled its asks past the cap plugged 16 GiB, whose page structures took
  the budget), so that the guest's own kernel drops its run's page cache before its host
  must take anything, as a container's kernel drops its page cache within its cgroup.
  Where the room is short, the budget's warm microVMs end first, which are speculation;
  then the microVM gives back what it holds cold (`RECLAIM`; idle, it raises no pressure
  that would ask) and is told the room the budget has after, until the budget has room
  again (its `memory.events`, a give-back's end, another microVM's), when it is told so,
  and told again each window of the host's pressure while it is held short, as a guest
  held short asks for nothing its host hears. Its cap is the budget's alone: a give-back
  that held a run below it, at what the run used, once room had come back starved it, a 1
  GiB read crawling at 0.13 MiB/s for 100 minutes (PM M309). And never closer than the
  least room a run goes on in to what the run uses, however short the budget: what its
  kernel charges it ahead of the pages it takes, a batch of 64 pages for each CPU
  (mm/memcontrol.c, `refill_stock`), which no reclaim takes back; two windows of a read's
  read-ahead, 128 KiB each (`VM_READAHEAD_PAGES`); a reader's block as large as a
  share's request (`SHARE_MAX_PAGES`, 1 MiB), which with no swap no reclaim takes either;
  and the page cache that request fills on its way to the block, as many pages: 3.25 MiB
  on 4 CPUs, 6.75 on 18. Held within all but that page cache for the whole of a
  gigabyte's read through FUSE, alone in its slice under a budget a mebibyte short of what
  it held, a run on CI's runners read in 0.80 to 0.88 times its time with none at p50 on
  each of five runner CPUs, its slice refaulting none at p50 (PM M318), but its guest
  took its reads' own pages back and read them again, 2,899 times a read at the median on
  the EPYC 7763s and 16,327 at p90, its reader at times asleep at its run's
  `memory.high`, and 3 of 144 reads took over twice their CPU's time with none, 2.77
  times at most (an EPYC 9V74's); with it, 1 and 687 times, and of 288 reads on four
  runner CPUs none over 1.25 times its time with none (PM M321). Before the share kept its
  buffers, held within 2, 4, 8 or 16 times it, no faster than within it, 2.2 to 3.1 times
  its time with none (a Xeon's three reads at 8 times, 1.07), the share's fresh memory for
  each request holding it back (PM M314). Held at what it used, a run could not take a
  page past it: its reader slept in the kernel's throttle of a cgroup past its
  `memory.high` (`__mem_cgroup_handle_over_high`, up to 2 s each return to user space),
  and on CI read a gigabyte at 0.16 to 0.57 MiB/s for 190 to 672 s, each until its
  budget's own pressure brought room back (PM M309). A room short of the least raises no
  hold past what the run was held at, so that being told it again each window lets its run
  grow none, and lowers one its run no longer fills. Init answers what it holds the run
  within, which the daemon's log says where it is past the room the budget leaves. The cap
  is kept in whole pages, as the kernel keeps `memory.high` (`page_counter_memparse`): one
  past a page boundary read back short of itself, and the grower took a run held at it for
  one held short of it, writing its hold again at each of its run's events. A warm microVM
  restored under a budget copies its template's written pages ahead of its run as any
  does (64 MiB at most each, `hv::PREFETCH_PRIVATE`, which every warm microVM spends of
  the budget before any run comes: 65 MiB of a 384 MiB budget's anonymous memory for one
  such VM, 1 to 4 MiB for one without, PM M309). Restored with none, as from M309 to M333,
  each read of a budgeted slice's after its first, which met a warm VM restored before the
  budget, took 1.42 to 1.48 times its time with none at p50 against the first's 1.26 to
  1.28, each written page it touched copied as its run went; with them, 1.20 to 1.22, as
  the first (the test alone on CI's runners, 319 and 320 runs an arm; PM M333). On the Mac
  they bought no time (PM M62), where no budget holds a run. What they hold is a warm VM's,
  which the budget's room takes back first. None is made ahead of the runs that wait where
  its budget has no room.
- **What its host takes back of its guest's RAM is no room** (PM M318). A restored guest's
  RAM is its template's file pages as much as its anonymous memory, and a budget's host
  takes back file pages first. Counted as room as they went, with the inactive pages kept
  beside them, a lone microVM's 71 MiB of them told its guest 111 MiB of room where its
  budget was 23 MiB short; its page cache filled it in 3 s, its host then took back all of
  its RAM it could, and its vCPUs were throttled 68 s as its guest read it back, each
  give-back of a pressure pass telling it its room again. Each microVM's file pages are
  held at the most its VM process has held resident since its run began (its `RssFile`,
  which another VM sharing its template's pages leaves as it is), less those of them it
  let go as it gave back, read first as its run begins, before a budget set later takes
  any back: its host's taking them back makes no room, its own giving back does. Read
  first at a budget's word instead, a budget set a mebibyte short took a lone microVM's
  template's pages back as it was written, and 87 MiB of room was told where none was.
  Held a mebibyte short, alone in its slice, a gigabyte's read through FUSE took 0.80 to
  0.88 times its time with none at p50 on each of 5 runner CPUs (EPYC 7763, 9V45 and 9V74,
  Xeon 8573C and 8370C), 2.07 times at most, its slice refaulting none at p50; none of its
  336 ran away, where 7 of 126 did with the share's copy kept within its reads' room alone
  and 31 of 144 on the tree.
- **Less what its host's own reads need below it** (goal 71's cluster 8). On adacachy2
  (KVM x86_64, CachyOS, Linux 7.3.3, 32 CPUs, so 32 vCPUs; 237f3ebe7) the FUSE budget
  E2E's first read held within the least room ran 28 minutes until it was ended: from 60 s
  to 1,710 s its slice held 127 to 134 MB against a `memory.high` of 123,101,184, 110 to
  118 MB of it anonymous, under 2.1 MB of files and 15 to 16.5 MB neither; its vCPU threads
  and its share's reading thread asleep in `__mem_cgroup_handle_over_high`, its reclaim
  scanning 62 to 247 million pages and its major faults 114,000 to 566,000. Its kernel
  charges a cgroup ahead of the pages its processes take: a charge takes a batch of 64
  pages from its counter and leaves what it did not use on its CPU, up to
  `MEMCG_STOCK_HIGH`, 64 pages a memcg on each CPU (mm/memcontrol.c `try_charge_memcg`,
  `refill_stock`, Linux 7.4-rc2, 2026-11-12), which `memory.current` counts; reclaim at
  `memory.high` takes back pages and drains no such stock (`reclaim_high`,
  `__mem_cgroup_handle_over_high`), which only a write of `memory.high` or `memory.max`
  below what it holds, or a charge past `memory.max`, does (`memory_high_write`,
  `try_charge_memcg`). A share's request in flight and its read-ahead are page cache charged
  to the budget too. The share kept its copy only past that room (`fs::headroom`
  `reads_room`: 64 pages a host CPU, a request, two read-ahead windows), but every room the
  daemon told gave it all to the guest, whose run filled it, and what the host's kernel and
  share charged then had only the guest's own RAM to take back: 2.25 MiB so told on CI's
  4-CPU runners, which hid it, and 9.25 MiB on 32 CPUs. So the room a budget leaves its
  microVMs, and a build's builders, is less that room, the share's own derivation shared
  (`Holding::reads`, read at each count from the host's CPUs online and its page size), and
  a budget's word says it ("leaves N KiB below it for its host's own reads"). It is a kernel
  and protocol bound, not a learned value, and has no cold start; it is an upper bound,
  what its kernel had already charged ahead as the budget was read being counted in what
  it holds too. One daemon's microVMs under a parent are one spawner's scope (D183), one
  memcg, counted once. Tested (light): daemon/budget.rs
  `a_budgets_room_leaves_its_hosts_own_reads_their_room`, a slice whose budget leaves its
  reads' room past all it holds and the inactive pages beside its mapped ones telling its
  microVM none, and the rooms of the other budget tests less it; tests/budget.rs's budget
  short of a lone run counts it as the daemon does. Red at 377d49ca7 with the test
  (adacachy2, Linux 7.3.3-1-cachyos x86_64, 32 CPUs, rustc 1.98.1): its microVM told
  9,699,328 bytes, 32 CPUs' reads' room, where none was left; green with the change:
  shards-vmm's `headroom` tests 4 of 4, shards' `daemon::budget` 8 of 8, clippy of both
  `--all-targets -D warnings` clean. Not run: the E2E and every real VM, ROOT's. Not
  settled without a real VM: what else of that slice's overage was the guest's own least
  room (10.25 MiB on 32 vCPUs, init's `working_room_of`), which a budget short of what its
  run holds leaves its host to find in what its microVM holds cold, and what was its
  guest's free pages on its CPUs' lists, which may grow to an eighth of each zone
  (mm/page_alloc.c `zone_highsize`) and which no report gives back (D151): the
  measurement is ROOT's.
- **The share's copy of what its guest reads, kept only within its budgets' room** (PM
  M318). What a share reads for its guest its guest keeps in its own page cache, so the
  copy its host's page cache keeps beside it is a second one, under a budget charged to
  the run: as the tree's copy filled a lone microVM's slice, its host took back the
  guest's RAM, the slice's mapped files falling from 67 MiB to 15 while it held 213 MiB of
  the copy. The share process drops its copy of each range it reads (`posix_fadvise`
  `POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED`, which lets go of the range's clean pages no process maps, another
  program's of the same file among them) once keeping it would leave the budgets over its
  cgroups, each `memory.high` and `memory.max` short of `max` from its own up, less room
  past it than its own reads need: what its host's kernel charges ahead on each CPU, the
  read in flight and two read-ahead windows, as init's least room has them
  (`fs::headroom`, 2.25 MiB on 4 CPUs). It looks at the budgets again on D215's pace
  (`shards_abi::pace`, `sqrt(2 c w)`; memory-10, R03): `c` its last look's own cost on this
  host, `w` how long its verdicts had been right as that look was made, a look's room on
