its saved file); the order of the restore is OpenVMM's, Microsoft's own VMM over WHP (virt_whp's
`vp_state.rs`, `apic.rs` and `lib.rs`, at 429b72a9).

- **Each vCPU's state** (`hv::whp::state`): its registers as WHP names them, 69 every host reads
  (what it runs from, the MSRs a Linux guest writes, its APIC base, the VP assist page its
  Hyper-V setup gives it, its pending interruption, interrupt state, pending event and activity:
  an AP still held for its SIPI among it) and the optional ones its host reads (the variable
  MTRRs MtrrCap counts, XSS, the CET registers, SPEC_CTRL, TSX_CTRL, TSC_ADJUST, UMWAIT_CONTROL,
  XFD and XFD_ERR, the pending debug exception), asked once a process, each alone; its local
  APIC's page and its XSAVE area by WHvGetVirtualProcessorState (InterruptControllerState2,
  XsaveState), not the two functions it supersedes, which Microsoft's reference marks deprecated
  ("WHvGetVirtualProcessorXsaveState", "WHvGetVirtualProcessorInterruptControllerState2"). A
  restore sets the APIC base first, which the APIC page's mode follows, then the page, then the
  XSAVE area, then every register (XCR0 after the area, OpenVMM's order); a state naming a
  register no snapshot keeps is refused as it is read, as is one taken on another CPU (the
  leaves of its vendor, family, features, XSAVE components and address sizes, as WHP gives a
  guest: not its caches, which a hybrid host's cores describe apart, M258).
- **The partition's time, held.** A partition's TSCs and reference time stand still while it is
  suspended (WHvSuspendPartitionTime), and a partition never run keeps them where it was made
  (M345). A save holds them once every vCPU is parked, reads each vCPU's TSC there, at one
  instant, with the reference time and the Hyper-V MSRs the guest writes once for all its vCPUs
  (its OS ID before its hypercall page, then its reference TSC page), and resumes them: no
  vCPU's TSC comes back apart from another's by however far apart their captures were, and the
  guest's clocks run through the save as a KVM guest's do. A restore holds them before it sets
  them, and they stay held until a vCPU first runs (WHvSuspendPartitionTime's reference): the
  guest's clocks go on from the snapshot whenever its vCPUs are released, a held restore's wait
  (`--hold`) unseen, as KVM's restart their TSCs at the release. Its reference TSC page then
  reads the saved reference time, run on (M345).
- **The IOAPIC is the VMM's** (D140) and is saved with the partition: its registers and each
  pin's line; a level-triggered entry keeps its remote IRR, which the restored local APIC's
  EOI clears.
- **Memory.** A snapshot's memory file is sparse (FSCTL_SET_SPARSE): NTFS keeps no hole it is
  not told to, and writes the zeros of every page up to the last written (M345: a 2 MiB guest's
  four pages took 192 KiB, NTFS allocating sparse files 64 KiB at a time). A restore's RAM is the
  file's runs of data mapped copy-on-write (PAGE_WRITECOPY), a view each, and memory of its
  own between them, zeros (D151), placed at the address its RAM was reserved at:
  guest RAM is reserved as a placeholder that committed memory replaces at once
  (`platform::reserve_ram`), which the restore frees back to its placeholder, splits into one
  a part and replaces with each part's view or memory, leaving no moment in which another
  thread could take the range. WHP maps any view
  at stage 2 (copy-on-write, read-only, shared or of the pagefile, M345); the guest's stores
  land in the view and never in the file, and every restore shares the file's pages in the
  cache until it writes one. The file is made sparse as it is made, by whoever makes it: for a
  confined VM its spawner, since the VM process may make no FSCTL (D141). So is a run's
  swap kept by its save (D176), and every copy that skips zeros makes its file sparse
  before it ends it at its length (`platform::copy_ranges`), or is refused where it may
  not. Four saves of runs at once on windows-2025 took the 29.5 GB its temp disk had free
  within 20 s and failed as it filled, its memory and page file steady (budget-e2e run
  40627507997, its host sampled every 5 s); of a save's files only a run's swap was not
  sparse, which NTFS takes whole as a copy sets its length (M349).
- **Every VM's grants link kept, sealed, for its files' ranges** (M377). A copy reads only
  the ranges that hold data, which a confined VM asks its spawner (`RANGES`). A run's VM,
  given neither a snapshot to save nor a vsock path, let go of its link as it started, and
  saved later read its whole layer, having none to ask: on NTFS a sparse file's holes read
  through its handle while a writable view of it is mapped become allocated, so each save
  of a 10 GiB layer took 10.6 GB of its host's disk while its files held 104 MB, and
  saved.rs still ran windows-2025 out. Every VM now keeps the link and says `SEALED` once
  granted what it starts with: its spawner refuses every grant after, as after a vsock
  path's listen, and answers its ranges for its life (a save's copy then 1.5 MB, 107 MiB of
  the disk). Held by `a_sealed_vm_is_granted_nothing_more_and_its_ranges_are_read`. Until
  platform-03 (PM M570) a VM that staged its snapshots and had no vsock path said no
  `SEALED`, and was granted whatever it asked after its guest started; its last ask now
  seals (`grant_ask::obtain_sealed`), its stages and commits still answered
  (`a_vm_that_stages_its_snapshots_is_granted_nothing_more_once_it_starts`).
- **One partition a process.** WHP maps no memory into a second partition of a process while
  another lives (STATUS_VID_PARTITION_ALREADY_EXISTS, until the first is deleted, M345). A VM
  process holds one; the partition that reads the host's vCPU limit is deleted before it.
- **Windows Server 2022 restores none.** Its WHP (build 20348) sets no vCPU's APIC page back
  through WHvSetVirtualProcessorState: the page as read is refused (ERROR_MORE_DATA), and its
  first 1 or 2 KiB too (E_INVALIDARG), where builds 26100 (windows-2025) and 26200 (jupiter)
  take it whole and in part (M345). The function it supersedes stays unused, deprecated as
  Microsoft marks it, so a snapshot taken there restores nowhere there, and a restore says
  why rather than an HRESULT alone; builds between 20348 and 26100 are unmeasured. Whether
  a host restores is asked of its hypervisor once a process, only where it is asked, so that
  no VM's start pays for it (`vm::restores_here`: the same page set back on a partition of
  one, and only that refusal says no): a daemon there keeps no template or warm pool and
  boots every run cold (D25, D26), and the tests of snapshots skip there, saying why.
- **A confined VM writes its snapshot through its spawner.** An AppContainer writes in no
  directory of its user's (D141), and a directory handle would give it every name in it: the
  spawner makes the snapshot's directory the VM asks to write in, stages each generation there
  on the VM's word (`kind::STAGE`), hands the VM the generation's files to fill, its memory
  and state and what its machine keeps beside them, its writable layer's head and file
  system (D190) and its DAX windows' heads (D189), as `STAGE`'s first byte asks
  (`platform::Kept`), and makes it durable and the one in use on its next (`kind::COMMIT`),
  as the daemon stages a run's save (D176), every file of the generation closed first: NTFS renames no
  directory a file in which is open (ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, M345), so the VM's handed files go
  with its save, and a commit's own close before the rename that puts the generation in
  place, on every host. Once a generation is committed the spawner gives the directory
  up, as a Unix VM seals its own (vm_run.rs `seal`): a guest that took the VM's process over
  later cannot have every later restore of the template restore what it wrote. One staged and
  never committed goes with the VM. A template is saved by its image's first run, whose
  machine has a layer: staged with its memory and state alone, it was refused, and a Windows
  daemon's pools never filled (CI run 40602662393, 2026-10-27).
- **A restore reads its template through its grants**, as on macOS: the pointer, then the files
  of the generation it names (`granted_template`). A backing file's identity is its volume's
  serial number and its file index, as a Unix file's device and inode are: a file of the same
  bytes and times renamed over a disk is another (audit A18). An AppContainer may not even ask
  a file's metadata by its path (M201), so on Windows a restore first reads which backing files
  the snapshot's state names (`snapshot::backing_named`), has them granted, then reads the
  generation, and refuses one whose backing files changed between, a snapshot saved again as
  it was read. Its writable layer, where NTFS clones no file for it, it copies from the
  generation's into the empty file it is given: the ranges that hold data alone, which its
  spawner reads for it (`kind::RANGES`, FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES), as its save copied
  them, each layer's file sparse.
- **A rename over a file Windows will not yet let go of.** The store replaced its pointer and a
  generation's working set by renaming a new file over the old (`write_in`, a POSIX rename,
  M344). On jupiter Windows refused such renames (STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED): a single writer's once
  in 8,000, and eight writers' at once in episodes of a minute and more, Restart Manager naming
  no process holding the file (M345; Microsoft Defender's real-time protection was on, and
  logged nothing); in those holds it refused too the link and the move that might have
  stepped around one, while a rename of a file to a name no file had was never refused. So on
  Windows no write replaces a file: `write_in` lands each as its name's next version
  (`name.~N`, one past the highest listed, by a rename that replaces nothing; a writer that
  finds its version's name taken lists again), flushes the directory, then removes the
  versions before it, and a file at the name itself, where Windows lets them go. Versions
  count from those listed, never from a clock, which may step back. Readers take the newest
  (`platform::newest_in`): the store's pointer and working set, a template's record, and a
  confined VM's, through its spawner, which opens the newest for the path it asks
  (`grant::Access::ReadNewestIfThere`). The store's tidy removes the pointers a newer one
  superseded, and with no pointer to read keeps every generation; the daemon's sweep of
  templates takes every version of a record. Elsewhere `write_in` renames over the file, as
  rename(2) does. In five passes of the probe's writers on jupiter, 30,000 writes, none was
  refused (M345, 6). `point` writes the pointer by `write_in` on every host. A commit's rename
  of its generation's directory was never refused (M345: 2,000 commits, alone and beside
  churn).
- **What a restore costs** (M345, `benches/restore.rs`, jupiter, 256 MiB, n=100): a cold
  restore runs its guest again 69.8 ms after its process starts at p50, 84.8 at p99, a
  `shards restore` start to exit 171 ms; a warm one 59.6 ms after its release at p50, 71.6 at
  p99, its peak working set 10.1 MiB. Nearly all of it is the guest's first touches: a restore
  is ready to run 9 to 10 ms after its process starts, its vCPU entering the guest within 34
  µs of that, and from there to the guest's next store after its snapshot point took 79 to 95
  ms, and 3.4 ms with the whole of RAM populated at stage 2 beforehand (a populate that itself
  took 74 to 79 ms). The same at 1 GiB: what a guest touches, not what it has.
- **Working sets** (`vm::WORKING_SETS`, the platform parity audit's row 11). Without one a
  restore takes each page into stage 2 as its guest first touches it (M345: 6.4 µs a page
  read and 8.3 µs a page written at p50 on jupiter, where a populate maps a 2 MiB range at
  0.4 to 0.7 µs a page, M341). WHP reads back no access bit at stage 2, and a confined VM
  process may not ask its memory file's allocated ranges (an FSCTL, D141); what the VM
  process's host maps of its guest's memory is what it touched, as on KVM (`vm::mapped`):
  its own working set, which QueryWorkingSetEx reads it (`platform::mapped_pages`), a page
  there valid and shareable its file's, read, and one valid and private a copy its guest
  wrote. A fault maps the page it touches alone, whether its file's pages are in the cache
  or read in around it from disk, which go to the cache alone, so no fault-around is held
  off (`platform::FaultAroundOff` holds nothing; windows_process.rs
  `mapped_pages_are_the_working_sets`, `a_fault_from_disk_maps_the_page_it_touches_alone`).
  As KVM's, the first warm restore of a template records it (`vm::RESTORES_RECORD`), for the
  daemon (D25, D26), and `shards restore` of a generation without one hands what it records
  to the CLI that started it, which keeps it beside the generation as the VM ends, on a
  thread of its own (`working_set::keep`): the confined VM writes none of its snapshot's
  files (D30), and the CLI, which waits for its VM as a child, needs no writer process, as
  Linux's, which becomes its VM, does. A restore of a generation that has one maps it ahead
  before its guest runs, every run of its pages populated at stage 2 in two calls
  (WHvAdviseGpaRange, WHvAdviseGpaRangeCodePopulate; `hv::Vcpu::pre_fault_runs`): the pages
  its guest wrote for writing, which copies each one its copy-on-write view of the snapshot
  still shares with the file in the host's kernel, as the guest's first write would, and
  the rest for reading. What a populate costs is its pages': read from the cache, 2.5 µs a
  page on jupiter and 4.7 on CI's windows-2025, its generation held (M421); read from the
  disk, 65 to 87 µs a page on jupiter and 50 to 78 on CI's, as Windows drops a sparse
  file's pages from its cache once no process maps them, held open or not, and a memory
  file is sparse: so a held generation keeps a view of its memory mapped (D25,
  `platform::keep_cached`; M415's 50 to 78 had been put down to CI's WHP running nested,
  M308). With it mapped ahead against without, held, a cold restore ran its guest again
  15.1 ms after its process started at p50 against 17.5 on jupiter (17.0 against 22.4 at
  p99) and 20.4 against 36.0 on CI's, a warm one 2.49 against 6.79 on jupiter; not held,
  59.0 against 108.9 there (M415, M421). On jupiter, 512
  pages populated for writing in one call took 3.68 ms at p50 (n=20), where copying them from
  the VM process, each page's first word written as it holds it (Windows has no call that
  faults a range in writable from user mode, PrefetchVirtualMemory reading one in), took 2.58
  and populating them for reading after it 1.33 in one call or 2.33 a call each (hv::whp
  `a_write_populate_copies_a_views_pages_in_the_kernel`, which checks each copy holds the
  file's bytes and no other page is mapped): one call does both, for about what the two cost.

**Tested.** Unit: the states' round trips and damage, and a state naming any other register
refused (`hv::whp::state`); a restored IOAPIC going on as the saved one; a generation staged by
its spawner reading back once committed, and the store's every on-disk test, which run on
Windows now (`snapshot`), among them eight writers saving working sets into one generation at
once, which on jupiter failed in 3 runs of 10 with no fallback, in 3 of 10 with one retry
after a link, and in none of 25 with each refusal of another writer's file linked in turn; a
write landing as a version beside one held open that shares no delete, eight writers' at once
each landing whole, and a version one past the highest listed (`windows_files`); a spawner
granting a pointer written twice as its newest version (`grant_answer`); on Windows, a spawner
staging and committing a VM's snapshots over real pipes, refusing a stage elsewhere and a
commit of what is not staged, giving the directory up, and removing what is never committed
(`grant_answer`). On real WHP guests (jupiter and CI's windows-2025):
tests/snapshot.rs, every test, the storms of busy machines among them, which run on Windows
now, and the unwritable directory by an access list there; tests/restore.rs, cold restores of
one snapshot side by side and a held (warm) restore whose guest runs nothing until released.
Working sets (the platform parity audit's row 11): unit, `platform::windows_process`
`mapped_pages_are_the_working_sets`, a working set read back exact, the pages touched and no
other, and `a_fault_from_disk_maps_the_page_it_touches_alone`, and `hv::whp`
`a_write_populate_copies_a_views_pages_in_the_kernel`; on real WHP guests, snapshot.rs
`a_restore_maps_ahead_the_working_set_the_restore_before_it_recorded` and images.rs
`repeat_runs_restore_a_template_of_the_image`, a template's working set recorded by its first
warm restore and mapped ahead by the next: each on CI's windows-2025 (41176475317 at
54f7c0fb), which fails rather than skips a VM test it cannot run; and the restore bench's
arms with and without, held and not, n=100 each, on jupiter and CI's windows-2025 (M415,
M421); `platform::windows` `a_file_kept_cached_is_a_view_of_all_of_it_until_it_drops`.

### D195. The daemon and its client on Windows: request slots of named pipes (built)

**2026-11-13, platform-07/08/11 remain open:** handle inheritance, notification-error
waiter lifecycle and chosen pipe quotas require jupiter red/green checks and an online
capacity/admission design. [Commands and held design](../research/measurements/platform-fixes/held.md)
retain those obligations; no Windows check or quota replacement is claimed completed.

**2026-11-14, platform-07 and 08 fixed; 11 open** (PM M578, Windows 11 x86_64 unit tests).
- **07** (7905b3c03; red 5260eea78). A confined spawn gives its child copies of the standard
  handles it is lent, inheritable for its handle list alone, as `spawn_env` did; the caller's
  handles are left as lent. A child of std's Command inherits every inheritable handle of
  this process (CreateProcessW bInheritHandles TRUE, Rust library/std/src/sys/process/windows.rs;
  std's CREATE_PROCESS_LOCK is private and `CommandExt::inherit_handles` unstable, issue
  146407), so each shards spawn holds `INHERITING` to read from its first inheritable handle
  until it has closed them, and `shards_ipc::spawn_std`, through which every production std
  spawn on Windows now goes (the registry's and AWS's credential helpers, the SBOM scan, the
  API client's boot, the Windows VM-binary handoff), holds it to write while std makes its
  child. A new production std spawn must go through `spawn_std`; nothing enforces it but
  review (a workspace `disallowed-methods` would also hold every test's spawns). No literal.
  **Superseded 2026-11-14 (control-04, D248):** no production std spawn remains on any OS;
  `spawn_std` and `INHERITING` are deleted, and each child's handle list names its own alone.
- **08** (6ff8f51f4; red 10bf97ed7). A waiting client watches its list's directory by its
  own name (its OsStr encoded as UTF-16, not through `to_string_lossy`), says no list only
  where the directory is absent (ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND, ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND) and refuses any
  other failed watch; its watch is made before its WaitNamedPipe thread, so a call starts one
  thread at most and leaves one only where the daemon named its lists anew. No literal.
- **11** stays open (held.md).

**2026-11-14, every random byte from ProcessPrng, not BCryptGenRandom** (Hex's ask; its
`hex_exe_imports_only_what_nanoserver_carries` failed on bcrypt.dll, which Windows Nano
Server does not carry). Pipe and slot names (`random_hex`), the VMM's `fill_random` and the
network process's `entropy` all take `shards_ipc::fill_random`, which calls ProcessPrng,
bcryptprimitives.dll's per-process generator (windows-sys 0.61.2's
`Win32_Security_Cryptography`, now shards-ipc's feature alone). It is the source Rust's std
fills its own randomness from (rust-lang/rust 1.98.1, library/std/src/sys/random/windows.rs,
bound raw-dylib in sys/pal/windows/c.rs) and AWS-LC seeds from on desktop Windows
(crypto/rand_extra/windows.c); Microsoft documents it as always returning TRUE
(https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/seccng/processprng). The names stay the
system CSPRNG's, never time or a hasher's seed, so no squatter can guess one and make it
first. A FALSE is `RandomFailed`, typed, and no name is made. Every BCryptGenRandom call is
gone, no fallback kept. No literal.
Shown on Windows 11 x86_64 (the adacachy guest, MSVC 14.44, Rust 1.98.1, 2026-11-14): at
main 8d1c89a05 the shards-ipc and shards-vmm unit-test binaries import
`bcrypt.dll!BCryptGenRandom` (`dumpbin /imports`); at b1c7235ec neither imports bcrypt.dll, only
`bcryptprimitives.dll!ProcessPrng`; `random_names_are_distinct_hex_of_their_length` (4,096
16-byte names, all distinct lowercase hex) and the VMM's `random_bytes_differ_between_calls`
pass, and clippy -D warnings of shards-ipc, -net and -vmm is clean. `shards.exe`'s own
imports are not yet checked (ROOT's).

**Why.** Every feature on every host (the user, 2026-10-27; docs/audit/2026-10-27_platform-parity.md
row 1): on Windows `shards` had no daemon, so no `run IMAGE` and none of the commands of its
microVMs, images, volumes and networks. D185's slots are FIFOs in the home, their
streams handed by `SCM_RIGHTS`, its spawner a forked process: Windows has no FIFO in a
filesystem and passes no descriptor over a socket, and a process there is made, not
forked.

**Decided and built.**
- **Slots, named by files in the home** (`slots/named.rs`). Each list, without streams and
  with, is a named pipe whose name the file `requests/free` or `requests/free-streams`
  gives: a fresh random name each time the daemon makes its lists, the file written whole
  before it is renamed into place, so that a client reads a whole name or none. Its DACL
  grants the daemon's user alone, not an AppContainer of that user's (a VM process's) nor
  another user, and it refuses remote clients. A slot is an instance of its list's pipe: a
  client takes one by opening the name, which gives it an instance no client has opened,
  and no other client can then open that one (PM M340). The daemon's first word on it is
  its number; a slot with streams has three pipes more, `<list>-<N>.in`, `.out` and `.err`,
  each its name's first and only instance, so that no other process holds one first. Then,
  as on Unix, the client writes which streams it opened, what each descriptor its request
  stands for is, and its request. No socket of shards' own is made.
- **Liveness, each way**, as D185's: each side's end ends the other's reads after all it
  wrote (M340). A list's name lives while the daemon holds an instance of its own, as a
  Unix list has its daemon's reader. A client waits for a free slot in WaitNamedPipe, and
  hears of its daemon's end at once, its wait ending as the last instance closes (M348);
  it looks at the list's file again every quarter of a second, for a daemon that made its
  lists again under another name. A slot no client opened is stopped by an event of its
  own. Where the file names no pipe, or the pipe has no instance, the client starts the
  daemon. One daemon a home: it takes `daemon.lock` by LockFileEx (std's `try_lock`).
  A slot's `say` and `answer` being one instance, which its client hears end only once
  every handle of the daemon's has closed, the daemon reads what the client says only
  until its side has said all it will: a run whose microVM was killed left its client
  waiting for ever before (M348). Likewise a run's VM gives up its client's stdio at the
  run's end with its output first and without waiting on a read of its input, which an
  interactive client's open stdin never ends (M348).
- **Waits.** A read of no bytes on an overlapped pipe waits for what comes without taking
  it (M348): the daemon's followers wait on its runs' streams, and on processes' ends and
  events, through `pipe::Poller` (an I/O completion port, and a thread-pool wait on each
  process and event), and clients through `await_any`, where Unix has poll(2) and kqueue(2).
- **Handles where Unix passes descriptors.** A stream of `shards_ipc`'s carries handles:
  the sender duplicates each into its receiver's process (DuplicateHandle), and their
  values follow the message. A child's end takes them only from its spawner, its spawner
  none from it. So the daemon hands a run's VM the client's connection and the slot's
  streams as it does on Unix. A stream the daemon makes in pairs and gives one end of to a
  VM gives that VM its handles from the other: a joiner's connection, its provider's VM's
  (D119), whose run had reached the VM without them (M354). A VM's AppContainer opens no
  file by name, NUL included, which Windows Server refused it where Windows 11 let it open
  it (M351): the daemon opens NUL and gives it beside the VM's link, and the VM holds it
  for every client's stdio it lets go of, an `exec -d`'s among them.
- **A VM not ready says why** (M351). Its error closes its link as it returns, before the
  VM has written it, so the daemon gives a VM whose link closed a second to end of itself
  before it kills it, and says the status it ended with: its word of why reaches the
  daemon's log whole.
- **Cold boots held to the host's CPUs** (M357). Windows' daemon boots every run cold
  until the parity plan's step 4, and Server 2022's always, as it restores nothing (M345).
  Cold boots at once whose vCPUs pass the host's CPUs cost more than their work: eight of
  4 vCPUs at once on a 4-CPU runner took 52 to 55 s each on windows-2022, where one took
  1.6. On WHP the daemon holds the cold boots under way to their VMs' vCPUs of twice the
  host's CPUs, the most runs a second on both CI runners; a VM of more boots alone, and a
  restore takes no turn. Turns are taken in the order asked for (tickets, M357's hang: a
  boot asked for first waited out its client's minute as later ones went).
- **Not held across the host's daemons** (M376). Tried: a slot of the host's taken
  beside a daemon's turn, named mutexes every daemon on the host shared, two on CI's
  4-CPU runners. It tied each daemon to the slowest on its host: on windows-2025, where
  a boot alone takes 0.5 s quiet, 7 of containers.rs's 132 tests failed with it, their
  runs left Created as their boots waited on other tests' daemons' slots past their
  clients' minute, and all 132 passed without it (CI 40782667644 with it, 40796215375
  without it and with D196's sealed link besides, both quiet); on windows-2022 the one
  test that failed without it failed with it too, its daemon's one boot behind the
  others'. Each daemon
  counts its own boots alone: what a boot costs while others boot beside it is to be cut
  where it is spent (M376).
- **Lines and streams.** A slot's line holds 64 KiB, what a Linux FIFO holds (pipe(7)), so
  that what a client leaves untaken is what it leaves on Linux (D185, "What it said last");
  a stream's pipe holds 1 MiB, which moved more than 64 KiB in M340.
- **No spawner process** (D158). A Unix child is forked holding every descriptor its parent
  holds, so the daemon's children come from a process made before it held any. A Windows
  child is made by CreateProcess with the handles named for it alone
  (PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST) and inherits nothing else, so the daemon makes its
  children itself. Having no console, it starts its confined VM processes detached: one
  started with CREATE_NO_WINDOW alone failed as it started (STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED, M348).
- **Another build's daemon steps aside**, `shards run daemon` serves and `shards stop daemon`
  ends it, as on Unix (D185).
- **Containers' directories** (M347). NTFS renames no directory while a file in it is open,
  and a run's VM or a reader of its log may hold one, so a removal marks its run's
  directory instead of renaming it: an empty file `.ID.removing` beside it, made durable by
  the `containers` directory's sync as the rename is; the next start deletes a marked
  directory, then its mark. The directory is deleted where it is once no record of its
  run is being written (a write under way lands in it, which Windows leaves in
  place), and its mark only once that deletion is durable: removals completed together
  share that sync. A directory's entries are made durable by FlushFileBuffers of a handle
  to it that may write, in the VMM's platform and the image store, where Windows synced
  nothing before.
- **Files sized ahead are sparse** (M349). NTFS took every cluster of a file as it was
  sized, so each run's 10 GiB writable layer (D190) took 10 GiB of its disk at once, and
  eight runs filled jupiter's. A run's layer, its swap (D159) and a build's cache part
  (D134) are made sparse before they are sized, as a Unix file is: a running microVM's
  layer took 1.5 MiB.
- **Smaller things a daemon on Windows needed** (M348): guest RAM to plug (D133) reserved
  alone, its commit charge taken as each part is granted, since a host short of commit
  refused it whole; the daemon leaves its home before removing what is left of it, since
  Windows removes no directory a process stands in.

**Measured** (M347, M348, jupiter). A request through a slot costs 143 to 149 µs at p50 and
238 to 253 µs at p99, five times its two lines held open (28 µs), against 83 to 112 µs on
macOS and 34 µs on Linux (M254). A slot takes its daemon 7 µs to make and remove, 28 µs
with its streams, where macOS's FIFOs took 116 and 291 (M255): two are kept offered of each
kind, as on Unix. A removal costs 0.9 to 1.4 ms at p50 with its two syncs, against macOS's
4.3 (M46).

**Tested.** The slots' cases are one set that Unix's FIFOs and Windows' named pipes both
pass (`slots.rs`), beside each host's own (`fifo.rs`, `named.rs`, `pipe.rs`, `poll.rs`):
`shards_ipc`'s tests pass on jupiter, 58 of 58. A mutation run changed one line at each of
23 places of Windows' slots and pipes, among them a pipe's DACL granting Everyone and a
stream's pipe made without FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE, which another process could then
take first, and the tests caught every one: the last a client that read its list's name
just before its daemon made its lists anew (`take_listed`). On jupiter, 2026-10-27, the
daemon's and the containers' unit tests pass, 225 of 225, and tests/daemon.rs with real
microVMs, 37 of 37, `an_idle_daemon_wakes_for_nothing` among them, each thread's cycles
read there (QueryThreadCycleTime) where Linux reads its switches. Its eleven pool and
template tests, which the parity plan's step 4 takes up, skip there (`cannot_pool`), and so
do those of the other suites that reach a daemon's templates, warm pools and saves (images,
run, saved, warm): its daemon boots every run cold until then, though WHP takes snapshots
(D196). Those it leaves out on Windows are Unix's by nature (a terminal's job control,
descriptor limits, systemd's slices) or a later step's (the Engine API's stream, step 8;
FUSE under a budget, steps 6 and 7). Every command of the catalog was asked of a daemon
there once and answered; `pause` said a microVM was not paused on Windows yet, until a
pause became the VMM's own on every host (D191, step 2). On CI's Windows runners, nested in
Azure VMs of 4 CPUs, tests/daemon.rs passes too with real microVMs, 37 of 37 on each, the
same eleven skipping: on windows-2022 (Windows Server 2022, 10.0.20348) and windows-2025
(Windows Server 2025, 10.0.26100) at 61a07442 (CI 40618994939), and windows-2025 at
b7d8ee30 before (CI 40601221843). There it had first failed whole, every VM refused NUL
(M351); then, on windows-2022, two tests whose cold boots ran beside others' waited past
the daemon's 60 s, until cold boots waited their turn (M357). `shards_ipc`'s tests pass on
both, their pipe's DACL read by SID (M354).

**Not on Windows yet**, each refused with a message that says so, each a later step of the
parity plan: a host's network (step 5); a host's directories as volumes and binds (step 6);
memory given back under a budget (step 7); the Engine API, another machine's clients,
`--use-api-socket` and what log drivers wait on a TCP connection for (step 8). Templates,
warm pools and saves are served (step 4, on WHP's snapshots, D196), and published ports
(step 5, D142).

**A waiting client's look at its list (audit of picked constants, 2026-11-09).** A client
whose list's every instance was taken waited 250 ms at a time in WaitNamedPipe, then looked
at its list's file, as a daemon that made its lists again offers on another name: a poll,
its interval picked. It now waits on both events at once (`slots::named::wait_free`): a
thread waits in WaitNamedPipe for as long as it takes (no handle waits for a free instance,
which only WaitNamedPipe does), its end an event, beside a change notification on the
lists' directory (FindFirstChangeNotificationW), armed before the list is read again. A
thread whose list was renamed first is left to its wait, which ends as an instance of the
old name frees or its last closes, or with its process.

| Literal | Was | Now | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LOOK_AGAIN` (ipc slots/named.rs) | 250 ms | none: WaitNamedPipe's end and the directory's change notification | Win32 WaitNamedPipeW (`NMPWAIT_WAIT_FOREVER`), FindFirstChangeNotificationW |

Owed: the ipc crate's tests on Windows (it builds and lints here for x86_64 Windows).

### D194. The registries Docker's daemon configuration names: an insecure one asked in plain HTTP too, Docker Hub's mirrors first (built)

**Found.** A registry off loopback that speaks plain HTTP, a `registry:2` on another
machine of a LAN, a CI job's, could be neither pulled from nor pushed to: shards asked
every registry in HTTPS but loopback's (containerd's defaults, `core/remotes/docker/
registry.go`), and nothing could say otherwise. dockerd takes such a registry from its
daemon.json's `insecure-registries`, and Docker Hub's mirrors from its `registry-mirrors`;
shards read neither, and its `info` left out the `Insecure Registries` lines docker/cli
prints.

**Decided.**
- **Read where Docker's daemons read it** (`shards_registry::registries`): Docker Desktop's
  `~/.docker/daemon.json` (docker/docs `desktop/settings-and-maintenance/settings.md`), the
  rootless engine's `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/docker/daemon.json` or `~/.config/docker/daemon.json`,
  and the native one's `/etc/docker/daemon.json`, `%PROGRAMDATA%\docker\config\daemon.json`
  on Windows (`engine/daemon/_index.md`); what they name taken together, found through the
  environment of whoever asks, as `certs.d` is (D23). A missing file names nothing; one that
  cannot be read, or whose two keys hold what dockerd refuses, fails the pull, naming the
  file and why, as dockerd would not start with it. Checked as dockerd checks them (moby
  docker-v29.8.1 `daemon/pkg/registry/config.go`, `loadInsecureRegistries`,
  `ValidateMirror`).
- **Or one file named** (2026-11-13, CI cluster 14): where `SHARDS_DAEMON_JSON` names a
  daemon.json, that file alone is read, as `dockerd --config-file` names the one dockerd
  reads, and as there one named and missing is an error naming it (moby docker-v29.8.1
  `daemon/command/daemon.go:679-684`): what shards is told of registries apart from the
  Docker on its machine. A client sends it to the daemon with the rest of what registries
  are reached by (`REGISTRY_ENV`). The tests name their own, `{}` (tests/common
  `as_tests_run`), as they give their own `DOCKER_CONFIG`: before, every test read the
  host's files, so a host's mirror, insecure network or a file dockerd would refuse changed
  what a test did; a stand-in host file under `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` naming a mirror dockerd
  refuses failed a build from the tests' own registry (red at 0a3dde0db), and reaches no
  test now (`images`' `a_hosts_daemon_json_reaches_no_test`; `registries`'
  `the_daemon_json_named_is_read_alone`). D194's own E2E tests name their file through it.
- **Which registries are insecure**: one named by its `host[:port]` as a reference names it
  (dockerd's `IndexConfigs` keys), or one with an address in a network named in CIDR
  notation, its name looked up within a dial's time where any network is named
  (`isCIDRMatch`).
- **How one is asked**: in HTTPS first, then in plain HTTP once it answers HTTPS so or never
  finishes the handshake (containerd's `isTLSError`, as a loopback registry on a port is
  asked); one named without a port, once its HTTPS port refuses the connection too, then at
  HTTP's port, as dockerd tries its `https://` endpoint and then its `http://` one
  (`lookupV2Endpoints`). Pulls, pushes, logins and searches alike.
- **Better than dockerd**, three deliberate differences:
  - its certificate is verified where it answers in HTTPS, against `certs.d` and the
    system's roots, as every registry's is: dockerd skips verifying an insecure registry's
    (`newTLSConfig`, `InsecureSkipVerify = !isSecure`) and reads no `certs.d` for it. One
    whose CA no system trusts is refused; its CA in `certs.d` is the remedy, as D167
    refuses `splunk-insecureskipverify` and asks for its CA;
  - its credentials never go to it in plain HTTP: a registry off this machine that asks for
    them there is refused, saying so, where dockerd answers its Basic challenge with the
    password (`daemon/internal/distribution/registry.go`, `newRepository`: one credential
    store for every endpoint). A loopback registry is still given them, as containerd gives
    them (`dockerAuthorizer`);
  - no registry's name is looked up to decide whether it is loopback's: dockerd's networks
    always hold loopback's, so it looks up every registry's name at each pull, and takes one
    that resolves to loopback for insecure. shards takes `localhost` and loopback addresses
    alone, and looks a name up only where a network is named; a registry that resolves to
    loopback is named by its name.
- **Docker Hub's mirrors** (`registry-mirrors`, slice 2): a pull from Docker Hub asks each
  in order first (the order `registry-mirrors` names them in, read as daemon.json's key
  means it), then Docker Hub; pushes, deletes, logins and searches never ask a mirror. A
  mirror is a registry of its own (`Registry::mirror`): its host's certificates
  (`certs.d`) and its host's credentials, where its user logged in to it, never Docker
  Hub's, which dockerd gives a mirror (`newRepository`: one credential store for every
  endpoint); one in plain HTTP off this machine is asked with none. A request of the
  repository goes to the first mirror that has not failed; one that cannot give a manifest
  or a blob, or cannot be reached, is asked nothing more for the pull, so that a broken
  mirror costs one failed request, not one per blob; one with no list asked for
  (referrers, tags) is asked the next request still, as the mirror may hold the next.
  Tested: `registry`'s `a_pull_asks_its_mirrors_first_and_a_failed_one_nothing_more`
  (mutation-checked), and `images`' `a_mirror_daemon_json_names_serves_docker_hubs_pull`:
  `test/image:v1`, a Docker Hub name, pulled from a mirror on loopback, its digest the
  test image's.
- **`info` says them** in the answer shape Engine API clients parse (`SystemInfo`, built
  in daemon/info.rs): `RegistryConfig`'s `IndexConfigs` (Docker Hub's, with its mirrors,
  and each named insecure, not secure), its `InsecureRegistryCIDRs` (the networks named,
  then loopback's) and `Mirrors`; and in its text, laid out as scripts read docker/cli's
  (cli/command/system/info.go `prettyPrintServerInfo`), the `Insecure Registries` and
  `Registry Mirrors` lines, which it left out before.
- **Tested**: `registries`' (each key of daemon.json read with its meaning, and refused
  where it is malformed, a registry insecure by its name or its network, every file read
  together); `registry`'s (a registry at this host's address on its route out answering
  HTTPS in plain HTTP: asked in HTTPS alone unnamed, in HTTPS once and then in plain HTTP
  named, its credentials refused there and never sent; where each kind of registry is
  asked in plain HTTP); `info`'s text and JSON; and `images`'
  `a_registry_daemon_json_names_insecure_is_pulled_from_in_plain_http`: `shards pull image` from
  such a registry fails, then pulls once the rootless engine's file names it, then fails
  again, naming the file, once it holds what dockerd refuses. The fallback and the
  credentials' refusal are mutation-checked.

**Next.** A mirror that answers but stalls a blob's body: the pull's resumes go on asking
it (fetch.rs), where dockerd's pull would fall to its next endpoint.

### D226. Pushes and pulls learn their network path: as many transfers at once as pay, chunks of the size that costs least a byte (built; measurements owed)

**Found.** `shards push image` uploaded a manifest's blobs 5 at once, dockerd's
`max-concurrent-uploads` (moby `daemon/config/config.go`, `DefaultMaxConcurrentUploads`),
whatever the link, where a pull's fetcher measures its connections and doubles them while
that pays (M114): a figure of Docker's machinery, listed open in the de-Dockerify audit
(docs/audit/2026-10-16_docker-framing.md). And it sent each blob in one PUT, as
containerd's pusher does, so a registry that takes no request so large could not be
pushed to at all: nginx refuses a body past `client_max_body_size`, 1 MiB unless set, with
a 413 (nginx.org `ngx_http_core_module`), the limit distribution's own nginx recipe tells
its users to lift "to avoid HTTP 413 for large image uploads" (distribution
`docs/content/recipes/nginx.md`). Measured (M488): where more uploads at once stop paying
differs from link to link, and so does how much they bring. On one host sixteen carried
7.3 times what one did and still gained; across a LAN one carried what the link does and
eight carried less than four; to ttl.sh across the Internet four carried twice what one
did, and blobs of 256 KiB, bound by their round trips, gained to sixteen everywhere. A
blob sent in chunks cost what a request does: whole 632 MB/s on one host, in 8 MiB chunks
421, in 1 MiB 166. Its first version (2026-11-08) still chose three figures, a start at four, a doubling
kept for a tenth more, chunks only after a 413; the user refused them as encoding our own
network: every value is now a protocol's, measured on the path as shards runs, or an
estimator's of what was measured (the table below).

**Decided.**
- **A path is learned, and kept in the home** (`crate::links`): one record a path,
  `images/links/<registry host:port>@<address>`, which its pulls and its pushes learn
  into, each its own part, beside D222's waits and troubles of the path (patience.rs,
  `#[serde(default)]` each part, so a record of one part is read whole); the address
  this host's on its route to the registry: the local address of a TCP
  connection dialled there as the client dials its own (to its proxy, where one is used),
  then let go, one handshake. Over Wi-Fi and over a wire a host has two addresses, so the
  same registry is learned apart over each; two networks that lease the host the same
  address are one path until its samples say otherwise (the aging below). A record holds the
  count of transfers the path converged to, Welford's mean and variance of what each
  window at that count carried, the least a request took to answer, and the bytes of
  bodies sent and the sends that failed. It is written whole by a rename, so a reader
  never sees half of one, and changed only under `links/.lock`, the image store's own
  lock (`Locked`: flock(2), `LockFileEx` on Windows, unlocked before its file closes, PM
  M244): each change reads the record, merges into it what its transfer learned itself,
  and writes it, the lock held throughout, so transfers that end at once, in threads or
  processes, all keep theirs (before, two at once left one's change). The merge
  (`Learned::merge`): samples of the record's count and of the same path (means within
  the pooled standard deviation) are combined by Chan, Golub and LeVeque's pairwise
  formulae (n = nₐ + n_b, δ = mean_b − meanₐ, mean = meanₐ + δ·n_b/n, M2 = M2ₐ + M2_b +
  δ²·nₐ·n_b/n; "Updating formulae and a pairwise algorithm for computing sample
  variances", Stanford STAN-CS-79-773, 1979), exactly what Welford's update over them all
  gives; samples of another count, or of a path that changed, measure another thing and
  replace them, as the climb itself goes on from them; the least answer is the least of
  the two; bytes and failures are summed where the failures are the path's, by the
  aging below. D222's waits merge into the same record (D222). A path's pulls and pushes
  are learned apart within it: a home's uplink and downlink differ (M114 pulled at 98
  MB/s where M488 pushed to ttl.sh at 4.5).
- **A path never seen starts at one transfer and doubles while a doubling pays**
  (`crate::climb`, for push.rs's uploads and fetch.rs's connections alike): TCP's slow
  start (RFC 5681 §3.1), one transfer the least window. Once its requests have answered
  and a count has carried something, it goes straight to what the path needs in flight
  where that is past a doubling: the bandwidth-delay product over the mean blob or layer a
  transfer holds, the bandwidth the most a window carried a second and the delay the least a
  request took to answer, as BBR estimates both (Cardwell et al., ACM Queue 14(5), 2016).
  Never past the cores this process may run on (`available_parallelism`): each transfer
  hashes, runs TLS, and a pull's decompresses, and more contend. Nor past a push's blobs.
- **A window lasts as long as its rate needs** (`climb::Window`): it samples what the
  transfers carried once each of the path's answer times, the least a request took to
  answer (BBR's delay estimate; RFC 6298 §2.1's first second where none is known yet,
  as a round trip assumed before one is measured), and ends once its samples' standard
  error, s/√n (Student, "The probable error of a mean", Biometrika 6(1), 1908), is under
  its mean by as much as `pays` needs (`climb::resolving`), with at least two samples,
  the fewest with a variance. A doubling that pays in full gains the count's own rate m
  (twice the transfers carry twice the bytes); `pays` keeps a gain past the windows'
  pooled standard deviation s, and the gain measured between two counts' means of two
  windows each has the standard error s·√(1/2 + 1/2) (the difference of two means,
  Welch, Biometrika 34(1/2), 1947). Past the line by one of its own standard errors, the
  one-standard-deviation line every test here draws, that is m ≥ s·(1 + √(2/2)) = 2s; a
  window's samples spread as its rate does between windows, so a window ends once twice
  its error is under its mean. A steady path's window is two answer times; a bursty
  one's as many as its bursts need (a burst of four periods' bytes in one sample of four:
  thirteen samples); one whose transfers carry nothing never ends, as nothing it says is
  a rate. Once the count is kept, nothing more is sampled. Before, a window was a second,
  M114's period, chosen. Its first version (2026-11-08) ended a window once the error
  was under the mean alone, the rate told from none: windows so noisy that a doubling
  paying in full read as no gain, and `shards push image` of forty 2 MiB layers at 4
  MiB/s an upload converged at two where every doubling paid (containers.rs'
  `a_push_climbs_from_one_and_the_next_starts_where_it_got` on KVM; simulated over 300
  seeds in `climb::simulated`, 217 settled under four; with the power above, none).
- **A doubling pays only past the path's own noise**: each count is measured over two
  windows after one that settles (two, the fewest that have a variance), and a doubling
  is kept where its mean is above the count before's by more than the two counts' pooled
  standard deviation; one that is not goes back to the count before, kept for the rest of
  the transfer. A lossy path, where more streams lose more, keeps fewer that way.
- **A learned path starts where it converged**, held to the cores; its first two windows
  are judged against the record: where their mean is under the record's by more than the
  pooled standard deviation, the path got worse, and its count is halved, as TCP halves
  its window on a congestion signal (RFC 5681 §3.1, equation 4, the inverse of the
  climb's own doubling), then climbs again from there; one that measures better goes on
  doubling while that pays, as it would. That is its aging: a record is believed as long
  as the path still measures as it did, never for a time chosen. Before (2026-11-08), any
  change either way learned it again from one: a two-sided test at the pooled standard
  deviation, which a path that had not changed failed about one transfer in six (the
  difference of the means has a standard error of about s/√2 against the record's many
  samples, so |Δ| > s is 1.4 of them), each then relearned from one (`climb::simulated`:
  78 of 300 second pushes back to one; halved and one-sided, none). A path's failures age the same way: this transfer's count is added to
  the record's where it is within a Poisson count's spread (the root of its mean) of what
  the record's rate expected for the bytes sent, and replaces it where not.
- **A push's chunk is the size that costs least a byte** (`links::optimum`): a chunk of c
  bytes costs c/rate to send and one request's answer, and a send that fails loses, on
  average, the half of its chunk sent; the time a byte, 1/rate + answer/c + loss·c/(2·rate),
  is least at c = √(2·answer·rate/loss), Young's optimum interval between checkpoints
  (CACM 17(9), 1974), with rate what each upload carries a second, answer the least a
  request took, and loss the path's failures a byte. A path that never failed has no
  finite optimum: a blob goes in one PUT, the fewest requests. One that fails goes in
  distribution-spec v1.1.1's chunks (spec.md, "Pushing a blob in chunks": in order, each
  `Content-Range` inclusive, each answered 202 with a `Location` and a `Range`), then a
  PUT with the digest and no body. A send that fails is resumed from what the registry
  says it has, a GET of the upload's `Location` answered 204 with its `Range`, never from
  the blob's start unless the upload is gone (404, begun again); a file's body is not
  resent whole by the request's own retries. A failure is a reset, a timeout, or a send
  cut short (now a transient failure, not a refusal). Each resume waits a random share of
  how long the trouble has lasted (D222's `Trouble`), and the upload gives up once its
  sends have failed for its path's trouble budget without the registry taking more
  (twice the longest trouble the path passed, at least TCP's R2: crate::patience); no
  count of attempts.
- **The registry's own limits bound the chunk too**: never less than the
  `OCI-Chunk-Min-Length` its POST's answer names (spec.md), and never more than it takes
  in one request: a 413 (nginx before it refuses a body past `client_max_body_size`, 1 MiB
  unless set) makes the next chunk the midpoint of the most it took and the least it
  refused, a bisection that ends at the most it takes. A proxy's 413 comes before the
  registry has the request, so the upload begun stays open and takes the chunks. A refusal
  of a chunk at the registry's least fails the push, naming the request.
- **On every host alike**, through std and what each system documents:
  - The path: each system gives a connected TCP socket the source address its route
    chose, and getsockname says it: Linux (net/ipv4/tcp_ipv4.c `tcp_v4_connect`, its
    source from `ip_route_connect`), XNU (bsd/netinet/in_pcb.c `in_pcbconnect`, from
    `in_pcbladdr`'s route lookup), Windows ("the local association that has been set by
    the system", Microsoft Learn, winsock `getsockname`). A UDP socket's would send
    nothing, but Windows may not say its address before I/O (the same page), so a TCP
    connection is what tells it. The route's gateway and interface (Linux's routing
    table, macOS's SCNetworkReachability, Windows' `GetBestRoute2` and its interface
    LUID) are not read: the source address alone keys the path.
  - The cores: `std::thread::available_parallelism`, each system's count of the CPUs
    this process may run on, as std documents it (on Linux the affinity mask and the
    cgroup's CPU quota taken into account).
  - Failures: std's `io::ErrorKind` of each system's errors (ECONNRESET and WSAECONNRESET
    as `ConnectionReset`, EPIPE as `BrokenPipe`, ETIMEDOUT and WSAETIMEDOUT as `TimedOut`,
    ECONNABORTED and WSAECONNABORTED as `ConnectionAborted`), taken as transient by
    `Error::from`; a send cut short is shards' own error, transient alike.
- **The CPU is bounded by the cores, not their load**: shards reads no host CPU load to
  reuse (its budgets read memory pressure, D188), so the cap is the cores this process may
  run on, and the noise rule finds where contention for them stops a doubling paying.

**Every value, and where it comes from.**

| Value | Where | Source |
|---|---|---|
| a start at 1 transfer | `Climb::new` | RFC 5681 §3.1 slow start, the least window |
| ×2 a step | `Climb::window` | RFC 5681 §3.1: a window doubles a round trip |
| need = ⌈peak · answer / unit⌉ | `Climb::need` | measured bandwidth and delay (BBR's estimators), measured mean blob |
| most = min(blobs, cores) | push.rs, fetch.rs | the push's blobs; `available_parallelism` |
| 2 samples a count | `SAMPLES` | the fewest with a variance (n − 1 ≥ 1) |
| pays: gain > pooled sd | `pays` | Welford's variance of the path's own samples |
| changed: \|Δmean\| > pooled sd | `same` | the same |
| failures kept: \|n − E\| ≤ √E | `links::aged` | a Poisson count's standard deviation |
| c = √(2 · answer · rate / loss) | `links::optimum` | solved minimum of the time a byte (Young 1974); the 2 is a failure's mean loss, half a chunk |
| whole where loss = 0 | `links::optimum` | the optimum has no finite value |
| chunk ≥ `OCI-Chunk-Min-Length`, none where unstated | `Registry::begin` | distribution-spec v1.1.1 |
| midpoint of took and refused | `Registry::chunk` | bisection |
| `0-0` taken as nothing | `Registry::status` | distribution `blobupload.go`: an upload of 0 or 1 bytes says `0-0` |
| a sample each answer time | `climb::period` | the path's least answer (BBR's delay estimate); RFC 6298 §2.1's 1 s where none is known |
| a window ends: s/√n · (1 + √(2/2)) < mean, n ≥ 2 | `climb::Window`, `climb::resolving` | the standard error of the mean (Student 1908); a full doubling's gain past `pays`' line by one standard error of a difference of two means of two windows (Welch 1947); n − 1 ≥ 1 |
| worse: record's mean − now's > pooled sd; halved | `Climb::window`, `worse` | the pooled sd, one-sided; RFC 5681 §3.1 eq. 4's halving |
| no sample once kept | `Climb::settled` | a kept count measures nothing more |
| record changed under `links/.lock` | `links::update` | the image store's `Locked` (flock(2), `LockFileEx`; unlocked before close, PM M244) |
| samples combined: n, mean, M2 | `Spread::combined`, `Learned::merge` | Chan, Golub and LeVeque 1979's pairwise formulae |
| combined only at the same count and path | `Learned::merge` | `climb::same`, the pooled sd; else another count's samples, which replace |
| least answer: min of the two | `Learned::merge` | the least is the delay estimate (BBR) |
| bytes, failures summed | `Learned::merge` | `links::aged`, a Poisson count's spread |
| failures without progress, for the path's budget | `Trouble`, `Client::budget` | D222's: twice the longest trouble the path passed (doubling search), at least RFC 1122's R2 |
| the connection that looks the route up, made within the path's connect wait | `Client::route`, `Client::dial` | D222's learned connect: RFC 6298 over the path's connects |

- **Tested** (Fedora, x86_64; the merge and the window on macOS arm64 too, 2026-11-08):
  `climb`'s `two_spreads_combine_as_their_samples_do` (Chan et al.'s against Welford's
  over all), `a_window_samples_once_an_answer_time`, `a_window_lasts_until_its_rate_is_resolved`
  (steady: two samples; bursts of one in four: more; nothing carried: never);
  `links`' `a_transfers_own_is_merged_into_the_record` and
  `transfers_at_once_keep_every_sample` (eight threads, 200 adds to one record: every
  sample, byte and failure kept); `climb`'s
  `a_spread_is_its_samples_mean_and_variance`, `a_doubling_pays_past_the_noise_measured`
  (1.41 within a √2 spread, 1.42 past it), `a_new_path_starts_at_one_and_doubles_while_it_pays`,
  `a_count_jumps_to_the_paths_bandwidth_delay_product` (10 MB/s, 300 ms, 256 KiB: 12),
  `a_learned_path_starts_where_it_converged_until_it_changed` (worse: halved, then climbs;
  better: climbs on), `a_count_stops_at_its_most`; `climb::simulated`'s
  `a_second_push_starts_where_a_noisy_first_converged` (containers.rs' pacing registry
  simulated, 32 seeds: the first at four or more, the record its count, the second
  starting there and never back to one; mutation-checked: without the power the first
  settles at two, with the two-sided reset the second goes from 16 to one);
  `links`' `a_paths_record_is_kept_by_its_path` (another route, another record),
  `a_chunk_is_the_least_time_a_byte`, `failures_age_by_the_change_measured` (100 expected:
  110 kept, 111 and 89 replace it), `a_links_chunk_follows_its_failures` (1 MB/s, 20 ms,
  1e-5 a byte: 63,246 bytes); `push`'s `uploads_climb_from_one_and_the_next_push_starts_where_they_got`;
  `registry`'s `a_blob_refused_whole_goes_up_in_chunks_the_registry_takes`,
  `chunks_hold_at_least_what_the_registry_asks` and
  `a_failed_send_resumes_from_what_the_registry_has` (a PUT cut off, 4 bytes in: the next
  PATCH starts at byte 4); and containers.rs' `a_push_climbs_from_one_and_the_next_starts_where_it_got`
  (`shards push image` of forty 2 MiB layers at 4 MiB/s a connection: the first starts at one
  and tries a doubling; its measured count and variance are recorded in the home; the
  second starts at the count kept). The real-host test does not require four uploads:
  an idle-policy launcher on a busy host may gain nothing beyond two, or keep one after
  trying two. Convergence to four where each doubling pays is the seeded simulation's
  assertion; the E2E pins the actual decision and its reuse, without imposing a count.
- **Which input bound each case**: M488's first measurements had all its hosts at 32
  cores and at most 16 transfers, so none was bound by the CPU: one host's rose to 16 (the
  blobs), the LAN's and ttl.sh's were bound by the link. The adaptive push's and pull's own
  numbers, cold and warm, over the wired pair (adacachy, adacachy2), the Mac Studios' Wi-Fi,
  and tc-netem's induced loss and delay, are owed (M488's list), as is what the derived
  window does to them against the second it replaced: where a new connection's slow start
  outlasts a settling window of a few answer times, the windows after it see it still
  climbing (owed with M488's).

### D193. A run past its pids limit says so: a `pids-limit` event (built)

**Found** (kiln's harnesses, 2026-10-21). A run held to `--pids-limit` whose processes or
threads were refused, a fork or clone past its cgroup's `pids.max` failing with EAGAIN,
said nothing of it: its command failed as such a failure makes it, and nothing outside its
microVM said why. dockerd says nothing either: no event, and its State has no such field.
A harness that sorts its runs' failures could not tell a pids limit from any other.

**Decided.**
- **init reads the workload cgroup's `pids.events`** as the run ends, where its end is said
  alone and where its joiners go on past it (D119): a `max` count above 0 goes to the host
  before `EXIT` as `PIDS` (shards_abi::run::kind::PIDS, `pids_refused`), with the cgroup's
  `pids.max`, `pids.peak`, the count and `pids.events` whole, as `OOM` goes with memory's
  (D159). `max.imposed`, a newer kernel's count of an ancestor's limit, is not it.
- **The VM process passes it on** (shards_ipc::kind::PIDS), as it passes `OOM`; the daemon
  logs the facts and says a **`pids-limit` event** of the microVM's, shards' own action
  (dockerd has none): its attributes the name and image every event of a microVM's has,
  with `pids.max` and `refused`. Docker's typed State stays Docker's: inspect gains
  nothing.
- **A joiner's too** (D119): init reads its own cgroup's `pids.events` as its process is
  reaped, before its cgroup goes, as its OOM is read (D159), and sends `PIDS` before its
  `EXIT`; the VM process passes it on as it passes a joiner's `OOM`, and the event is the
  joiner's.
- **Tested** (containers.rs `a_run_past_its_pids_limit_says_so`, on real microVMs): a
  `--pids-limit 4` run starting eight threads at once says one `pids-limit` event, with
  `pids.max` 4 and a count of what was refused, and the daemon's log its facts; a run
  within its limit says none; a `--network container:` joiner held to `--pids-limit 4`
  says its own, by its own name (without init's read of its cgroup, the test fails).

### D192. A network's egress: its members' own commands reach the destinations it names, and nothing else (built)

**Found** (kiln's harnesses, 2026-10-21). A run's own command had three reaches past its
microVM: none (`--network none`, and every network by default), its network's own members,
or everything (`--network host`, D124). An Agentfile's egress and remote MCP grants are its
agents' (D59), never the command's (D115). So a sandboxed run could not be granted
"api.anthropic.com on 443, and its name": the one thing an agent harness needs, and
`--network host` gave it all of the host's reach instead.

**Decided.**
- **Where a grant lives: on a network**, as shards' own driver option `shards.egress`
  (`networks::EGRESS`): `docker network create --opt shards.egress=HOST:PORT[,...]`, which
  the Docker CLI, a Compose file's `driver_opts` and the Engine API's NetworkCreate all
  say, so no flag of `docker run`'s is added (its flags stay docker/cli's, held to them by
  the CLI's golden answers). Who is granted: the network's members, each joined by name;
  to whom: each destination, a host's name or an IPv4 address; which port: its TCP port;
  which way: out alone. A network without the option grants nothing past its microVMs,
  as before: default deny.
- **Held by the member's network process**, as a remote MCP server's grant is (D59 part
  seven): its policy the destinations alone (`encode_policy`, no ports, the names), a flow
  passed only to an address its own resolver answered for a destination's name, or the
  address a destination is, on that destination's port; and of names, only the
  destinations' asked of the host's resolver (`SHARDS_DNS` or its own), every other
  question REFUSED. A member asks through the network's relay at 127.0.0.11 (D46), which
  asks the gateway, where the network process answers its members' names and the granted
  ones.
- **Refused where it could not be held.** A destination that is no `HOST:PORT` (a port of 1
  to 65535; a host a name of DNS's letters, digits and hyphens, or an IPv4 address; no
  pattern, no IPv6 address yet), said as the network is made; on a driver but bridge, or
  an internal network, whose members reach nothing past their microVMs; and, as a run
  starts, beside its image's agents' grants past the microVM: its network process holds
  those for the whole microVM, and its command's flows and its agents' come to it alike,
  so the command would reach what the agents were granted (D115).
- **Tested** (containers.rs `a_networks_egress_is_a_grant_of_its_destinations_alone`, on
  real microVMs): a member reaches its destination by name; not another port of the same
  host, not a name the destinations do not name though the host's resolver has it, not
  the destination's address in a microVM that never asked its name; a run of the default
  bridge reaches none of it; and the option's refusals as the network is made. build.rs
  `a_remote_mcp_server_is_a_grant_of_that_server_alone`: beside an image's agents' grants,
  the start is refused. networks' `egress_names_each_destination_and_its_port` holds the
  option's reading.

**Since (D236).** An Agentfile's `NETWORK --egress=HOST:PORT` grants its members
destinations as this option grants a network's: one parser for both, which refuses a host
whose last label is all digits and `localhost`, and takes `host.docker.internal` for the
host itself, the gateway at that port alone, its loopback there.

**DNS authority lifetime (network-03, 2026-11-13).** The network process replaces the
current answer for each granted name and A/AAAA question type, instead of accumulating
addresses. Its next timer includes the earliest DNS expiry; expiry drops the answer's
address storage. Each answer fits DNS-over-TCP's u16 wire length, and each distinct
granted name admits at most the two address question types. No chosen cache limit or
TTL floor is introduced. RFC 2181 §§5.2/5.4/8 define replacement, the shortest received
TTL and a sign-bit TTL treated as zero. Zero TTL retains no authority for a later flow;
supporting a zero-TTL transaction across a separate connect request would require an
explicit transaction identity, which the present guest IP stream does not provide.
Established TCP flows keep their opening authorization until their normal close;
expiry/replacement affects new flows. Clock overflow/allocation failure refuses new
learned authority through the existing policy denial, with io::Error from admission.
Answer owner/class/CNAME validation remains network-11, a separate pending finding.
Native macOS test correction68968478b waits on UDP readiness before invoking the
receive handler, as the real dispatcher does; send completion alone was no delivery
witness. It changes no production authority rule. Native red and merged gates are
in the same evidence record.
[Unit reproduction and remaining VM checks](../research/measurements/network-fixes-v1/README.md#network-03-dns-authority-lifetime).

**Answer records tied to the name (network-11, 2026-11-13).** What a granted name
resolved to is what the resolver answered for that name alone: `shards_dns::a_records`
takes a whole response (QR, OPCODE 0, TC clear, RFC 2181 §9) without error (RCODE 0) to
one IN question, and of its answer section only records of the question's type and
class IN owned by the name, or by the end of its CNAME chain (RFC 1034 §§3.6.2, 4.3.2),
names read with compression (RFC 1035 §4.1.4) and compared without case (RFC 4343). A
record of another owner, class or type, an error or a truncated response, and a chain
that loops grant nothing; both transports read answers through it. Before, every A or
AAAA record of the answer section became the name's address. Red/green and four
mutations (owner, class, RCODE, loop) on macOS arm64;
[evidence](../research/measurements/network-fixes-v1/README.md#network-11-a-responses-addresses-are-its-questions-names-alone).

**Next.** IPv6 destinations (the network process learns A records alone); a destination
on a network whose members' images have agents with grants of their own, held apart by
the address its flows come from; a run's own grant on the default bridge, if one is
asked for beside a network's.

### D191. A run's microVM has every CPU of its host, its workload the CPUs its limits give it (slices 1 and 2 built, its contended start and hold mended, Windows' too)

**2026-11-13, platform-10/11 remain open:** per-thread Windows credit does not prove
aggregate host fairness, and benchmark-derived production periods are not the required
online derivation. [Held findings and cold-start/admission design owed](../research/measurements/platform-fixes/held.md)
record the unavailable Windows checks, normal-priority cold state, measured clock/cost
inputs and still-unresolved cross-process budget owner. No scheduler change or new
performance claim is made by that design record.

**2026-11-14, the governor's own CPU is not charged to the rate** (PM M590). A rate holds the
guest's vCPUs, as `shards_abi::rate` says. The governor thread that holds them is shards' own
cost: on KVM at a quarter of one vCPU it ran 0.247–0.401% of wall (n=8, 2 s windows, no load
of ours and 16 busy loops on 32 CPUs), and nothing while unheld. Tests of a rate bound the vCPUs'
guest time, read in its hypervisor's step, never their VM process's CPU.

**2026-11-14, platform-10 fixed within a process; across processes owed; 11 open** (9f95ae7db,
f0cd08598; red 190b49d9b; PM M578). The Windows governor also keeps a pool for each set of
CPUs its raised threads may run on (GetThreadGroupAffinity: a processor group and a mask,
read at every look): credited half of each of those CPUs' time, charged what its threads ran
raised, kept to half a period of each and none; a thread is raised only while its own credit
and its set's pool both have some. Values: the half is the existing fair-share derivation (a
raised thread beside one busy host thread), now of each CPU; the count of CPUs is the
thread's own affinity, learned at each look, never assumed; the cap is half a `PERIOD` of
each CPU, as a thread's own is (PERIOD itself is platform-11's, open). Cold start: a set's
pool starts full, as a thread's credit does, so a burst of raised threads takes half a period
of each CPU at most before the first look. Failure: a thread whose affinity cannot be read as
it is raised is refused (`raise_current` errs, the thread stays at its priority); one unread
at a later look keeps the set last read. Tested by unit
(`platform::windows_thread::tests::raised_threads_sharing_a_cpu_take_no_more_than_half_of_it`,
three raised spinners pinned to one CPU beside a normal one, and `a_pool_is_half_of_its_cpus_time`).
Pools are per process: another VM process's raised threads draw on pools of their own. Owed
to ROOT, an R02 decision before any code: the host-wide owner (each VM process is in an
AppContainer of its own, `shards.vm.<pid>.<n>`, so no named object is shared; candidates are
a section the spawner creates once per user session and hands every VM process with its
grants, or the daemon's hold governing every VM's raised threads), then on jupiter: two and
four 1-vCPU microVMs of a daemon held to one CPU (started under an affinity mask of one,
`start /affinity 1`, whose microVMs get its mask's CPUs, D191) with a busy guest each, beside a normal-priority host spinner on that CPU, and 2x the host's CPUs of busy
vCPUs across unheld microVMs; the host spinner's CPU time over 60 s, each vCPU's priority
changes, n=20 a side, before and after, through `cpu-elastic/phases.py`.

**The priority governor's period and credit (platform-11, 2026-11-14).** `PERIOD` (100 ms,
the hold's old period) is gone: each look's period is D191's for one thread held to half a
CPU (`HALF`, 500 milli-CPU: the most a fair scheduler gives a thread that contends for its CPU
at all, as a raise matters only where another thread is ready there: beside k ≥ 1 ready
threads of its priority Windows gives each a slice in turn, Scheduling Priorities, as Linux's
fair scheduler gives threads of one weight w / (w + k·w), kernel/sched/core.c
`sched_prio_to_weight`, so 1 / (k + 1) ≤ 1/2, at k = 1 the most: a bound, not a pick),
`granule::period(1, 500 milli-CPU, g)` = 2g, derived as each look begins from g as the
process knows it (`granule::g`; one function with the hold's, migrate-09), the governor's
sleeps teaching g their lateness (`granule::LATE`). On a host whose GetThreadTimes counts
15.625 ms ticks (PM M294), 31.25 ms.
- *Its credit, a thread's and a pool's per CPU: a whole period, where it was half.* One look
  can charge a thread the whole period of its one CPU (every tick of the look landing on its
  runs), a physical bound: the credit holds it, so no single look's ticks put a thread that
  keeps to its half back to normal. At half a 2g period, one tick of slack, a thread running
  1 ms of every 6 charged both ticks of a look went back to normal (the risk platform-11's
  2026-11-14 Status named). A raised thread so takes half a CPU over a long stretch and two
  periods more at most (4g, 62.5 ms at ticks), where it took a period and a half of 100 ms
  (150 ms).
- *Cold start*: the governor measures its wake and its thread clock's step as it starts,
  before it is raised and before its first look (`granule::measure`: one shortest wait, and
  two of its clock's steps of its own CPU time, 31.25 ms at ticks); a thread raised before
  then is credited at a g of `LEAST_WAIT`, a 2 ms period, as small a credit: it may go back to
  normal until the first look, less authority, never more.
- *Failure, typed*: a period that outgrows a u64 of ns (`granule::Outgrown`) raises no thread
  (`raise_current` errs, the thread at its priority) and, at a look, puts every watched thread
  back to normal and lets go of them; a clock that cannot be read leaves g its wake's
  (`Unclocked`), and a thread whose time is unread is refused as before.
- Held (light, Windows): `platform::windows_thread::tests::the_look_is_d191s_period_for_half_a_cpu`,
  `a_look_charged_its_whole_period_keeps_a_thread_raised` (red at half a period's credit:
  none left after one look's two ticks), `credit_carries_a_thread_that_waits_across_its_clocks_steps`
  and `a_pool_is_half_of_its_cpus_time` at 2g. Linted for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc; their run on
  Windows is owed to ROOT: `cargo test -p shards-vmm --lib windows_thread` on windows-2025
  (CI) and jupiter, with `a_thread_that_waits_between_its_runs_stays_raised`,
  `a_thread_run_long_goes_back_to_normal_and_is_raised_again_as_it_waits` and
  `raised_threads_sharing_a_cpu_take_no_more_than_half_of_it` at the derived period, then PM
  M495's start latency (`cpu-elastic/phases.py` against `winnone.patch`, n 100 a side) at 2g
  beside 100 ms.

**macOS's time-constraint pair: each thread's own (platform-11, 2026-11-14).** M10's fixed
pair (`COMPUTATION_NS` 0.5 ms, `CONSTRAINT_NS` 1 ms, and the suspect look at the latter) is
gone, with no fallback (`platform::macos_thread`).
- *Computation: the thread's batch, learned.* The governor already reads each watched
  thread's CPU and run state at every look; the CPU a thread ran between two looks that each
  found it waiting, while it was real-time, bounds every run between its waits in that span
  from above. Its batch is the most such span seen (`learned`), so that no run of it is
  preempted by another real-time thread for its computation's sake; a thread's pair is set
  again when its batch moves it. A vCPU's own waits are in-kernel (HVF's WFI, M8): no user-space
  point sees each, and timing each `hv_vcpu_run` would read a clock at every exit, so the
  governor's looks are where the batch is measured. Held to XNU's bounds, 50 µs to 50 ms
  (osfmk/kern/sched_rt.c `sched_realtime_timebase_init`: `min_rt_quantum`, "smallest rt
  computation (50 us)"; `max_rt_quantum`, "maximum rt computation (50 ms)").
- *Constraint: D191's period for one thread at half a CPU of its computation*
  (`granule::period(1, HALF_CPU, computation)`, twice it; `HALF_CPU` the fair-share bound, as
  Windows' governor's). A guest timer's deadline would be the better constraint where known,
  but no thread's is: HVF arms the guest's virtual timer in the kernel, and one vCPU thread
  serves every timer its guest sets.
- *The suspect's look*: as finely as the host wakes, the cold pair's constraint (twice the
  measured wake, held to XNU's least), where M10's 1 ms was: a look must land in one of a
  suspect's waits where it waits at all. Its own constraint, twice a batch of up to 50 ms,
  looked too seldom: `a_thread_that_waits_between_its_runs_stays_real_time` (4 ms run, 1 ms
  waited) went to timeshare at it on adas-mac-studio.local, and stays real-time at the cold
  one.
- *Cold start*: before a batch is seen, the computation is the host's measured wake
  (`granule::measure`, the lateness of one shortest wait, once a process), held to XNU's
  least: a thread asks for no more than its host's own wake grain until it is seen to need
  more. The governor's own pair is the cold one.
- *Typed failure* (`Unconstrained`): no wake measured, a constraint past D191's
  (`Outgrown`), or a pair the timebase cannot say in a u32 of its ticks leaves the thread at
  its policy, why said; a thread not made real-time is not watched, as before.
- *The demotion rule is M317's, unchanged*: a look each scheduler tick, a suspect after a
  tick run past its last wait, timeshare after a tick of looks finding it running, the
  fail-safe at a second's run (`3 * TICK < FAIL_SAFE`).
- Held: vmm `macos_thread::tests::a_threads_pair_is_its_batchs` (red with the pair held at
  0.5 / 1 ms whatever its batch) and `a_batch_is_the_most_run_between_two_waits`, beside
  M317's three governor tests. Owed to ROOT: M8's and M10's timer-lateness and idle-IRQ runs
  and M317's busy-loop and block-read runs at the learned pair beside 0.5 / 1 ms, through
  `docs/research/measurements/macos-sched/launchd-run.sh` (a user's QoS, not the agent's
  clamp), n and p50/p90/p99/max as M10 reports them.

**The Windows pipes' quotas: each its caller's window (platform-11, 2026-11-14).** `BUFFER`
(1 MiB, M340's throughput) and `LINE_BUFFER` (64 KiB, a Linux FIFO's) are gone, with no
fallback: each pipe is made with its caller's window (`shards_ipc::Window`), its quota each
way (CreateNamedPipeW's `nOutBufferSize` and `nInBufferSize`).
- *A caller whose protocol writes frames of a bound asks for its longest*, so that a writer
  writes one whole without waiting on its reader mid-frame (CreateNamedPipeW, Remarks: a
  write past the quota "will block until the data is read from the pipe"):
  - a [`Stream`] pair's, a message: its 6-byte header, `MAX_PAYLOAD` (a run's request, its
    head and spec, `RunHead::LEN` + `run::MAX_PAYLOAD`) and a u64 for each of `MAX_FDS`
    handles (`pipe::MESSAGE_FRAME`);
  - a share's stream (D197, `shards_ipc::byte_pair`, through `os::share_pipe`, the daemon's,
    an image run's, a CLI's and a remote client's shares): its length word and `fs::MAX_FRAME`
    (`fs::STREAM_FRAME`), a control frame of the VM process's own (a share's tables) longer
    and rarer, waiting on its reader past it;
  - an input pair (`input_pair`), its caller's room, as before (`run::CHUNK`).
- *A caller whose flow has no frame of its own asks for the system's* (`Window::System`): a
  slot's line and its list (D185: on Unix a pipe, holding the kernel's default; an answer
  past it waits on its client, as M261 decided), a slot's streams (a client's stdin, stdout,
  stderr), a pair of bytes written in messages (`plain_pair`, a member's streams) and a
  Docker client's pipe (`Listener`, HTTP). CreateNamedPipeW documents no default for a size
  of zero, so its quota is the one CreatePipe's `nSize` of zero is given ("the system uses
  the default buffer size"; anonymous pipes "are implemented using a named pipe"), read once
  a process from an anonymous pipe made so (`pipe::system_quota`, GetNamedPipeInfo).
- *Cold start*: none to learn; a frame is a protocol bound, and the system's quota is read
  the first time a pipe of it is made (one CreatePipe and its two handles closed).
- *Failure, typed*: a frame of no bytes or past a DWORD is refused (`WindowRefusal`, as
  `io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput`); a system quota that cannot be read refuses the pipe
  (`io::Error`, each time asked). The quota is advisory ("the system default, the system
  minimum or maximum, or the specified size rounded up", CreateNamedPipeW): a reserve below
  a frame is not refused, as a write past it waits on its reader rather than fails, so the
  frame still arrives whole, only waited on; refusing would refuse every pipe on a host whose
  maximum is lower.
- Held: ipc `window::tests::a_pipes_quota_is_its_callers_window` (all hosts; red with a
