there, managed.rs) and its command PID 2, in a mount namespace of its own whose root it
pivoted into, then confined: its uid and gid, no capability, `no_new_privs`, a Landlock
ruleset, the run's seccomp filter.

**Alternatives** (R02), read at their sources:
- runc v1.5.1 (8f2685a4): `runc exec` joins each namespace by its `/proc/PID/ns/TYPE` path, one
  setns(2) each (libcontainer/nsenter/nsexec.c, `join_namespaces`), forks again to be born in
  the PID namespace, and joins the cgroup by writing `cgroup.procs` (process_linux.go,
  `setnsProcess.addIntoCgroupV2`) or, where it can, clone3 `CLONE_INTO_CGROUP`
  (`prepareCgroupFD`); the process then sets its console, `no_new_privs`, LSM labels, its
  seccomp filter, capabilities and user, and closes every descriptor it inherited
  (setns_init_linux.go; CVE-2024-21626).
- crun 1.31 (a84965e1): one setns(2) of the container's process's pidfd with every flag
  (src/libcrun/linux.c, `try_setns_with_pidfd`), clone3 `CLONE_INTO_CGROUP`, then a fork for
  the PID namespace; the child sets every signal to SIG_DFL (container.c,
  `unblock_signals`), then labels, seccomp, capabilities and its working directory.
- Docker's exec terminal (moby docker-v29.8.1, daemon/resize.go `ContainerExecResize`;
  containerd v2.3.5, cmd/containerd-shim-runc-v2/process/exec.go `execProcess.Resize`): the
  runtime hands the pty's master to the shim over a console socket, and a resize is
  TIOCSWINSZ on it, which the kernel tells the foreground group as SIGWINCH (tty_ioctl(4)).

**Decided and built.**
- *Joined as crun joins, from init* (as built first; since confine-10 a command is born of its
  member's starter instead, below, and init joins it to nothing). Init holds a pidfd of a process of the member's command
  (hotplug.rs `member_process`, the command first, each held before it is checked to be the
  member's still, so a PID taken meanwhile is never entered), enters its PID namespace for its
  next child (setns(2) of the pidfd with `CLONE_NEWPID`, Linux 5.8), and makes that child with
  clone3 `CLONE_INTO_CGROUP` into the member's cgroup (run.rs `born_in`), taking its own
  namespace back at once, as `fork_in` does for a run's execs. Born into the cgroup, the child
  is held to the member's `pids.max`, which a move into `cgroup.procs` is not ("Organisational
  operations are not blocked by cgroup policies", cgroup-v2.rst, "PID"): at the limit the
  clone fails EAGAIN and the exec is refused. The child enters the command's mount, network,
  IPC, UTS and cgroup namespaces in one setns(2) of the pidfd; the command pivoted into its
  root (domains.rs `child`), so the mount namespace's root, where setns(2) leaves a joiner,
  is the member's.
- *Confined by the same values, through the same steps.* A member's `Started` keeps its
  `Confinement` (its IDs, the last capability, its Landlock ruleset, its volumes, the run's
  plug roots, the socket directories it receives on, its seccomp filter, its environment and
  working directory as it started), and `domains::confine` is the one function its first
  process and a command run in it call, last before execve: the bounding set, its IDs and no
  group, no capability, `no_new_privs`, its umask, its Landlock ruleset entered, its signals a
  new process's, its seccomp filter. Its failure is typed (`domains::Confining`, a step of
  twelve).
- *One Landlock ruleset, the member's own* (confine-01,
  [docs/bugs/2026-11-13/confine.md](../bugs/2026-11-13/confine.md)). Init makes the member's
  ruleset (`domains::ruleset`: every filesystem right handled, the TCP rights its links do not
  grant, both scopes) as it prepares the member, and keeps it in its `Confinement`. The
  member's first process adds the rules (`domains::rules`: reads and execution under `/`, its
  scratch, `/dev`, its volumes, the plug roots, its sockets' directories), each path as it sees
  it in its mounts before anything of the member's runs, and enters it; a command run in the
  member enters that same ruleset and adds nothing. landlock(7) attaches a rule to the inode
  its descriptor names, and `landlock_restrict_self` copies a ruleset into each new domain, so
  every process of the member is given exactly the rules its first process found. A command's
  rules were found again by name at each exec before: a member that renamed the directory
  holding a nested volume's mount point (the mount goes with it; only a mount point itself
  cannot be renamed) and left a symlink to `/proc` at its old name gave its command every
  right beneath `/proc`, a write to its own `/proc/self/comm` among them, which the member's
  own ruleset refused. Each child holds the ruleset at `domains::RULESET_FD`, next above its
  launch status or error channel, close-on-exec, past the descriptors of init's it closes, so
  its program holds none of it; init's own descriptor of it is close-on-exec, as every
  Landlock ruleset's is. The ruleset made at start fails the member's start, typed as init's
  start's errors are; the step `Confining::Ruleset` is gone.
- *Born of its member's starter, in the member's own Landlock domain* (confine-10,
  2026-11-14, [docs/bugs/2026-11-13/confine.md](../bugs/2026-11-13/confine.md); was: a
  domain of its own). landlock(7) gives a domain to the process that enters a ruleset and to
  its children, and has no way to join one: a command that entered the member's ruleset
  itself, joined and confined from init as above, was a domain beside the member's, and the
  member's scopes (`LANDLOCK_SCOPE_SIGNAL`, `LANDLOCK_SCOPE_ABSTRACT_UNIX_SOCKET`, Linux 6.12)
  held them apart: `docker exec C kill 1`, `pkill`, a supervisor's CLI and an abstract
  socket's client reached none of the member's processes (reproduced: domains.rs
  `a_command_run_in_a_member_signals_its_members_processes` at 457d75daa, `kill(2)` EPERM).
  - *The starter* (init's `starter.rs`). The member's first process, once confined and in
    its working directory, forks it just before its program runs, so it is everything that
    process is: its IDs, no capability, `no_new_privs`, its Landlock domain, its seccomp
    filter, its namespaces and its cgroup. It is that process's child, of no exit signal
    (ROOT, 2026-11-14; was `CLONE_PARENT`, which the kernel refuses that process, PID 1 of
    the member's PID namespace: kernel/fork.c `copy_process`, no namespace's init makes
    siblings, so no member had a starter and every command run in one was refused
    `NoStarter`; red domains.rs `a_member_first_of_its_pid_namespace_has_its_starter`). A
    child that reports by no SIGCHLD is waited for only with `__WCLONE` or `__WALL`
    (kernel/exit.c `eligible_child`), so the member's program, which a program that waits
    for every child would wait on, sees none of it, and it ends with the member, as every
    process of the member's PID namespace does once the reaper exits. It holds one descriptor, its end of a
    seqpacket channel to init (`starter::STARTER_FD`, next above the ruleset's), which the
    member's program never has (close-on-exec); its stdio, the launch status and the ruleset
    it closes. It is not dumpable (`PR_SET_DUMPABLE` 0), so no process of the member's, which
    has no capability, traces it, reads its memory or takes its descriptors (ptrace(2)
    `PTRACE_MODE_ATTACH`, pidfd_getfd(2)). It forks each command (`CLONE_PIDFD`), which lays
    its stdio, makes its session (its terminal's, `TIOCSCTTY`), enters its working directory
    and finds its program there (`run::exec_found`, the member's own search, confine-04), its
    failure said on its error channel as every exec's is. Its commands die with it
    (`PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` SIGKILL, kept across execve under `no_new_privs`).
  - *Its asks.* A start is one message: the exec's id, whether it has a terminal, and five
    descriptors, the command's spec (a memfd init writes: its working directory, candidates,
    arguments and environment, offsets the starter makes pointers of in a private mapping;
    sized by what it holds, no buffer of a chosen size), its stdio and its error channel. It
    answers born (the command's PID in its namespace and its pidfd) or not (its fork's errno:
    `EAGAIN` at `pids.max` is `Refusal::Processes`). It leaves the command's zombie unreaped
    until init has read its end from `/proc/PID/stat` (proc(5), field 52, `wait4(2)`'s form;
    init is root, so it is shown) and asked it to reap it, so that no PID is taken again
    before init has the end it is matched by.
  - *Init waits on none of it* but in its poll loop (run.rs `MemberExec`: asked, born,
    running, done): a process of the member's may stop the starter, or the command before
    it execs, as it may any of its own, which a synchronous wait in init would have let it
    hold init up by. The exec's start (`STARTED` or its refusal) is said once its error
    channel closes or reports; its end once its pidfd is readable.
  - *Its terminal.* A command asked with `tty` is its own session's leader, the pty's peer its
    stdin, stdout, stderr and controlling terminal (setsid, then `TIOCSCTTY` on fd 0, as runc
    makes an exec's), and neither the starter nor init holds the peer once it is born, so the
    master reads EIO as it ends (pty(7)). The exec's terminal, which its host's resizes
    (`EXEC_RESIZE`) size and the kernel tells its foreground group as SIGWINCH, is one lookup,
    `Exec::terminal`: the master its ask holds while asked and born, its stdout once
    running. The starter's first cut (53b5654b5) left the running exec's terminal unsaid
    (`Exec::tty` false), so every resize went nowhere and member_exec's
    `a_command_run_in_a_member_has_a_terminal_that_resizes` waited for its SIGWINCH for ever
    (ROOT, KVM adacachy2 at 8fdd66512 and HVF at 0ce6cdc66). Unit evidence on Linux x86_64
    (adacachy2, 7.3.3, under `unshare --map-auto --map-root-user`): run.rs
    `a_command_run_in_a_member_on_a_terminal_is_sized_by_its_host` red with main's lookup
    (born: `None`) and with the running exec unmarked (running: `None`), green after;
    domains.rs `a_command_run_in_a_member_on_a_terminal_has_it_as_its_sessions` (the member
    PID 1 of its PID namespace; `stty size`, `/dev/tty`, the master to EIO) green on the
    starter as it was, which refutes a starter fault, and red with `TIOCSCTTY` removed.
  - *Typed refusals.* A starter that could not be forked (its fork refused as the member
    started) or that a process of the member's ended is `Refusal::NoStarter` (wire code 7,
    `docker exec`'s 126); its commands running then end with it, their end SIGKILL, as the
    reaper reaps them. A command it could not fork is `Processes` at `pids.max`, `Ended` in a
    namespace whose first process has gone (ENOMEM), else `Joining(errno)`. The starter
    sends a pidfd only with a command born: the kernel writes a `CLONE_PIDFD` number before
    it charges the fork to `pids.max` and lets it go as it refuses it (kernel/fork.c
    `copy_process`, Linux 7.2-rc4 :2335 `put_user(pidfd, ...)`, :2394 `cgroup_can_fork`,
    :2568), so the first cut sent a closed descriptor as a refusal's, its sendmsg failed
    EBADF, and the exec waited for ever where `Processes` was due (confine-11, reproduced at
    `with_starter`'s mutant: init's end polled with nothing queued, `pids.events` `max 1`).
    init's other `CLONE_PIDFD` forks take the number only from a child born (audit,
    2026-11-14): `start`'s clone3 of a member's first process writes it into its
    `managed::Launch`, a bare `RawFd` that no `Drop` closes, made an `OwnedFd` only by
    `Launch::parent`, called past `pid < 0`'s return; the test fixture `managed::tests::Child`
    asserts `pid > 0` before it owns one; and shards-server's sandbox helper
    (`crates/server/src/sandbox.rs`) answers a refused worker `-1` and owns its number only
    past `pid < 0`. Nothing in crates/shards, vmm or ipc forks with `CLONE_PIDFD`.
    `domains::tests::a_first_process_refused_at_pids_max_closes_nothing_at_its_pidfd_number`
    holds the first: start's clone3 into a cgroup of `pids.max` 0 is refused EAGAIN with the
    number written, another descriptor takes it, and it outlives the `Launch` (Linux 7.3.3
    x86_64; red, `open: false`, with the slot a type that closes itself).
  - *Costs* (confine-11, 2026-11-14, [docs/bugs/2026-11-13/confine.md](../bugs/2026-11-13/confine.md)).
    One process of the member's for the member's life, a fork of init's address space as the
    member's first process was, its pages shared copy-on-write until either writes.
    - *Its own processes number what it declared.* The starter is one task of the member's
      cgroup, which the pids controller counts as every task (cgroup-v2.rst, "PID"), and it
      cannot be elsewhere: what it forks is born in its cgroup, and a process of no
      capability cannot put a child into another (clone3 `CLONE_INTO_CGROUP` asks write
      access to the target's `cgroup.procs`), so a starter outside the member's cgroup would
      start commands outside its `pids.max`, `memory.max` and freezing. So `start` commits
      the member's `pids.max` as what it declares and its starter's one task
      (`STARTER_TASKS`, `with_starter`; an overflow refuses the member's start), as a
      container's processes number its `--pids-limit` under runc, whose exec helper is gone
      once its command runs. Counted against what it declared, a member of `processes: 1`
      had no starter (its fork EAGAIN) and every command run in it was refused `NoStarter`,
      and one of two had a command refused at its first. Once its starter has gone
      (`Started::starter_gone`, as init reads its channel's end) its `pids.max` is what it
      declared again, so that a member that ended its starter and reaped it (`__WALL`) is
      given no process more; one that leaves its starter's zombie unreaped holds one less,
      its own doing. A write that fails is said on init's console and leaves the one task.
    - *`top` leaves it out*, with init's standby forks, by the file it runs: every process
      of init's own program, known by the device and inode of its `/proc/PID/exe`
      (procs.rs `image`), never by a name. It was left out by the path that link reads,
      which is a program's path in its own mounts (d_path(9) from a root its mounts do not
      reach), so a member whose image had its program where init's is, as an image's
      `/init` is, was left out of `top` as init's own fork (red
      `a_members_program_at_inits_path_is_listed` at 6f3cd4428, `listed: []`). The
      starter's name, `starter`, which any member's program could take, decides nothing. A
      process of the member's can run no copy of init's file: it is outside the member's
      root, and the processes that run it there, the starter and a command born of it before
      it execs, are not dumpable, so their `/proc/PID/exe` is refused it.
    - *The member's own `/proc` shows it*: it is a process of the member's PID namespace, as
      it must be to bear commands there, so a command that counts that namespace's
      processes counts it (member_exec's `confined pid=4 procs=4`), where runc's `runc init`
      shows only while an exec starts. A member may signal it, and ends what it runs then
      (above).
  - *Alternatives.* Starting from init and entering the member's ruleset: a sibling domain
    (above). The member's namespace init as starter: init's sealed reaper is outside the
    member's Landlock domain and seccomp filter, so what it forks is too. The member's first
    process as the starter's parent: its program would have the starter as a child. Relaying
    each command's end from the starter: a table of children in a process that may not
    allocate; the zombie's `/proc/PID/stat` gives it, kept until init asks.
  - *Owed to ROOT* (real VMs): `cargo test -p shards --profile test-release --test
    member_exec -- --nocapture`, with an exec that runs `kill -0 1` and `kill -TERM 1` in its
    member and connects to an abstract socket the member's program listens on, and an exec
    asked after the member killed its starter (`Refusal::NoStarter`); E2E tests that count a
    member's processes see its starter. confine-11's: `shards top vm` of a run whose member
    runs lists the member's program and not its starter, and `shards exec vm --for MEMBER`
    of a member that declares `processes: 2` runs one command and refuses a second held open
    beside it (`Refusal::Processes`, status 126).
- *Refused environment values* (confine-07): validation returns only the typed
  cause (empty name, NUL, reserved name), never the rejected entry. Both Debug and
  Display are value-free, and the existing member refusal wire renders only that
  safe cause and member identity. A malformed credential is not copied into errors.
- *Its program, environment and directory.* Its environment is the member's as it started,
  the exec's variables over it as moby lays an exec's over its container's
  (daemon/container/env.go, ReplaceOrAppendEnvValues: a name alone unsets one); none may name
  `SHARDS_DOMAIN`. Its working directory is the exec's, else the member's, entered as the
  member. Its program is found on that environment's `PATH` as every exec's is (run.rs
  `candidates`, Go's LookPath), with `docker exec`'s words and statuses when it is not.
- *Its stdio.* Pipes init relays as an exec's, owned by the member's uid as runc's
  fixStdioPermissions gives a command its own, or a terminal: a pty from init's devpts, its
  peer opened through the master (TIOCGPTPEER, Linux 4.13), as a member's `/dev` holds no
  `pts`, owned by the member's uid, the session's controlling terminal (TIOCSCTTY after
  setsid). A resize is init's TIOCSWINSZ on the master, as every exec's (`EXEC_RESIZE`). Its
  TERM, where neither its variables nor its member's name one, is the first of its client's
  terminal types the member's root describes (terms.rs, that root seen through
  `/proc/PID/root`), xterm last. It holds no descriptor of init's but its stdio (its error
  channel close-on-exec, everything above it closed).
- *Asked and refused, typed.* `shards exec vm --for MEMBER NAME CMD` (a flag of shards' own on
  Docker's exec, under "Shards options", as `plug volume --for` names a member, D235). The
  daemon resolves the name to the member's declared index (`devices::NoMember`: no member
  declared, none of that name, or files alone), refuses a user or privileges of its own
  (`commands::MemberExec`), and sends the command with `in-member=N` (abi
  `run::members::EXEC_KEY`) and none of the microVM's defaults under its variables
  (`spec::Options::member`). Init refuses again what the member has not, and says what
  stopped it as `run::members::Refusal` under `exec_failed::MEMBER`: a member that did not
  start, one that has ended (its pidfd's process gone, ESRCH, or its PID namespace's first
  process, ENOMEM, pid_namespaces(7)), its `pids.max` reached, a widening, its namespaces not
  entered, or a step of its confinement, with the errno. The VM process renders each with
  `docker exec`'s status: 1 for what its daemon refuses, 126 for what its runtime could not
  start.
- *It ends with its member.* The member's reaper exits as its command does, which ends its
  PID namespace and every process in it (pid_namespaces(7)), a command run in it among them.
- *A port its member contests* (D122): the command loads no chooser's filter, so its listen
  on a port several members are given is never chosen; connections there reach the member's
  own sockets alone. Default deny holds; the chooser's taking a second listener of a member
  is not built.

**Literals** (none chosen; each a protocol's or this wire's own):

| Literal | Source |
|---|---|
| `in-member=` | the exec's setup entry, beside D231's `member-*=` entries |
| `exec_failed::MEMBER` 2 | the next class after RUNTIME 0 and DAEMON 1 |
| `Refusal` codes 1 to 6 | this wire's own, each a variant |
| `step::JOIN` 12, `step::CONFINE` 13 | run.rs's child's steps, after MKDIR 11 |
| `Confining` 1 to 12 | the steps of `confine` and `rules`, in order |
| `RULESET_FD` 4 | the first descriptor above a child's stdio (0 to 2) and its status or error channel (3) |
| statuses 1, 126, 127 | `docker exec`'s (docker/cli; moby daemon/errors.go) |

**Tests.** Unit: the entry and refusals round trip and nothing cut short decodes (abi
`members::tests`); an exec's variables over its member's and what is refused (init
`enter::tests`); `--for` resolved and refused by type (daemon `devices::tests`), and its
privileges and user refused (daemon `commands::tests`); its variables sent as given, for init
to lay over its member's, and its TERM left for init to choose (`spec::tests`); the client's
request with its member (ipc); `exec --help`'s Shards options (cmdline). On a Linux kernel
with Landlock, as root of IDs past the test's own (`unshare --map-auto --map-root-user`):
`domains::tests::a_command_run_in_a_member_gains_no_landlock_right_its_member_lacks`
(confine-01's member and its command, through `rules` and `confine`, on Linux 7.3.3
x86_64: red before, `member refused (13); command written`). confine-11's, Linux 7.3.3
x86_64 (adacachy2): `a_members_top_lists_its_own_processes_alone` (the starter alive, left
out; green before, as main's path compare matched it too),
`a_members_program_at_inits_path_is_listed` (red at 6f3cd4428: `listed: []`), and with
SHARDS_TEST_CGROUP in a delegated scope
`a_member_runs_as_many_processes_as_it_declares_its_starter_apart` and
`a_command_past_what_its_member_declared_is_refused` (`with_starter` mutated to the declared
count: the first `not born: NotBorn { errno: 11 }`, the second `not asked: Gone`, its member
of one process left no starter; before the starter's pidfd fix the first waited for ever),
`a_member_whose_starter_went_is_held_to_what_it_declared` and
`a_first_process_refused_at_pids_max_closes_nothing_at_its_pidfd_number`. Real VMs, ROOT's
(`cargo test -p shards --profile test-release --test member_exec`):
`a_command_run_in_a_member_is_confined_as_the_member_is` (uid, PID namespace, name, caps and
`no_new_privs`, signals, Landlock on files and TCP, seccomp, cgroup and network, another
member's files by path and by link, and nothing of init's held),
`what_a_member_has_not_is_refused_to_a_command_run_in_it`, and
`a_command_run_in_a_member_has_a_terminal_that_resizes`. Record:
[member-exec-tty-v1](../research/measurements/member-exec-tty-v1/README.md).

**Run on real VMs** (PM M605, 2026-11-15, `SHARDS_REQUIRE_VMS=1`). Those three passed on HVF and on
KVM x86-64, in member_exec's whole runs, 6 of 6 at b8a861356 and at the vendor point 4124d8c70. Still
owed (ROOT): them on WHP and KVM arm64, and the runs *Owed to ROOT* above that member_exec's tests do
not make (an exec's `kill -0 1`, `kill -TERM 1` and abstract socket, an exec after its member killed its
starter, `Refusal::NoStarter`, and confine-11's `shards top vm` and `processes: 2`). M605's unit pass of
shards-init on adacachy2 (Linux 7.3.3) failed `a_members_top_lists_its_own_processes_alone` 3 of 3 ("the
member ended before its exec"), with init as at ce5f97ab6 too, which M605 lays to that host (a
Landlock-confined `execv` of `/bin/sleep`): a green run of it there is owed.

**How it reaches every run.** A command run in a member is the run protocol's exec with
`in-member=N`, resized by `EXEC_RESIZE`, whoever sends it: the daemon for `shards exec --for`,
and step 11's exec lanes, each exec a lane of its own whose ask carries it, a `run::Spec` byte
for byte, to the host's end of their TLS (D238 "Exec lanes", ROOT's design (B), 2026-11-13). So
there is no separate shards-api exec (ROOT, 2026-11-13); Hex's `MemberExec` is an exec lane's
ask. A member's own stdio is attached through step 5's streams (D240).

**A member's own terminal** is D244's.

### D244. A member's own terminal: its stdio a pty whose master init holds, shown as its stdout, typed into through its stdin, sized by its owner (built: plan step 6, an orchestrator's runs, and a daemon's since goal 58's step 6; its real-VM tests passing on HVF and KVM x86-64, PM M605; WHP and KVM arm64 owed)

**Why.** Plan step 6 (G24, D240): kiln shows a harness's own screen and its sign-in, so a
member must be able to run on a terminal of its own, its owner reading what it shows,
typing into it and sizing it, as `docker run -it` gives a container's command. shards-api's
`MemberSpec::terminal` asked for one and was refused `Unsupported` until this.

**Alternatives** (R02):
- Docker's: runc makes the pty in the container (libcontainer/console_linux.go) and hands its
  master over a console socket to containerd's shim, which copies it to the attached
  client's streams; a resize is TIOCSWINSZ on that master (moby daemon/resize.go
  `ContainerResize`; containerd's shim `Resize`), as D243's exec's is.
- A devpts instance of the member's own: a member's `/dev` holds no `pts` (D59), and one
  would add a mount and its device rules to every member for a peer it can be handed.
- Decided: init's devpts, the peer opened through the master (TIOCGPTPEER) and given to the
  member's uid, as D243's exec terminal; the master init's.

**Decided and built.**
- *Asked at create.* `member-terminal=N` (abi `run::members::TERMINAL_KEY`), one for a member
  at most, refused for a member that starts no program, as an input is. shards-api's
  `MemberSpec::terminal` rides the channel's `MemberStage::terminal` (version 11) to the run
  host, which refuses it for a member the image does not declare, one of files alone, or one
  asked twice, and gives the guest the entry.
- *Its stdio.* The member's command's process (PID 2 under its reaper) makes itself a session
  leader (setsid(2)) and the terminal its controlling terminal (TIOCSCTTY), then takes the
  terminal's other end as its stdin, stdout and stderr. Init lets go of its own copy of that
  end, so the terminal hangs up as the member's last process lets go of it.
- *Shown.* Init reads the master as the member's stdout channel (`capture::Pipe::master`):
  what the terminal shows, exactly, credited as any channel. Its end is the kernel's EIO once
  the terminal's last other end has closed (drivers/tty/n_tty.c, `n_tty_read`,
  `TTY_OTHER_CLOSED`), never an abort. Its stderr channel ends at once: nothing writes it.
- *Typed into.* Where its stdin is its owner's too (`MemberSpec::stdin`), init writes the
  owner's bytes to the master (`input::Input::terminal`), as keys typed, reading the
  connection a frame's worth at a time (`run::HEADER` + `run::CHUNK`, the most a `STDIN` frame
  carries, where a pipe's own size bounds a pipe's). The owner's end leaves the terminal
  open, as a typist leaving does; the terminal hanging up ends the input (POLLHUP, as a
  pipe's reader going is POLLERR).
- *Sized.* `ImageGuest::resize(member, rows, cols)` is the channel's `RESIZE`, answered
  `RESIZED` by its ask's id; refused as `ImageRefusal::Spec` for a member its spec gave no
  terminal and as `ImageRefusal::Terminal` in its init's words. The run host runs init's
  `builtin::RESIZE` (21) with the member's index, rows and columns: TIOCSWINSZ on the master,
  a 0 in either leaving it as it is, as an exec's terminal is (run.rs `resize`; runc's
  setupConsole), and the kernel tells the terminal's foreground process group SIGWINCH.
- *Its size at start.* 0 by 0, as the kernel makes a pty: no size is chosen (R03). Its owner
  sizes it once it knows its own screen's.

**A daemon's run** (D238, goal 58's step 6): `shards.terminal=KIND:NAME` gives a member a
terminal of its own, the same entry, with `shards.control=true`, and its resize is a steer of
the member's own lane, run as the same built-in.

**Literals** (none chosen):

| Literal | Source |
|---|---|
| `member-terminal=` | this wire's own, beside D231's `member-*=` entries |
| `builtin::RESIZE` 21 | the next after `NOTICE` 20 |
| the channel's version 11 | ROOT's reservation (9 and 10 were other lanes', and are never used: ROOT, 2026-11-13; D246) |
| `to_host::RESIZE` 11, `to_client::RESIZED` 28 | the next of each |
| `run::HEADER` + `run::CHUNK` | one `STDIN` frame's bound |
| 0 by 0 | the kernel's size of a new pty |

**Tests.** Unit: abi `members::tests::a_member_has_one_terminal_at_most` and
`a_resize_says_its_member_and_size`; init `capture::tests::a_terminals_master_ends_its_channel_as_its_last_other_end_closes`
and `input::tests::a_terminals_input_is_typed_into_it_and_its_hangup_ends_it`, on real ptys;
shards-api `wire::tests::resizes_and_their_answers_read_back_as_said` and the request's
version tests, `session::tests::a_resizes_answer_is_kept_for_its_awaited_ask_alone`, and
`what_the_guest_refuses_is_refused_first` (the terminal rides the request); the run host's
`a_terminal_is_a_running_members_once`. Real VMs, ROOT's (`cargo test -p shards --profile
test-release --test member_exec`): `a_harness_on_a_terminal_of_its_own_is_shown_and_sized_by_its_owner`
and `a_harness_on_a_terminal_of_its_own_reads_what_its_owner_types`. Record:
[member-exec-tty-v1](../research/measurements/member-exec-tty-v1/README.md).

**Run on real VMs** (PM M605, 2026-11-15, `SHARDS_REQUIRE_VMS=1`). Both passed on HVF and on KVM
x86-64, in member_exec's whole runs, 6 of 6 at b8a861356 and at the vendor point 4124d8c70. Owed
(ROOT): both on WHP and KVM arm64.

### D245. A CPU baseline: the CPU every machine a home moves among gives a guest, told each microVM it starts (decided; built on Hypervisor.framework, KVM arm64 and KVM x86-64; on WHP x86-64 its CPU checked at a move, its baseline researched, not built; real-VM runs owed)

A microVM saved on one machine resumes on another only where that CPU has every feature its
guest found (D176 part 6, "Its CPU"). Between two machines neither of which has every
feature of the other, no move goes either way: an M3 Ultra (macOS 26.4) and an M4 Max
(macOS 26.2) refused 38 of 40 at `ready` (PM M460, M462). A baseline is the CPU a guest is
told so that it moves among a set of machines.

**Alternatives.**
- *A named, fixed CPU model.* Firecracker's CPU templates and QEMU's named models are fixed
  feature sets a person picks for a fleet. "Representing one CPU vendor as another CPU vendor
  is not supported", and "Disabling a feature in a CPU template does not generally make it
  completely unavailable to the guest" (Firecracker, docs/cpu_templates/cpu-templates.md).
  A fixed list is a choice of ours (R03), stale with each CPU generation.
- *The meet of each machine's hypervisor's own view* (chosen). libvirt's
  `hypervisor-cpu-baseline` will "Compute a baseline CPU which will be compatible with all
  CPUs defined in an XML FILE", which "is different from cpu-baseline which does not consider
  any hypervisor abilities" (virsh(1)). Hyper-V's dynamic processor compatibility (Windows
  Server 2025) "dynamically calculates the common set of processor features across all
  nodes" (Microsoft Learn, processor compatibility mode). KVM makes a guest's CPUID from
  KVM_GET_SUPPORTED_CPUID's "x86 cpuid features which are supported by both the hardware and
  kvm in its default configuration", constrained, for one, "for feature consistency across a
  cluster" (Documentation/virt/kvm/api.rst §4.46).
- *None*: `ready` refuses a CPU short of the guest's (D176 part 6). A guest keeps its whole
  CPU, and moves only to machines that have more.

**Decision.** `shards configure cpu --baseline CONTEXT[,CONTEXT...]` asks this machine's
daemon and each context's for its CPU as its own hypervisor shows a guest (`move step cpu`,
which runs `shards-vm cpu`), and keeps their meet in the home's `cpu-baseline`. Each microVM
the home starts is told it; the run keeps it (its directory's `cpu-baseline`), its templates
are keyed by it (`run::template`), its plan carries it (`Plan::baseline`), and the machine
moved to checks it against its own hypervisor's view (`covers`) before anything moves,
refusing typed. `arch::cpu` names a CPU per architecture:
- *arm64* (Hypervisor.framework, KVM): ID registers by encoding, each 4-bit field the lowest
  of the machines' (`arch::aarch64::cpu::meet`, the Arm ARM's ID scheme, Linux's own rule
  across a system's CPUs); each vCPU is told the lower of its host's and the baseline's.
- *x86-64* (KVM): leaf 0, the vendor, and CPUID's feature registers (`cpuid::FEATURES`: the
  SDM's and APM's feature leaves; leaf 0DH's XCR0 and IA32_XSS components; leaf 1EH subleaf
  1's AMX instructions; leaf 0x40000001's EAX, KVM's own paravirtual features, which differ
  from host to host), each the AND of the machines' (`cpuid::meet`), of one vendor
  (`Lacks::Vendor` otherwise). A VM's CPUID, KVM_GET_SUPPORTED_CPUID's, is brought within
  it (`cpuid::within`) before the VM's shape is written in (`for_vcpu`: HYPERVISOR,
  TSC-deadline, HTT, APIC IDs, topology), so the shape's bits stay the VMM's. Not in it:
  leaves 1DH and 1EH's subleaf 0 (AMX's tile sizes, numbers that its leaf-7 and XCR0 bits
  gate), leaf 0x40000000 (KVM's signature, every KVM host's alike), leaf 7's EAX (its highest
  subleaf: one a host lacks reads as zeros in `covers`), and family, model and caches, which
  are no features. It holds every feature register of cloud-hypervisor's migration check
  (v54.1 `arch/src/x86_64/mod.rs`, `CpuidFeatureEntry`), and leaves 14H, 19H, 0x80000007,
  0x80000008 and 0x80000021 besides.
- *WHP on x86-64*: none told. Its restore takes only the CPU its snapshot was taken on
  (`hv::whp` `state.rs`), and `configure cpu` says so there. So a move carries that CPU
  (`Plan::cpu_identity`: the leaves of `cpuid::IDENTITY`, which WHP's restore compares, as
  the machine's VM process reads them from a partition's vCPU), and the machine moved to
  refuses another before anything moves (`Refused::CpuIdentity`), where it was refused only
  at the restore, after the whole stream. WHP on arm64 tells a guest its ID registers, as
  KVM and Hypervisor.framework do (`whp_arm64`'s `cpu_id`).

**A baseline on WHP x86-64: researched, not built.** WHP has the means: its
processor-related partition properties (ProcessorFeaturesBanks, ProcessorXsaveFeatures,
CpuidResultList2) "control the processor features that are made available to the virtual
processor of the partition" and are set before WHvSetupPartition (Microsoft Learn,
Partition Property Data Types), and Hyper-V's own processor compatibility mode moves a
saved VM between hosts of different processors by giving it a common set of features,
cancelling a restore whose sets differ, never across vendors (Microsoft Learn, Processor
compatibility for Hyper-V virtual machines). What decides it is live and unmeasured:
whether WHP sets a vCPU state saved on another CPU (the registers of features one CPU has,
an XSAVE area of its components) into a partition told the same features; and a restore
there must give the guest its snapshot's CPUID, as KVM's restore gives it
(KVM_SET_CPUID2 from the snapshot), which shards' WHP restore does not yet. The runs that
decide it: on one Windows host, a partition told a baseline less one feature leaf, saved
and restored into a partition told the same; then between two Windows hosts of different
CPUs of one vendor, of which there are none here.

**Masked, not enforced.** A guest's kernel and programs use a feature only where its CPUID or
ID registers say so; an instruction a program runs regardless is not stopped.

**Literals (R03).** None chosen: each register of `FEATURES` is one the SDM, the APM or KVM's
`cpuid.rst` defines as feature bits; `decode` takes at most `FEATURES.len() + 1` leaves (leaf
0 and each feature leaf once), derived from it. The meet has no threshold.

**Cold start.** A home with no `cpu-baseline` tells none: each guest is told its host's own
CPU, as before, and `configure cpu --none` takes one away. A plan that carries no baseline
field is another build's, refused at `ready` (D176, `Refused::OtherPlan`). A baseline written before a register joined
`FEATURES` names no leaf for it: `within` leaves that leaf the host's, and `covers` checks
only what the baseline names.

**Failures, typed (R04).** `cpuid::Lacks::{Vendor, Bits}` and arm64's `Lacks`, carried as
`Refused::{CpuVendor, Cpu}` (`CpuShort::{Bits, Field}`) on a move's wire (D176 part 6,
"Refused before anything moves"). `configure cpu` across vendors says the machines' CPUs have
no baseline, and why.

**Held by** the unit tests `a_baseline_masks_what_any_machine_lacks`,
`a_baseline_reads_back_as_written` and `a_baseline_holds_supervisor_state_amx_and_kvms_own_features`
(cpuid.rs), `a_vm_told_a_baseline_gives_its_vcpus_no_more` (`hv::kvm`, a KVM VM with no
guest), `a_machine_short_of_a_baseline_refuses_it_by_each_register` and
`a_baseline_masks_every_feature_an_x86_guest_finds` (moves.rs), run on KVM x86-64
([migrate](../research/measurements/migrate/README.md)); `light-gate.sh`'s mutants M4-M10
failed their tests once, at the predecessor's tree. By E2E:
`an_x86_cpu_baseline_is_all_its_guest_finds_and_goes_with_it` (tests/moved.rs, two homes of a
KVM x86-64 machine) and arm64's `a_cpu_baseline_is_all_its_guest_finds_and_goes_with_it` (PM
M497).

**Owed** (ROOT). The x86-64 E2E on KVM x86-64; a move told a baseline between two machines of
different CPUs on KVM x86-64 and on Macs (two-hosts.sh `BASELINE=1`); the arm64 unit tests
(CI on main); WHP x86-64's move refused at `ready` between two Windows hosts of different
CPUs (two-hosts.sh on each; none here), and the WHP baseline's deciding runs above. PM M605's
real-VM batch (HVF and KVM x86-64, 2026-11-15) ran none of them: it ran no `tests/moved.rs`.

**Review migrate-06 (2026-11-13).** KVM's TSC-deadline capability is admitted by the
baseline's CPUID1.ECX24 before vCPU shaping; shaping may not restore a masked feature.
Without a baseline the host capability remains native. [Focused red/green evidence and
remaining two-host checks](../research/measurements/migrate/fix-review-2026-11-13.md).

**Review migrate-08 (2026-11-13).** Arm baseline readiness uses the shared CPU map for
both macOS feature names and Linux HWCAP spellings. Unknown and multi-register names
remain checked conservatively, so a partial baseline does not hide an exposed feature.
[Regression proof, mapped scope and remaining native checks](../research/measurements/migrate/fix-review-2026-11-13.md).

### D246. Members held apart by an orchestrator: each member's reach of the names kept, named in its request and held by the run host before the microVM starts (built; its api_image test passing on HVF and KVM x86-64, PM M605; on WHP and KVM arm64, Hex's run and inithex-02's live twin owed)

**Why.** Kiln plan 01a1cd8e862e7169a074db3d5fa33f3d, step 15 (Hex's): a harness Hex launches
reaches exactly its granted providers and kiln's endpoint. D236 lets an orchestrator keep or
drop each destination for the whole microVM (`Narrowing.destinations`): the network process
holds the microVM to the union of the names kept, each member's init lets it out on its own
destinations' ports, and `held` makes the members that reach a port by name reach it alike.
So a destination kept for one member is reached as well by every other member whose image
names it, and shards-api names no member's destinations before a boot or after it
(`Started` holds the members and each published port's receivers, `Bound::to`, alone). Hex's
grants each name who, to whom, which port and which way, so Hex refused every destination
(`Awaits(MemberDestinations)`) until a run could be held to them member by member.

**Alternatives** (R02):
- *Keep, then hold the run as its boot returns*, as an orchestrator holds a publish to
  `Bound::to`: stop a run in which a member the grants don't name is let out on a kept
  destination's port. That member could reach the destination between its start and its
  stop. Not taken (Hex's lead, 2026-11-12).
- *The orchestrator reads an image's members and their reach before its boot.* A member's
  destinations live in the image's normalized Agentfile (`/.agentfile.json`, in its EROFS
  root in the store; `agentfile::agentfile`), and shards-api holds no store, EROFS or
  Agentfile code: every orchestrator would take on the run host's own reading of the image
  (D109). Not taken.
- *Each member's addresses held apart in the network process*, D236's own deferred
  alternative (Cilium's toFQDNs programs each endpoint's allowed addresses from the answers
  its DNS proxy relays, `Documentation/security/policy/layer3.rst`): a change to init, the
  switch and the network process, where `held` already makes a port's names alike across its
  members, which is what lets one comparison at the run host be exact. Not taken here; it
  stays D236's route to lifting `held`.
- *Each member's reach in the request, held by the run host* (taken). Hex built it first as
  its vendored changes 0002 (shards-api's `Narrowing::members`; the run host's
  `held_apart`, through Hex's shards-gpu), on Shards 66113379 as channel version 5 (Hex's
  cp/t7-goal15-network-grants-r3, ec729e9d and 13ad751f; ROOT's ruling (b') of 2026-11-12).
  Upstream it is version 12, and it holds the remote MCP servers kept beside the
  destinations, since the network process holds the microVM to both alike.

**Decided.**
- *Wire* (image channel version 12): after each member's terminal (version 11, D244), a flag,
  then where it is set each member's kind, name and names (`MemberReach { kind, name,
  destinations }`, each `host:port` as the narrowing keeps it). Unset (`members: None`): no
  member held apart, the names kept are every member's whose image names them, as through
  version 11. A request of version 11 is refused by its version, as every older one is.
- *What a member reaches* (`agentfile::named_reach`): of each member its Agentfile declares,
  its networks' destinations (D236) and its remote MCP servers' (§4.4), as its init lets it
  out to them; the reading `held` makes (`tcp_reach`); and every other name the image grants
  (any member's destination or remote MCP server) on a TCP port its networks open it to any
  address (amended 2026-11-13, inithex-02): its init lets it out on that port to any
  address, and the network process admits a kept name's addresses for whichever member asks
  them, as it holds no member apart, so the member reaches that name by its address once any
  member has resolved it. The run host reads it with the Agentfile it holds a run to
  (`Agentfile::named`). Of those a member reaches the ones kept, destinations and remote MCP
  servers alike.
- *Held* (`api_run::held_apart`, before anything starts): every member the image declares,
  named in the request or not, reaches of the names kept exactly its entry's names (sorted,
  each once; a member in no entry, nothing). Else the run is refused as a widening of what was
  asked (`Cause::Widening`, `ImageRefusal::Widening`), naming the member, what it would reach
  and what it was let. An entry for a member the image declares not is the image's refusal
  (`Cause::Image`), and a member's second entry the request's (`Cause::Request`). Init, the
  switch and the network process are unchanged: under `held`, a member that reaches a kept name
  is let out on its port by its init, and the network process admits only the kept names'
  addresses there, so equal reaches mean each member reaches exactly what it is let.
- *Ports to any address* (`Narrowing.egress`) stay the whole microVM's: the hold is of names.
  An orchestrator that holds its members apart keeps no such port (Hex keeps none).

**Literals.** Version 12, the channel's next version above the one on main as it landed (11,
D244's): a version only appends, so it is the next number up, whichever lane lands first.
Versions 9 and 10, reserved for other lanes as D244 took 11, are never used (ROOT,
2026-11-13): each side decodes its own version exactly (`Request::decode`,
`WireError::Version`), so a request of 9 or 10 is never made, and is refused by its version
as any other is. A
member's entry is at least nine bytes on the wire (its kind, its name's length, its names'
count) and a name at least four (its length): the least sizes `count` refuses a hostile count
by, read off the encoding. No bound, wait or size of its own.

**Tests** (unit, one macOS arm64 host). The wire,
`each_members_reach_rides_the_request_last`: none held apart, an empty list, one member and
two (one reaching nothing) read back as written, every cut refused, a flag that is no flag, a
member of no kind and a hostile count refused by type; `unknown_versions_and_tags_are_refused`
refuses version 8. The Agentfile, `each_member_reaches_its_own_names`: a harness's provider and
the host, an agent's provider and its own remote MCP server, a server every agent is granted,
an agent joining no network, each member's the same read back as the run host reads it. The run host,
`each_member_is_held_to_its_reach_of_the_names_kept`: exact reaches pass; a member left out,
let nothing, let more, or let less than a kept remote MCP server, refused as a widening in
those words; an undeclared member the image's refusal, a second entry the request's; no hold,
nothing kept, and no Agentfile with no entry pass.
Through a port grant (inithex-02, red at 9efde7252 and green after, on macOS arm64,
adas-mac-studio-3): `a_port_grant_reaches_every_name_the_image_grants_on_it` (agentfile: a
and b both granted 443 to any address, a reaching a provider on 443 by name, c another port
alone: a and b reach the provider, c nothing; red, b reached nothing) and
`a_member_granted_a_names_port_is_held_to_that_name` (the run host, the reach derived from
that Agentfile as `agentfile::agentfile` derives it: 443's grant dropped, the provider kept and
a alone let it, refused as a widening naming b; both let it, passes; red, accepted). Mutation:
the port range's lower bound made strict (`lo < port`) fails the first.

**Evidence owed** (ROOT, real VMs).
`cargo test -p shards --profile test-release --test api_image what_the_image_does_not_grant_is_refused_before_boot`
on WHP and KVM arm64 (on HVF and KVM x86-64 it passed, PM M605, 2026-11-15,
`SHARDS_REQUIRE_VMS=1`: in api_image's whole runs, 33 of 33 at 6a0adfc09, KVM twice, and 32 of 32
at the vendor point 4124d8c70): members held apart that would reach other than asked, and an
undeclared member, refused before boot. A boot whose members are held exactly runs, its harness
reaching its kept provider and the host's service and nothing else, another member none of them:
Hex's image_grants_real on KVM, HVF and WHP, once Hex vendors this revision.

**What would falsify it.** A member that reaches a kept name its entry does not let it (then
`named_reach` misses a rule init's netplan follows: a port grant to any address was one,
inithex-02); a run refused where every member's reach is exact (then the narrowing's names and
the build's `host:port` are written apart).

**Evidence owed for inithex-02** (ROOT, real VMs): the
`api_image what_the_image_does_not_grant_is_refused_before_boot` run above (made on HVF and KVM
x86-64, PM M605), and a live twin of
the finding's fixture: a resolves and dials a controlled provider on 443; b, granted 443 to any
address and let nothing, dials its known address directly. The request letting b nothing is
refused before boot; with this guard removed it boots and b's dial connects.

### D247. An orchestrator's rate: D191's hold told through its run's host, in milli-CPU (built; its real-VM test passing on HVF and KVM x86-64, PM M605; WHP and KVM arm64 owed)

**Why.** Kiln plan 01a1cd8e862e7169a074db3d5fa33f3d, step 14: Hex caps each microVM it runs at
its water-filled share of its fleet's CPU budget each window, in milli-CPU, at least the
kernel's least quota (Hex `docs/design/learned-charge.md` C4, `charge::Node::rates`,
`hex_api::MIN_CPU_MILLI`). On Linux its VM's cgroup holds it (`cpu.max`); on macOS and Windows
it has only caps of a whole process (a native helper's control rate, a job's hard cap), which
stop a VMM's device threads with its vCPUs. An image an orchestrator boots (D231) is held by
D191's hold only as its RUN head says, its vCPUs' whole count, and shards-api had no call to
move it: Hex had no rate for a Shards image VM but stopping its process.

**Decided.**
- *The call.* `ImageGuest::rate(rate, patience)`: the CPU time the run's vCPUs may use of the
  host's together, in milli-CPU, or none for no hold. The run host tells its VM (`RATE`, its
  number and the rate) on the VM's link, on a thread of its own as a room is; the VM sets its
  hold and answers (`RATED`): what it holds the vCPUs to, nothing where it lets them be (no
  rate, or every vCPU's whole CPU or more), or why not (`ImageRefusal::Rate`: the microVM not
  started, its governor's thread not made). A VM holds what it is told or nothing, so its run
  host takes any other word as a broken one, never a hold.
- *The hold in milli-CPU.* D191's hold takes its rate in milli-CPU where it took whole CPUs: a
  period's share is `rate × PERIOD / MILLI_PER_CPU`, exact to the nanosecond below (in u128),
  no hold at none or at every vCPU's whole CPU. The daemon's own holds, the RUN head's `cpus`
  and `CPUS`, stay whole CPUs on their link and are held at a thousand milli-CPU each, so its
  runs are held exactly as before. The governor, its period and its reads are D191's:
  the hold holds the whole guest, its kernel's threads and interrupts among it, as `cpu.max`
  holds a VM's cgroup on Linux, while the VMM's device threads go on.
- *Not the guest's cgroup.* The rate is the orchestrator's cap of what its microVM uses of the
  host, the guest's kernel included; the workload's own limits inside it stay its run's (D191's
  `cpuset.cpus` and `cpu.max`), so the call writes no cgroup.
- *The channel.* Version 13, the next above the channel's at its landing (11 is D244's
  terminals, 12 members' reach's): `RATE` 12 and `RATED` 29, after every kind before. The rate
  is one u64, 0 for no hold, so no rate of nothing can be said (that is a pause, D191's). A host
  of an earlier version ends a run at a frame it has no kind for, so a pair that differs
  refuses the run at create. On the VM's link `RATE` 94 and `RATED` 95 (shards_ipc), answered
  as `GUEST_TIME` is, matched by number with the run host's other asks, and none awaited once
  the link closes.
- *One ask.* The client's room and rate are one numbered ask (`session::Asked`), each held while
  it is awaited, and no longer.
- *Its period* (2026-11-13, channel version 17, the Hex lead's ask for plan step 14; moved to
  each `RATED` answer in version 31, 2026-11-14, as D191 derives a period for each rate: D191's
  hold, "Its period, in force").
  `ImageGuest::rate_period()` is the period the run's VM's governor holds a rate over. Hex's
  learner derives its window from it (Hex `learned-charge.md` C1) and copies no 100 ms of its
  own.
  - The run host tells it as the run starts, in `STARTED` (`Started::rate_period`,
    nanoseconds after every field before, the control endpoint's (15) among them; none is
    refused as no period). It reads it from its own build's hold
    (`shards_vmm::vm::hold_period`), which the VM process it carries holds by (D36).
  - It is no shards-api constant: a client of one version beside a host of another hears the
    host's. So the period D191 derives once measured (D191's hold, "Its period") reaches an
    orchestrator as it is, per run, with no client change. A period that came to move with
    each rate would ride `RATED` as well.
  - A request of version 16 (the GPUs a run names, D232, the version before) is refused by
    its version, so no orchestrator waits on a period its host never tells.

**Literals.** `MILLI_PER_CPU` (1000, `vm`): the unit, a CPU's time in thousandths, as
Kubernetes counts CPU, no finer than `1m` ("Resource Management for Pods and Containers", CPU
resource units), and as Hex charges and caps a microVM (`hex_api::MIN_CPU_MILLI`): a unit, not
a tuning. `PERIOD` and `SOONEST` stay D191's, cited to CFS (sched-bwc.rst l. 94-95; kernel
sched). The kinds are the next free numbers.

**Cold start** (R03). Nothing here is learned or estimated. The rate is the orchestrator's
learned number (Hex's water-filled share each window), told as it moves; until it tells one, the
run's vCPUs are held as its RUN head said (an image run's: by none), the microVM's vCPUs its
ceiling, the envelope the person made the ceiling. A rate below what one read of the governor
resolves (`SOONEST`, 1 ms of a period for each vCPU) is held on average: what a period overran
comes off the next ones (D191).

**Tested** (light): vmm `hold`'s `a_rates_share_is_its_thousandths_of_the_period` and
`a_hold_holds_a_rate_below_its_vcpus_alone`, and its tests before, at whole CPUs in milli-CPU;
`image::wire`'s `rates_and_their_answers_read_back_as_said` and the version before refused;
`image::session`'s `a_rates_answer_is_kept_for_its_awaited_ask_alone` and
`a_rate_no_host_hears_is_refused_and_leaves_no_ask` (the room's too, through the one ask);
`api_run`'s `a_rates_answer_reads_as_it_was_asked`; `warm`'s
`a_rate_ask_reads_its_number_and_rate_alone`: green on macOS arm64 at its landing. Their
guards' removal was not run (implementers run no mutation runs, the person, 2026-11-13): each of
seven taken out in turn must fail its test, the hold's none at every vCPU's whole CPU (`holds`)
and its exact share (`share_of`), version 12 refused, an answer kept for its awaited ask alone
and the ask let go once answered or given up (`session`), a VM's other rate than the one asked
refused (`rated_of`), and a `RATE` of other than 16 bytes no ask (`rate_asked`). Real VMs,
ROOT's: `api_image.rs` `the_orchestrators_rate_holds_its_run_to_it` (a one-vCPU run
spinning, held to a quarter CPU, runs its guest within a quarter of the time passing and a
period's share; its vCPU's whole CPU holds nothing; none lifts it), `cargo test --profile
test-release -p shards --test api_image the_orchestrators_rate_holds_its_run_to_it`.

Its period (light, version 17): `image::wire`'s `a_runs_rate_period_reads_back_as_its_host_said_it`
(a nanosecond to a u64's most, its eight bytes last; none and past a u64 refused), `STARTED`'s
round trip and version 16 refused. Owed (ROOT): its two guard-removal mutants (a period of
none read back, version 16 taken), and the real-VM test above, which now reads the run's
period, checks it is its build's hold's, and holds the run to two periods past a quarter
where it took 100 ms as known: run since on HVF and KVM x86-64 (below).

**Run on real VMs** (PM M605, 2026-11-15, `SHARDS_REQUIRE_VMS=1`).
`the_orchestrators_rate_holds_its_run_to_it`, reading its run's period, passed on HVF and on KVM
x86-64, in api_image's whole runs: 33 of 33 at 6a0adfc09 (KVM twice) and 32 of 32 at the vendor
point 4124d8c70.

**Owed.** The real-VM test on WHP and KVM arm64 (ROOT); the seven guard-removal mutants above,
these light tests on Linux and Windows, and `scripts/lint` on the 7 targets (ROOT). How far past
its rate a VM runs at each rate and vCPU count, measured, as D191 owes for its marks.

**Landed** (s37). This entry at `81049eaf6`, `bc395685f`, `e34176b54` and `2d3da286c`, via
`4c5341a3d`; its period at `b8fe24750`, told with each `RATED` answer since `f54dbfe34`. Hex's
adoption, on Hex main: each Shards image VM capped through its rate by its charge learner (Hex
`2e482c5b`, `2a399d82`), over a window the longest of its platform's and each held image VM's
rate period (Hex `48cafffc7`), at Shards `9975d1f55` (Hex `1969a423`).
`docs/research/s37-decision-inventory.md` lists each landing (rows P3 and 14).

**What would falsify it.** A run held to a rate whose guest time over a window passes the rate
by more than a period's share and its vCPUs' overrun; a daemon run, its whole CPUs held in
milli-CPU, held otherwise than before (D191's tests).

### D248. An orchestrator's run host is started holding its three standard streams alone (built; api_image passing on HVF and KVM x86-64, PM M605; on WHP, an SDK run of several images in one process, and Hex's runs owed)

**Why.** "Children get only what they are given" (D26's warm pool, `shards_ipc::spawn`; on
Windows D195's handle list) held for every child shards starts but one: shards-api started
D231's run host, `shards api-run`, through std's `Command`. That hands it whatever another
thread of its orchestrator holds inheritable at that moment, for as long as its VM runs
(CVE-2024-21626's class). On macOS std's spawn, posix_spawnp, sets no
`POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT` (rust-src `library/std/src/sys/process/unix/unix.rs`), and
pipe(2), socket(2), socketpair(2) and accept(2) take no close-on-exec flag, so a descriptor
another thread has just made waits unmarked until that thread marks it; on Windows std's
CreateProcessW inherits every inheritable handle (`inherit_handles`, with no
`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST`; `library/std/src/sys/process/windows.rs`). Hex starts
every program holding its stdio alone, so it booted no image VM on macOS or Windows (Hex plan
step 12; Ada, 2026-11-12: the image class works there too). Hex carried the fix as its
vendored change 0001 (Hex main,
`vendor/patches/shards/0001-image-the-run-host-started-holding-its-three-standard.patch`).

**Alternatives** (R02, R12):
- *std's `Command`* (as it was): the leak above. Not kept.
- *A spawn of shards-api's own* (Hex's change 0001: posix_spawn with file actions for 0, 1
  and 2 and `POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT` on Apple's; CreateProcessW with a
  `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST` of its three; 768 lines): a second copy of what
  `shards_ipc::spawn` does for the daemon, the CLI and the registry's credential helpers. Not
  taken (R12).
- *`shards_ipc::spawn_with`* (taken): the child gets exactly the descriptors named for it,
  each at its number, its signal mask empty and every signal at its default; on Linux every
  descriptor shards holds is close-on-exec (`cloexec_inherited` marks what this process was
  given open); on Windows the three handles alone, in its handle list. Its `Child` waits
  without reaping (`ended`), reaps once (`wait`) and signals only while unreaped (`kill`),
  what the session's own waiter did with libc and windows-sys by hand. shards-api now depends
  on shards-ipc: an orchestrator that vendors shards-api vendors crates/ipc beside it.

**Decided.** The session starts its host with `shards_ipc::spawn_with(program, ["api-run"],
[stdin, stdout and stderr pipes at 0, 1 and 2], not detached, its spec's variables over this
process's)`. A program named alone (`shards`, the spec's default) is found as std's `Command`
found it: the first file of that name in a directory of this process's `PATH` (on Windows
`.exe` added to a name with no extension), else refused (`ImageRefusal::Boot`, "in no directory
of PATH"). It is never taken from the current directory, where std never looks for one either
(its Unix spawn is posix_spawnp, its Windows `resolve_exe` searches PATH, the program's own and
the system's directories; rust-src `library/std/src/sys/process`): `shards_ipc::spawn` is
posix_spawn(2), which would take a name alone as relative to the current directory, and
CreateProcessW, given no application name, searches "the current directory for the parent
process" second and `PATH` last (Microsoft Learn, CreateProcessW, `lpCommandLine`). A directory of `PATH` that is empty, which exec(3) reads
as the current one, is skipped, as std's Windows spawn skips it. A variable's name that is not UTF-8
is refused as the spec's (`ImageRefusal::Spec`, "the run host's environment"), as the spawn
names variables in UTF-8. The host is reaped under the state's lock as `exited` is set, and
killed only while unreaped, by the `Child`'s own lock.

**Literals.** 0, 1 and 2: the standard streams' numbers (POSIX `STDIN_FILENO`,
`STDOUT_FILENO`, `STDERR_FILENO`; Windows' first three in the handle list, as
`shards_ipc::spawn` numbers them). `exe`: the extension CreateProcessW adds to a name that has
none, and std's spawn adds as it searches. None of its own.

**Tests** (unit, one macOS arm64 host). `image::session::tests`:
`a_run_host_holds_no_end_it_was_not_given` (macOS and Windows, in a test process of its own:
a pipe's write end left inheritable, a run host started, that end let go; its read end finds
every writer gone), `a_run_host_takes_its_environment_and_speaks_on_its_streams` (a host named
alone found on `PATH`, its variable said, its stdin's line read back, its stderr empty, its
exit 0; a variable's name not UTF-8 refused as the spec's),
`a_program_named_alone_is_found_on_path_alone` (names on no directory of `PATH`, one of them a
file in the current directory, refused as not found; one named with its directory as it is; a
shell named alone found in a directory of `PATH`), and
`a_feed_sends_its_callers_bytes_within_its_room_then_its_end`, its host's stdin a pipe now
(on every OS). Red/green on adas-mac-studio.local (Darwin 25.2.0 arm64, rustc 1.98.1),
`cargo test -p shards-api image::session`: with the spawn as it was (std's `Command`, behind
the same interface) and 6ab5332f3's fallback (a name alone that no directory of `PATH` holds
passed on as it is), 8 passed and 2 failed, `a_run_host_holds_no_end_it_was_not_given` ("the
run host holds the write end of a pipe it was never given") and
`a_program_named_alone_is_found_on_path_alone` (`Ok("Cargo.toml")` where not found was
expected); as built, 10 passed. Clippy for shards-api, all targets, `-D warnings`: clean. The
Windows leak check is unrun on a host here (CI's Windows legs build and run it).

**Evidence owed** (ROOT, real VMs). `cargo test -p shards --profile test-release --test
api_image` on WHP; on HVF it passed whole, and on KVM x86-64 (PM M605, 2026-11-15,
`SHARDS_REQUIRE_VMS=1`: 33 of 33 at 6a0adfc09, KVM twice, and 32 of 32 at the vendor point
4124d8c70). Hex's image_real on macOS and Windows once Hex vendors this.

**What would falsify it.** A run host that holds a descriptor or handle of its orchestrator's
it was not given (then `shards_ipc::spawn` leaks to every child shards starts, D26).

**2026-11-14, every child (control-04).** D248 held for the run host alone. The flaky3 lane
found the same leak in every other production std spawn (docs/bugs/2026-11-13/control.md,
control-04, 7e452a9fe): on macOS std's `new_pair` (rust-src
`library/std/src/sys/net/connection/socket/unix.rs`) makes a socketpair and then marks it
close-on-exec, and its `Command::spawn` sets no `POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT`, so a child std
starts in that instant keeps what another thread is making (7,473 inherited writers in 20 s of
8-thread stress). In one SDK process run B's `shards` held run A's input pair or output pipe,
so A's member stdin never saw EOF, or A's drain never ended.
- *Decided* (ROOT, option (a)): every production child is started by `shards_ipc`'s spawn,
  on every OS, with cfg twins where Windows needs them: the SDK's `shards` (shards-api
  `client.rs` `spawn_shards`, its watcher on `shards_ipc::Child`'s `ended`, `wait` and
  `kill`), the registry's credential helpers (one `Talk` on every OS; a cancel's helper in a
  job of its own on Windows, `spawn_grouped`), the SBOM scan (`agent.rs`), the Windows
  VM-binary handoff (`cli/mod.rs` `instead`), the browser opener (`oidc.rs`), AWS's
  `credential_process` on Windows (`spawn_in_raw`, cmd.exe's `/C` text kept as it is, as
  std's `raw_arg` passed it) and `SHARDS_VMMAP`'s vmmap (`alloc_count.rs`). `on_path` moved to
  shards-ipc, a `PATH` of the caller's own allowed (the credential helper's). Unix
  `instead` stays an exec(2): it replaces this process, and keeps no descriptor not
  already its own.
- *Deleted* (no legacy paths): `shards_ipc::spawn_std` and Windows' `INHERITING` lock, which
  only it needed (D195's platform-07), with its test. Linux's std uses pipe2 and
  SOCK_CLOEXEC and was not exposed; it takes the one path all the same.
- *Literals.* None in production. The test's 4 making threads and 64 children are a test's
  load, not a runtime value: with std's spawn back, 14 to 26 of the 64 children held a
  socket in each of six runs, so a run where none holds one is not a miss by chance.
- *Test* (unit, macOS arm64): `client::tests::a_started_shards_holds_no_socket_another_thread_was_making`:
  4 threads make and drop `shards_ipc::input_pair`s while `spawn_shards` starts this test
  binary 64 times as a child that reports, from /dev/fd, every socket it holds. On
  adas-mac-studio-3.local (macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.1), `cargo test -p shards-api --lib
  <that test> -- --exact`: red, std's `Command` back in `spawn_shards` (the carrier's
  `mutate.py`), 19, 18 and 14 of 64 children held 1 to 6 sockets each at 85a2727a1, and 26,
  24 and 23 at f25955697; green, none in any of three runs at f25955697. Beside it: `client::tests` (46), `image::session` (41), the registry's
  `credentials` (20) and shards-ipc's tests (78) pass; clippy, `-D warnings`, for shards-ipc,
  shards-api, shards-registry and shards: clean on macOS; on Windows x86_64 (cargo xwin,
  adas-mac-studio.local) clean for the first three, and shards' one error main's own
  (`daemon/health.rs`'s fields unread on Windows, runs-11), none of this change's.
- *Owed* (ROOT): `cargo test -p shards --profile test-release --test api_image` on WHP (on HVF
  it passed, PM M605, above), and an SDK run of several images in one process on HVF and WHP; the
  Windows unit `a_raw_command_line_keeps_its_quotes` and the registry's credential tests on Windows (CI's
  Windows legs).

### D249. An orchestrator's run whose command never started ends failed, in its VM's words (built; api_image passing on HVF and KVM x86-64, PM M605, though no test of it ends a run failed; a real-VM run of each failed end, and Hex's, owed)

**Why.** A run's `DONE` (warm.rs `finish`, `joined_finish`) carries the command's status and,
where the command never started, why not: the words dockerd says for it, after the code dockerd
gives such a run (`start_failed`). The daemon reads both (daemon.rs `run_ended`): the words
for the run's client, the code its client exits with. D231's run host read the status alone
(api_run.rs `follow`, `DONE`'s first byte), so a run whose command never started ended
`RunEnd::Exited` with that code, as a command that ran and exited with it does, and the VM's
words were lost. Hex's image_real found a run's exit wrong on a real KVM node (HEX-IMG-3,
`/bin/sh -c 'exit 3'`, where `shards run --rm --network none` of the same image and command
exits 3; the Hex lead's notes, 2026-11-13).

**Decided.** `api_run::run_end(failed, done, started)`: the link's failure first; a `DONE`
whose status words follow, where its guest never said `STARTED`, is `Failed("its command never
started (status N): WORDS")`; any other `DONE` is `Exited(status)`; no `DONE` is a failure, as
before. That is the daemon's reading (`run_ended`): warm.rs writes the words only for a
command that never ran (`not_run`), and `STARTED` says it ran (ipc's `kind::DONE`,
`kind::STARTED`); the Hex lead's draft made the run host track `STARTED` as the daemon does. No wire change: `RunEnd::Failed` is "its VM, its host or its guest
failed". Whether HEX-IMG-3's command started is not known here: if it did not, its run now
fails saying why, and that cause is its own fix.

**Literals.** None.

**Tests** (unit, one macOS arm64 host).
`api_run::tests::a_command_that_never_started_ends_its_run_failed_saying_why`. Red/green on
adas-mac-studio.local (Darwin 25.2.0 arm64, rustc 1.98.1), `cargo test -p shards --bin shards
-- api_run::`: with the run's end composed as `follow` composed it (`DONE`'s first byte alone),
14 passed and that test failed ("a command that never started ended its run as Exited(128)");
as built, 15 passed. Clippy for shards, all targets, `-D warnings`: clean. Its `STARTED` case
(the Hex lead's): with the words taken whether or not the guest said `STARTED`, as first
landed (f176b3e61), 15 passed and that test failed (`Failed(…)` where `Exited(128)` was
expected); as built, passed.

**Evidence owed** (ROOT, real VMs). Hex's image_real (HEX-IMG-3) on KVM once Hex vendors this,
and `cargo test -p shards --profile test-release --test api_image` on a KVM host. The latter ran
(PM M605, 2026-11-15, `SHARDS_REQUIRE_VMS=1`): api_image passed whole on KVM x86-64 and on HVF,
33 of 33 at 6a0adfc09 (KVM twice) and 32 of 32 at the vendor point 4124d8c70. No test of it
asserts a `Failed` end, so M605 holds no run whose command never started: that run is owed, with
Hex's.

**What would falsify it.** A run whose command started ending `Failed` for its `DONE`, or one
whose command never started ending `Exited`. (Superseded by the amendment below: a started run
whose `DONE` carries init's words ends `Failed`.)

**Amended (2026-11-14): a started run whose init fails ends `Failed` in init's words.** The
person's decision, verbatim "typed failure!". Init can fail a run after it said `STARTED`: its
relay (init run.rs, `workload.relay`) returns a `Failure`, and init sends `SYSTEM_ERR` with its
words and `EXIT` 125. The VM process keeps the words as `not_run` (workload.rs `relay_frames`),
and warm.rs `finish` keeps dockerd's code for them (`start_failed`, 128 here). The run host
read that as `Exited(128)`, which reads as the command's own exit. 5231d8279 (apiend128) fixed
one such cause, init's capture EOF race. Typing the failure stops this hiding any other.
- *`DONE`* carries the code the microVM keeps, then init's own words (warm.rs `done`, both
  `finish` and `joined_finish`), no longer dockerd's text for them. Each reader renders them at
  its own boundary:
  - the daemon (daemon.rs `run_ended`) says them as dockerd does
    (`start_failed(words).0`), for a command that never started, as before;
  - the run host (`api_run::run_end`) types them.
  The Docker CLI and Engine API answers are unchanged: the container's `ExitCode` stays 128 and
  `docker run` still exits 125, 126 or 127 as Docker defines.
- *`run_end`*: a `DONE` with words is `Failed`, its guest having said `STARTED` or not:
  - not started: `"its command never started (status N): WORDS"`, as before, now with init's
    unamended words;
  - started: `"its init failed after its command started: WORDS"`.
  A `DONE` of a status alone is `Exited(status)`. The branch that typed a started run's words
  as `Exited(status)` is deleted. There is one path.
- *API change for Hex* (shards-api `RunEnded.end`, the image channel's `ENDED`). There is no wire
  or VERSION change: `RunEnd::Failed(String)` already exists. A run whose command started and
  whose guest's init then failed it now ends `RunEnd::Failed("its init failed after its command
  started: …")` where it ended `RunEnd::Exited(128)`. An orchestrator matching `Exited(128)` as
  that failure matches `Failed` instead; an `Exited` status is now only ever a command's (or
  `ATTEND`'s holder's) own.

*Literals.* None new.

*Tests* (unit, one macOS arm64 host, adas-mac-studio-3.local):
- `api_run::tests::an_init_that_fails_a_started_run_ends_it_failed_in_inits_words`: through
  `run_end` and `Told::end`.
- `api_run::tests::a_command_that_never_started_ends_its_run_failed_saying_why`: unchanged
  but for its started-with-words case, which moved to the test above.
- `warm::tests::a_runs_done_carries_inits_own_words` (shards-vm-process): words that dockerd
  amends are carried as init said them.

*Results*: adas-mac-studio-3.local (Darwin arm64, rustc 1.99.1), `SHARDS_HELPERS=skip`.
- `cargo test -p shards --bin shards -- api_run::` at 331cdf2a4: 55 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p shards-vm-process -- warm::tests::a_runs_done_carries_inits_own_words`: passed.
- `cargo clippy -p shards -p shards-api -p shards-vm-process --all-targets -- -D warnings`:
  clean.
- Red: with the old guard put back (`if !started && !words.is_empty()`), the new test failed,
  `left: Exited(128)`, `right: Failed("its init failed after its command started: …")`.

*Evidence owed* (ROOT, real VMs): a run whose init fails after `STARTED`, through
`cargo test -p shards --profile test-release --test api_image` on HVF and KVM, and Hex's
image_real once Hex vendors this. M605's api_image runs on HVF and KVM x86-64 (above) hold no
such run.

### D250. An orchestrator's run keeps the network its image links its members to, letting nothing past that the request does not keep (built; its real-VM test passing on HVF and KVM x86-64, PM M605; on WHP and KVM arm64, and Hex's run, owed)

**Why.** D231's run host gave a run a network only where the request kept something past the
microVM or published a port. A request keeping nothing past it (Hex's image class's default:
`Keep::Only([])` for egress, remote MCP servers and destinations, no DNS) of an image whose
members are granted what lies past it (a harness and its provider) then ran with no network,
which the image's own check refuses (`Agentfile::refuse`, "cannot run without a network",
D59): Hex's image_real had Codex refused so on a real KVM node (the Hex lead, 2026-11-13).
That check holds a fact of the guest's: init links each member as the image's
`/.agentfile.json` grants it, whatever a request keeps (crates/init `netplan::plan`), and a
member granted egress, ingress, names or DNS is linked through eth0 (`domains::switch`), which
a microVM with no network has not: init kills it, "its link: the microVM has no address for
its agents' egress".

**Alternatives** (R02).
- *Check the run against the grants the request keeps* (the Hex lead's first draft): the
  refusal goes, the microVM boots with no NIC, and init kills each member linked past it, as
  above. Not taken.
- *Tell init the narrowing, so that it links no member past the microVM*: a setup entry and a
  change to init's netplan, where every other narrowing is the network process's (D231, D236,
  D246), and a guest older than its run host would link them all the same. Not taken.
- *Keep the network, its network process at DenyAll* (taken; the Hex lead's goal 12 found the
  same): the run host starts the network process at `Policy::DenyAll` ("a VM without
  grants") and tells it a policy only where the request keeps something (`tell_net`,
  `NET_POLICY`), so the members are linked as their image grants and nothing passes the
  microVM that the request does not keep, as a run that only publishes has it today. Its cost
  is a NIC and a network process for such a run (unmeasured).

**Decided.** `api_run::network` decides the run's network and its policy, `plan`'s whole
sequence: the grants as the request narrows them (`egress`), each member held apart where
asked (`held_apart`), a bridge where something is kept or the image links its members past the
microVM (`Agentfile::linked_past`: it grants them what lies past it, or their flows cross
init's namespace to eth0, D59), then `Agentfile::refuse`, whose `--network none` refusal takes
`linked_past` too, one rule for both. No wire change.

**Literals.** None.

**Tests** (unit, one macOS arm64 host).
`api_run::tests::a_run_keeping_nothing_past_the_microvm_has_its_members_network_and_no_policy`
(the Hex lead's: nothing kept of an image granting its harness egress and DNS, on a bridge
with no policy; kept whole, on a bridge with the image's policy; an image granting nothing, on
none). Red/green on adas-mac-studio.local (Darwin 25.2.0 arm64, rustc 1.98.1), `cargo test -p
shards --bin shards -- api_run::`: with the network decided as `plan` decided it (a bridge only
where something is kept), 15 passed and that test failed, refused "cannot run without a
network: the image's Agentfile grants its agents what lies past the microVM, and --network
none gives the microVM none"; as built, `api_run::` and `agentfile::` 24 passed. Clippy for
shards and shards-api, all targets, `-D warnings`: clean. Real VMs, committed unrun:
`api_image::a_run_keeping_nothing_the_image_grants_boots_and_its_harness_runs` (the Hex
lead's).

**Run on real VMs** (PM M605, 2026-11-15, `SHARDS_REQUIRE_VMS=1`).
`a_run_keeping_nothing_the_image_grants_boots_and_its_harness_runs` passed on HVF and on KVM
x86-64, in api_image's whole runs: 33 of 33 at 6a0adfc09 (KVM twice) and 32 of 32 at the vendor
point 4124d8c70.

**Evidence owed** (ROOT, real VMs). `cargo test -p shards --profile test-release --test
api_image a_run_keeping_nothing_the_image_grants_boots_and_its_harness_runs` on WHP and KVM
arm64; Hex's image_real with a box of no grants once Hex vendors this.

**What would falsify it.** A member of such a run reaching anything past the microVM (then a
network process told no policy is not at `DenyAll`), or one killed for its link.

### D251. A lane to a socket of a run's own command: the agent-control endpoint's socket lane, carried over vsock by shards-init's relay (built: the endpoint, its controller and its controller's wake, the VM process's leg and init's; the run host's endpoint is D252's; its three nesting tests passing on HVF and KVM x86-64, PM M605; on WHP and KVM arm64, and its other real-VM runs, owed)

**Why.** Hex's node runs under shards-init as the run's own command, its PID 1 kept (kiln plan
01a1cd8e862e7169a074db3d5fa33f3d, step 39; Hex's `docs/design/node-under-shards-init.md` §5).
Its host reaches the node through four AF_UNIX stream sockets its relay listens on in
`/run/hex/channel`. The workload cannot reach vsock itself: the Docker default filter
shards-init gives a run's command refuses `socket(AF_VSOCK)` (D238). D238 decided that a lane
reaches its microVM over vsock and that shards-init's relay carries it on. This entry is that
lane: OpenSSH's `direct-streamlocal@openssh.com` (PROTOCOL §2.4) in the endpoint's own terms.
Hex's acceptance (its INTERFACE.md and red tests, step11-a-socket-lane) is held to here.

**Decided.**
- *Its grant (default deny).* The run names one directory of its own command's sockets
  (`sockets=<dir>`, `shards_abi::run::socket`): absolute and plain, as a member's working
  directory is. A lane names one file in it: nonempty, no `.`, `..`, `/` or NUL, within
  `NAME_MAX`. A run that names none opens no lane, and only the run's own command's root is
  reached, never a member's. Init reads the grant as the run starts and refuses it in a run
  without a command of its own (`ATTEND`).
- *The endpoint* (`shards_remote::control::unix`). The lane's first frame is `UnixConnect`
  (tag 5): the run, its generation and the name. A name that is no file name is refused
  `Protocol` before the endpoint's host is asked. An endpoint that admits no socket lane, or
  another run, is refused `Scope`, and another generation `Stale`. A lane past the run's
  admitted `lanes` is refused `Capacity` (a new `Reason`, 6), never queued; the lanes its
  controller already reset are let go first. The endpoint hands its host the ask
  (`unix::Connect`). The host answers with the connected socket (`Connected`, tag 40, then the
  socket's bytes raw both ways) or with its connect's errno (`Unreached`, tag 41, then the
  lane's end).
- *Its bytes.* Each way holds at most the admitted `window` in flight: the endpoint reads no
  more of the controller than the socket's writer has room for, and the socket's reader reads
  no more than the controller has taken. A stalled reader holds up its own lane alone (RFC 9000
  §2.2, §4.1). Each way's end is that way's half-close: a FIN, the socket's
  `shutdown(SHUT_WR)`. An abort either way is the other's: RESET_STREAM or STOP_SENDING; the
  socket ended with `shards_ipc::end`, as M236 asks of a Mac. A write that fails resets the
  lane, never ending it in order. The socket's writer and reader run on threads of their own,
  woken into the endpoint's driver as exec's host is; the endpoint's end ends every socket.
- *Its cut* (the Hex lead's Link test, 2026-11-13). A socket cut short resets the lane
  (RESET_STREAM and STOP_SENDING), never its FIN first: its write fails (EPIPE, ECONNRESET),
