  its read fails, or it has hung up as its reads end, its peer gone rather than half-closed.
  A read's end alone does not tell: a peer's close reads as a half-close's end, and the
  writer finds EPIPE only at its next write, after the reader's FIN has gone (macOS 4 of 4;
  on Linux a close that left a byte unread reads ECONNRESET, which resets the lane, and one
  that left none an end, as on macOS, PM M559). So the reader asks the socket at its end
  (`shards_ipc::hung_up`: poll(2)'s POLLHUP or POLLERR asked for POLLOUT, which a peer's
  close sets as it ends the reads, and a half-close never; on Windows the pipe's other end
  closed, PeekNamedPipe's ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE, where a half-close is a message of no bytes).
  The endpoint holds each way's state (`Upward`, `Downward`, R04): hung up while the
  controller's way is open is a cut; hung up while the controller's FIN is being written
  waits for the writer, whose socket shut after all the controller sent (which hangs a Unix
  socket up as well) ends the lane in order, and whose failed write cuts it. A socket that
  cannot say is taken as hung up. Only a half-close, or both ways' ends, close in order. The
  transport's RST drops what the controller had not read (RFC 9000 §3.2; hyper-quic's
  `Recv::reset` clears its buffer): a cut promises no byte before it. No wire change: the
  cut is the stream's reset, `ConnectionReset` at the controller. On Windows a cut WinSock
  socket (AF_UNIX, the VM process's legs) reads WSAECONNRESET (10054), which std reads as
  `ConnectionReset`.
- *Its cut through the guest's legs.* Each leg between the workload and the endpoint carries
  the same rule: hung up at a read's end while the other way is open is a cut, carried on as
  both ways ended at once, never as a half-close first. No wire, tag or constant is added.
  - shards-init's relay (`relay.rs` `pump`, `EndPolicy::Independent`: lanes and MCP
    members) asks the workload's socket at its read's end (POLLHUP or POLLERR asked for
    POLLOUT at once, PM M559). Hung up while the host's way is open (still read, or bytes
    for the workload unwritten), it ends the vsock connection in one `shutdown(SHUT_RDWR)`,
    one SHUTDOWN of RCV and SEND (`virtio_transport_shutdown`), and ends
    (`Termination::ClientCut`). Hung up after the host's way has ended, or not hung up, the
    end is the workload's half-close (SHUT_WR, SHUTDOWN(SEND)), as before. A TCP peer's FIN
    sets no POLLHUP (`tcp_poll`), so testguest's TCP forward keeps its half-close.
  - The VM process's vsock muxer (`vsock/conn.rs`, `HostWrites`: `Open`, `Shut`, `Cut`):
    the guest's SHUTDOWN(RCV) while the host's way is open (no host end-of-stream read) and
    its SEND not ended in an earlier packet is a cut. Its host socket is closed once the
    guest's bytes are flushed, on the guest's RST, with no `shutdown(Write)` first, and on
    Windows held for nothing and closed resetting (`Conn::linger`; SO_LINGER {on, 0},
    `shards_afunix::UnixStream::close_resets`, closesocket's hard close): its peer loses what
    it had not read and reads a reset, as a cut promises no byte before it. A plain close
    resets a WinSock AF_UNIX peer only where the closer held some of its bytes unread (PM
    M358); with none, as where the workload read all its controller sent, the peer reads
    end-of-stream, which `pass` below carries on as a half-close: ROOT's WHP run of the
    nesting cut test at 2731499f7 read 196,618 bytes and then an end in order there. The
    guest's SHUTDOWN(SEND), then its close, is a half-close exactly as before (exec's run
    connection ends so, `shutdown_and_wait`), and M358's hold for it stands.
  - Windows' relay of a guest connection onto its owner's pipe (`warm.rs` `pass`): a read
    that fails (WSAECONNRESET from a cut socket) ends the other side both ways, the owner's
    pipe ended (`shards_ipc::end`, whose reader then finds it hung up: ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE) or
    the guest's socket shut down both ways; a read's end still half-closes it.
- *Amended (2026-11-15, the WHP lane): a guest's own end keeps its bytes the host's.* This
  replaces the relay's one `shutdown(SHUT_RDWR)` and the muxer's reading of RCV and SEND at
  once as a cut, above, and the Windows cut's reset (`close_resets`, now removed).
  - *Why.* Linux's close(2) of a vsock stream sends one SHUTDOWN of RCV and SEND
    (`virtio_transport_close`, net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c, Linux 7.2-rc4
    lines 1281-1282), the same packet the relay's cut sent. So every guest program that
    wrote and closed while its host's way was open was read as a cut, and on Windows its
    host socket was closed resetting: Hex's stamps port, a stream its guest writes and
    closes, reached the host's `read_to_string` as WSAECONNRESET (10054) instead of
    end-of-stream, 3.1 s into a boot on hex-winvm (Hex 414aa30d3 over shards d993d83ee,
    hex-cli `tests/guest_boot_record.rs:90`), and a reset loses its peer every byte it had
    not read (PM M358). On Unix the same close read every byte, then an end.
  - *The wire.* `shutdown(SHUT_RD)` sends a SHUTDOWN of RCV alone (`vsock_shutdown`,
    af_vsock.c lines 1205-1216; `virtio_transport_shutdown`, virtio_transport_common.c
    lines 1071-1083). The relay's cut is now its reads' end, then both ways (`relay.rs`
    `cut`): RCV alone, then RCV and SEND. The muxer reads a SHUTDOWN of RCV without SEND,
    while SEND has not come and the host's way is open, as the cut (`HostWrites::Cut`); RCV
    and SEND in one packet is the guest's writes' end, its host socket shut for writing once
    its bytes are flushed (`HostWrites::Shut`), as SEND alone always was. The contract is
    `shards_abi::run::socket`'s (*Its cut*).
  - *No guest byte lost, on every OS.* Every byte the guest sent before its end, its close
    or its cut, is its host's before any end. On Unix a cut socket still closes with no
    `shutdown(Write)` first, after its bytes are flushed, so its host reads them, then an
    end hung up (PM M559). On Windows a cut ends as an end in order does (`Conn::linger`:
    flushed, `shutdown(SD_SEND)`, held until the host ends its side, PM M358's hold), as no
    WinSock AF_UNIX close keeps the bytes its peer has not read while telling it apart from
    an end in order (M358: a close resets wherever the closer holds any of its peer's bytes
    unread or its peer sends after it). So on Windows a cut reaches the VM process's `pass`
    as end-of-stream, which it carries on as a half-close, and the controller reads `Ok(0)`
    where Unix reads `ConnectionReset`: *What would falsify it*'s "a socket cut short read as
    `Ok(0)`" holds on Unix and not on Windows, an open limit until the measurement below.
  - *No black hole.* After the guest's close or cut a host's write fails at once on Unix
    (its connection gone on the guest's RST, the socket closed: EPIPE). On Windows it does
    not: the held end reads and drops what the host writes until the host ends its side, and
    a send to an AF_UNIX socket already closed succeeds (M358's last row), so no close there
    fails a write without losing the host the guest's bytes it had not read. An open,
    measured platform limit, not a guarantee. Owed: whether WSAPoll's WRNORM, or the send
    buffer's draining (M199), tells the muxer its host has read every byte, so that it could
    reset only then; and, as evidence for the transport's choice alone, whether a Windows
    named pipe closed by its server (CloseHandle, no DisconnectNamedPipe) gives its client
    every byte, then ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE, and fails its client's write at once (ERROR_NO_DATA).
  - *An older shards-init.* One whose relay cuts in one SHUTDOWN of RCV and SEND would now
    be read as ending in order: its host reads every byte, then end-of-stream, never the cut.
    No such init runs against this VMM: its contract text in `shards_abi` changed, so
    `shards_abi::IDENTITY` (crates/abi/build.rs, the FNV-1a of the crate's sources) is
    another, and a saved microVM whose init announced the old one is refused before its guest
    runs (`snapshot::ResumeRefused::OlderInit`, D36); a template is keyed by its init's digest
    (`run.rs`), so none made with the old init is restored; and a fresh boot runs the init
    this `shards` carries.
  - *Literals.* None added. The shutdown flags are virtio's (1.3 §5.10.6.4).
  - *On no clock* (D264): a guest's end holds what its host has not taken past it, within the
    window it had, instead of the 2 s `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` after which it was dropped.
- *The controller* (`control::drive`). `Subscriptions::sockets` and `Dialed::sockets`;
  `Sockets::connect(name)` sends its ask at once and gives a `PendingSocket`, whose
  `wait(patience)` answers `Ok(None)` while it is unanswered, then a `Socket` or a typed
  `Fault`, `Fault::Unreached(errno)` among them (D238's *A lane's ask, waited for within its
  caller's patience*); one let go unanswered is cut as it connects. `Socket` is `Read` and `Write`, with `shutdown_write`, `abort` and `split` (a
  reader and a writer for two threads). `Ok(0)` comes only at the socket's own FIN; a reset
  reads as `ConnectionReset`, its `Fault` its source.
- *Its controller's wake* (Hex's ask D-10). A controller drives all its lanes from one thread
  without waiting on any: `SocketReader::try_read` and `SocketWriter::try_write` (and
  `Socket`'s) say `WouldBlock` where nothing has come or the lane has no room, and otherwise
  answer, end (`Ok(0)` at the socket's FIN) and fault exactly as `read` and `write` do, typed
  through the same `Fault`. The blocking `read` and `write` are unchanged; both styles share one
  state (`ReadState`, `WriteState`), and a call says which it is (`Waits`, R04).
  - *One wake per controller* (`Dialed::wake`, `drive::Wake`), an OS wait's handle: on Unix the
    read end of an AF_UNIX datagram socket pair, readable while a ring is pending (`AsFd`); on
    Windows an auto-reset event (`AsHandle`). The driver rings it once in each of its turns
    (each `Handler` call, and `Controller::run`'s end) in which it told any lane, or any lane's
    ask, anything: bytes, an end, a fault, room, an answer. Each lane marks what it was told;
    the turn's end takes the marks, and a sweep takes those of lanes it lets go first, so a
    lane's last word (a fault, its end) rings though its lane is gone. The driver's end rings
    too (`Ring`'s drop), so a controller sleeping on it finds every lane's end. No interval
    and no poll: the driver's own events are the only rings (R03, R05).
  - *The wake rule.* Level, and drained before the tries: wait (an OS wait, or `Wake::wait`),
    `Wake::drain`, then try every lane until each says `WouldBlock`, and wait again. The
    driver sends a lane's words before it rings, so a ring the drain took told what the tries
    then find, and a ring after the drain stays pending for the next wait: no wake is lost.
    The wake names no lane: its controller tries them all (a controller's lanes are bounded by
    its admission's `lanes`).
  - *Unix: a datagram pair, both ends nonblocking.* A ring with no room in the queue finds one
    pending (Linux's `max_dgram_qlen`), so rings coalesce. A ring whose wake is gone is an
    error, never a signal, where a pipe's or a stream's write to a closed reader raises
    SIGPIPE (pipe(7), unix(7)); and std makes the pair close-on-exec. *Windows: auto-reset*,
    as shards-netring's doorbell is: the one wait it satisfies resets it atomically
    (learn.microsoft.com, "CreateEventW": "the system automatically resets the event state to
    nonsignaled after a single waiting thread has been released"), so the rule leaves its
    controller no reset to order after its wait. A manual-reset event would need a
    `ResetEvent` strictly before the tries, and a reset after them loses the ring. `drain` on
    Windows is a wait of 0.
  - *Alternatives.* A Linux eventfd or a kqueue `EVFILT_USER` (mio's `Waker`, tokio's) is one
    platform's, where the pair is every Unix's (R12). The driver's own UDP waker (`net.rs`) is a
    SOCKET on Windows, which WaitForMultipleObjects cannot wait on. A readiness list naming
    ready lanes would add a second state beside each lane's channel for a controller of a
    handful of lanes; trying each is a `try_recv` per lane.
  - *Literals.* None chosen: poll(2)'s int and WaitForSingleObject's DWORD of milliseconds
    (`INFINITE`) are the APIs' own, a patience past them waiting until a ring, rounded up so no
    patience waits less than asked.
  - *A member's stdio, and an exec's and MCP connection's, on the same wake* (Hex's ask after
    D-10: one thread per output, input and MCP connection otherwise). `Output::try_next_record`
    and `Input::try_write` answer `Ok(None)`, their `WouldBlock`, where no record has come or
    the endpoint has no room, and otherwise exactly as `next_record` and `write` do: a record,
    `Got::Finished`, `Fault::InputEnded`, or the lane's `Fault`, then again. `None` is the
    crate's own "not yet", as a pending ask's `wait(Duration::ZERO)` says it; an `io::Result`
    would carry these handles' typed ends and faults as `io::Error`s (R04). The driver already
    rings for their words (records, finishes, room, faults, through each lane's mark), so the
    one rule drives sockets, outputs, inputs and the pending asks from one thread. Each shares
    its blocking twin's state (`Waits`, as the sockets'): an output's record handed out is
    acknowledged by whichever call comes next. An input's try takes its bytes as one record and
    answers at once, the record in flight (`Flight::Sent`, R04): no room until the endpoint has
    taken it, and the cursor passes it as its taken is heard, by the next try, `write` or `end`.
    `write` itself is unchanged, waiting for its record's taken. An abort with a record in
    flight names the cursor before it, which the endpoint takes (an abort at or before the next
    record's start, `managed::input`). No literal.
- *Its scope.* An endpoint that serves its run's member streams knows its run and
  generation, which an ask names. One that serves sockets alone knows only the keys its
  connection pinned, and an ask there names the zero run and generation 0, as a controller of
  sockets alone sends it.
- *The VM process's leg.* Its owner asks with `LANE_OPEN` (shards_ipc 98: the lane's number
  below 2^63, the name). The VM process asks its guest on the signal connection (run kind
  `SOCKET`, 52: a fresh token, the lane's id and the name). The guest's connection to the exec
  port, whose HELLO names that token, is the lane: it is matched in the exec port's registry as
  an exec's is (`Target::Socket`), then the lane's status is read (an errno; 0 connected). On
  Unix the connection is handed to the owner beside the answer, held until `LANE_HELD` (99)
  says the owner has it (M24). On Windows, where a VM hands its owner no handle, it is relayed
  onto the socket the owner's `LANE_HELD` gives, as `MANAGED_INPUT` is. What init refuses
  before connecting anything comes back as `SOCKET_REFUSED` (53: id, errno), as `EXEC_FAILED`
  does.
- *shards-init's leg* (`crates/init/src/lanes.rs`). Each ask runs on a thread of its own, so a
  connect is nonblocking: a full Unix listen backlog returns Linux's EAGAIN, carried as
  `Unreached`, instead of retaining a worker after its controller abandons the ask
  (control-02, [red/green record](../research/measurements/control-fixes-v1/README.md)).
  connect(2)'s AF_UNIX rule supplies this refusal; no retry or deadline is chosen.
  The thread resolves the path inside
  the command's root (`/proc/PID/root` opened `O_PATH`, then openat2 `RESOLVE_IN_ROOT |
  RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS`, `crate::inroot`), so no link the command planted leads elsewhere. It
  connects through the descriptor (`/proc/self/fd/N`), so the path is not resolved again and
  `sun_path` bounds nothing. Then it dials the exec port, says its HELLO and status, and pumps
  with relay.rs's pump, each way ended independently. Init's own refusals are errnos: EACCES
  (no grant), EINVAL (no file name), ENAMETOOLONG (past `sun_path`, where nothing could be
  bound), ESRCH (the command not running).
- *The lanes of D254.* kiln's MCP lane (goal 58) reuses this relay in the other direction: a
  listener init makes in the asking member's view, each accepted connection carried out the
  same way, its number at or above 2^63 (`LANE_ACCEPTED`, 100, reserved).

**Alternatives, and why not.**
- *Host-initiated vsock* (`CONNECT <port>`, Firecracker's form, D238's wording): it needs a
  host socket file per VM for the muxer to take clients on. Warm and orchestrated VMs have
  none, and shards' interfaces are files the home holds (the filesystem rule). The guest's dial
  to the exec port, token-gated, carries the same bytes through the same muxer, with the
  registry, hand-off and Windows relay execs already use.
- *An exec lane per connection* (D238's design (B)): a guest process for each of Hex's
  connections, three per call in flight (Hex's §5).
- *A published port into the workload*: the network path D238 declined for control.

**Literals.** None chosen. `NAME_MAX` (255) and `PATH_MAX` (include/uapi/linux/limits.h);
`sun_path`'s 108 bytes (unix(7)); TLS 1.3's largest handshake message, a uint24 and its
four-byte head (RFC 8446 §4), with D180's datagrams for a link of socket lanes alone, as the
daemon's endpoints take them, its liveness judged at use (D180; `tls::QUIET` before). The asks' bounds are the frame's
own: its head, the run (32), the generation (8) and the name. Linux's errnos are
asm-generic's, which every guest architecture shares. The window, the lanes and so every
buffer are the caller's admission (R03). The cut's probe waits for nothing (poll(2)'s
timeout 0): it reads the socket's state as its reads end, which a peer's close has set by
then (Linux's `unix_release_sock` sets the peer's `sk_shutdown` to SHUTDOWN_MASK before it
wakes it, net/unix/af_unix.c; macOS as measured, PM M559). A cut's close on Windows lingers
{on, 0}: WinSock's own value for a hard close (LINGER, learn.microsoft.com "closesocket
function"), no time chosen.

### D252. An orchestrator's run binds its own agent-control endpoint, and shards-api carries Shards' controller (built, its members' stdio lanes too; its two nesting tests passing on HVF and KVM x86-64, PM M605; on WHP and KVM arm64, the stdio lanes' run and its other real-VM runs owed)

**Why.** D238 built the endpoint for a daemon's run that asks for it (`shards.control=true`,
`bind_agent`), but D231's run host (`shards api-run`) bound none. Hex's node runs on such a run
(Hex's `node-under-shards-init.md` §5): its host reaches the node only through the run's
endpoint, over the socket lane (D251). Hex vendors shards-api, and D238 has a controller's side
be Shards' own code. Hex's acceptance (step11-b-run-host-endpoint) is held to here.

**Decided.**
- *The ask.* `ImageSpec::control: Option<ControlAsk>` holds the controller's key's SHA-256 (D180's
  raw public key, RFC 7250), the one key the endpoint takes. It also holds an optional
  `SocketGrant` (D251): the directory, the lanes and the window, the caller's numbers (R03).
  shards-api refuses a grant whose directory is not absolute and plain, one of 0 lanes or 0
  bytes, or one in a run without a command of its own, as a `Spec`, before a run host starts.
  The run host refuses it again, and so does init. The image channel carries the ask in its
  version 15 (`Request::control`), so a host of an earlier version refuses the run as it is
  asked, and guesses no endpoint.
- *The endpoint.* The run host binds it once its VM has started. The microVM's key is made
  then and held by the endpoint alone: never in guest memory, never a template's (D238), and
  two runs never share one. It binds on loopback, as step 5's endpoints do, and serves the
  run's socket lanes. Each lane goes to its VM as `LANE_OPEN` and is answered in the run host's
  follow of its link. The connection is taken (`LANE_HELD`) and handed to the endpoint
  (`Reply::Connected`), or the guest's errno is (`Reply::Unreached`). The endpoint is revoked as
  the run's asks end, and every lane with it. A lane its VM can no longer answer is refused
  ESRCH, as its command is.
- *What the orchestrator reads.* `ImageGuest::control()` gives a `ControlAt`: where the endpoint
  is bound and the microVM key's SHA-256, which the controller pins. It is told in `Started`,
  version 15. shards-api holds the run host to it: an endpoint told where none was asked, or
  none where one was, breaks the channel's contract (`Host`).
- *The controller in shards-api* (`shards_api::control`). It re-exports Shards' own:
  `Controller`, `Dialed`, `Ended`, `Fault`, `Hangup`, `Link`, `Linked`, `Socket`,
  `SocketAdmission`, `SocketReader`, `SocketWriter`, `Sockets`, `Subscriptions`, `Identity`,
  `Fingerprint` and `Reason`. shards-api now depends on shards-remote.

**Differences from Hex's interface, said.**
- `Fault::Lost(Ended)` is the connection's end where Hex proposed `Fault::Ended`. A socket's reset
  reads as `ConnectionReset`, with `Fault::Revoked` its source (Hex's `Fault::Reset`).
- The suite and the end are read through `Dialed::link` (`Linked::wait`'s `Link`: each end's
  `Negotiated`) and through a lane's `Fault::Lost`, where Hex proposed `Dialed::suite()` and
  `ended()`.
- Inside the microVM, the lane's connection is the guest's dial to the exec port, by the lane's
  own token (D251), where Hex proposed a host-initiated `CONNECT 1031`.
- An endpoint serving nothing is refused (`Capacity`), as shards-remote's endpoints are (D238), so
  Hex's case (g) grants a socket directory. Binding an endpoint of the control lane alone is goal
  58's to decide.
- A revoked endpoint's connections close with code 0, which a controller reads as
  `Transport(Peer)`: typed, never `Silent`. (g) asks never `Silent`, as (f) does.

**Amended** (goal 58). The run host's endpoint admits execs too, as the daemon's runs do
(`shards_api::control::exec_admissions`), so that it hosts its members' MCP connections (D254) through the
daemon's exec host, and hosts its execs and its members' own lanes (D238) through the daemon's
hosts too. Its asks name the zero run and generation 0, as its socket lanes do, its
endpoint serving no member stream (D238); where its control asks for its members' stdio, its
streams are the zero run's too (amended 2026-11-16, below).

**Amended** (Hex's ask, 2026-11-14): every socket the endpoint holds, named; image channel
version 30.
- *Why.* The endpoint's hyper-quic driver holds two more loopback UDP sockets beside the one it
  serves on: its waker and its wake, connected to each other since b6727996c
  (`shards_remote::net::Driver::bind_with_limits`). Windows' UDP table (`GetExtendedUdpTable`,
  `Get-NetUDPEndpoint`) shows no UDP socket's peer, so from outside the process they look like
  listeners nobody granted, and Hex's default-deny check of a run's sockets fails there.
- *Decided.* The endpoint tells all three: `control::Endpoint::{address, waker, wake}`, from
  `Driver::local`, `Sender::waker_addr` and `Driver::wake_addr`, each its socket's own
  `local_addr` (a sender's clones duplicate the one waker descriptor, so its address is theirs
  too). `ControlAt` carries them, typed and named: `address` (served), `waker`, `wake`, and
  `ControlAt::sockets()`, all three, so Hex can require that every UDP socket a run holds is
  exactly one of them. `Started` encodes the two after the microVM key's SHA-256, each an
  address and a port, inside the control block, so a run without an endpoint encodes as before.
  The same on every OS: the driver binds both on every one.
- *Version 30.* A version-29 reader would read the two addresses as the rate period, so the
  channel's version moves, and a side of version 29 refuses the run by its version as it is
  asked, never reading a `Started` laid out otherwise.
- *Tested* (unit): `net::a_driver_tells_every_socket_it_holds` (the three named addresses
  equal what the sockets report, the waker and wake connected to each other, all three held
  while the driver lives and free after); `image::wire`'s round-trip of all three, IPv4 and
  IPv6, and a version-29 request refused; api_run's `control_at` from a bound endpoint equals
  what its sockets hold.
- *Owed* (ROOT): Hex's Windows check over a real run's UDP table (WHP).

**Literals.** None new. The window and lanes are the caller's (R03). Loopback is where step 5's
endpoints bind.

**Built and tested** (unit, focused).
- shards-api, `image::wire`: the control ask crosses the channel whole at version 15, absent
  where not asked; `Started` tells where an endpoint is, IPv4 and IPv6, or none.
- shards-api, `image::tests`: a grant outside its bounds is refused before a run host starts,
  as Hex's red test asks; a grant within them is carried whole; a grant without a command is
  refused.
- shards (api_run): the run host holds the grant as shards-api does; its endpoint binds on
  loopback under a key of its own per run.

**Evidence owed** (ROOT, real VMs).
- Hex's cases (f) `nesting::a_nested_workloads_sockets_are_lanes_of_its_orchestrators_controller`
  and (g) `nesting::an_orchestrators_run_binds_its_own_agent_control_endpoint`, on WHP and KVM
  arm64. Both passed on HVF and KVM x86_64 (PM M605, 2026-11-15, `SHARDS_REQUIRE_VMS=1`): nesting
  ran whole, 14 of 14 on each at the vendor point 4124d8c70 (KVM three runs), and these two passed
  in each of M605's runs of it, whose failures (KVM, with 4e0b82699) were other tests'. M605 ran
  before the members' stdio lanes (amended 2026-11-16, below).
- The run host's resident and CPU cost with its endpoint, against the daemon's per run (R14).

**What would falsify it.**
- A run's key reached by another run's controller.
- An endpoint outliving its run.
- A grant shards-api takes and init refuses, or the other way round.

**Amended: a warm host makes its key as it waits** (2026-11-15, the start path's cuts; ROOT's
go). A warm host (D253) has started its VM before its run asks, and serves one run. It makes the
microVM's key then (`api_run.rs` `ControlKey`), after its VM is ready and before its run's
request, so a warm run that asks for an endpoint binds with it and makes none on its way. The
endpoint is still bound after the request, as the controller's key and the socket grant are the
run's own, and takes the key as it binds (`bind_control` consumes it). Until then the run host
holds it, never its guest, never a template: what this decision asks of it still holds, and no
two runs share one, as no two runs share a host. A key that cannot be made while warm is made
again as the endpoint binds, refused there as before; one never asked for goes with its host. A
run host's own runs (not warm) make theirs as their endpoint binds, as before. Tested:
`a_warm_runs_endpoint_takes_the_key_its_host_made_as_it_waited` (its endpoint's fingerprint is
the pre-made key's; two hosts' keys differ; a run with none makes its own). Timed:
`its agent-control key made` as the warm host waits, `its agent-control endpoint bound` on the
run's way. *Owed* (ROOT): a warm run asking for control in the A/B, which the rig's runs do not.

**Amended: its endpoint serves its members' stdio** (2026-11-16, kiln plan step 17's Duplex,
lane s17's finding).
- *Why.* kiln drove an isolated session's signals and MCP over the run's endpoint (D238, D254)
  but its stdio over this channel (`take_input`, `take_output`): the run host's endpoint served
  no member stream, where a daemon's run's serves its owned ones (D238, `bind_agent`). kiln's
  Duplex is a member's stdio over hyper-transport, so the run host serves it there.
- *The ask.* `ControlAsk::stdio`, a flag, asks it: the image channel's version 44 carries it
  after the request's last field, where the request asks for an endpoint, so a host of version
  43 refuses the run by its version as it is asked. Explicit, as every grant is: a run that asks
  none is served as before, and an orchestrator that takes its members' stdio from this
  channel is never raced by a lane for the same bytes. With it, this channel carries none of
  their bytes: shards-api pumps no pipe (`take_output` and `take_input` refused, typed
  `ImageRefusal::Spec`), its orchestrator gives no room, and a `CREDIT`, `INPUT` or `INPUT_END`
  for them breaks the channel's contract; each output's end is still told (`OUTPUT_END`), so
  `wait_channel` reads it typed.
- *What it serves.* Every running member's stdout and stderr and each stdin its spec asks for
  (`MemberSpec::stdin`), as lanes of the run's one connection, step 5's subscriptions and
  frames, with the same services the daemon's runs' lanes have (`managed::Service`,
  `managed::input::Service`): one record in flight each way, cursors resumed, ends and aborts
  typed. Each is named in the zero run, as the endpoint's asks are, by its member's generation
  (D270: 0 its first, each restart's one more), and admitted as an exec's stream of its kind
  (`exec_admissions`): `shards_api::control::member_output` and `member_input` name them, the
  run host binds them by the same functions, and a controller's `Subscriptions` names them with
  its cursors.
- *Its credits.* A member's output is credited to its guest one record at a time, of the room
  its lane's subscriber has (`Producer::wait_capacity`, at most the run protocol's
  `MAX_PAYLOAD`), as the daemon's credit worker credits an owned output (`send_credits`); its
  record goes whole into its lane's own buffer, the guest's capture record, which its
  controller decodes, as a daemon's run's owner does. A record that comes as its subscriber
  leaves waits for the next at the same place; one past its credit revokes the output. Its end
  or abort is the output's last record, its end told as its controller consumes it. A member's
  stdin is relayed by the daemon's relay (`managed::relay_input`, now shared: a connection to
  wait for and one to close) onto the input connection its VM hands over; its init's word on
  its end is its lane's (`input::Control::ended`).
- *Its generations* (D270). The endpoint is bound with each stream's first generation; a
  restart joins its member's next generation's streams before it asks its start
  (`control::Generations`), admitted as the streams they follow, so the connection's windows,
  each its streams' own, hold them (R03), and a restart that fails past joining them revokes
  them. A generation past is let go once its end was told and no lane holds it; a lane to it,
  or to one not started, is refused `Stale`. A controller dialing a next generation's streams
  names that generation in its asks (drive.rs): an ask is in scope at its endpoint's run and at
  any generation whose streams it serves (`Lanes::in_scope`). A channel of a generation past
  that no credit went to is revoked as its restart seals it.
- *Refusals, typed* (R04): a member the run has not, one of files alone, or a stdin its spec
  asks none of, `Scope`; another generation, `Stale`; a stream revoked (its capture cut before
  its end, a sealed channel, a failed restart's), `Closed`. A member that has ended has its
  streams' ends: an output's last records then `Got::Finished`, a stdin's `Fault::InputEnded`.
  Where its control asks for stdio, an exec, member or MCP ask naming a member the endpoint
  serves no stream of is refused `Scope` by the endpoint, as a daemon's run's is, rather than
  `Unstarted::Refused` by its host.
- *What kiln and Hex change to use it.* Hex: ask `ControlAsk { stdio: true, .. }`; dial
  `shards_api::control::Controller` with the member's `member_output` (stdout, stderr) and
  `member_input` scopes at cursor 0, its records decoded as `shards_abi::run::managed::Record`
  (`Event::Data` its bytes); after `restart`, dial its returned generation's anew (the newer
  connection supersedes the older, D238); `take_output` and `take_input` are then refused.
  kiln: re-vendor Shards and Hex; its `HexRun` is unchanged (lane s17).
- *Literals.* None new: the zero run, the run protocol's `MAX_PAYLOAD`, `exec_admissions`'
  bounds, step 5's frames. The channel's version 44 is the next.
- *Tested* (unit, written, not run: the person's rule of 2026-11-16, no builds or tests on
  this lane). `api_run::hosted::tests::an_orchestrators_run_serves_its_members_stdio_on_its_endpoint_by_generation`
  (credits as its lane has room, each record whole, its end; its orchestrator told each
  output's end and none of its bytes; its stdin's record one `STDIN` frame and its end an empty
  one, its init's word its lane's end; member 0 refused `Scope`; a next generation joined and
  served, one not started refused `Stale`); `image::wire`'s round trip of the flag, and one of
  another value refused; `control::tests::an_orchestrated_members_streams_are_named_in_the_zero_run_by_generation`.
- *Owed* (ROOT). The suites of shards-remote (`control::`), shards-api (`image::`, `control::`)
  and `shards` (`api_run::`, `daemon::managed::`), clippy on the seven targets, and a real-VM
  run of a harness's stdio over its lanes, a restart among it, on HVF, KVM and WHP; the stdio
  lanes' cost, its threads and buffers, against the channel's (R14). The run host's budget
  holding its stdio lanes, as the daemon's managed budget holds a run's owned streams: charged
  since (below).

**Amended: its stdio lanes charged to its budget** (2026-11-16, ROOT's decision; lane
orch-stdio-2).
- *Why.* The run host served its members' stdio as lanes (above), but its budget (`Agent::charge`,
  D238's run host) counted none of their buffers, where the daemon's managed budget counts every
  stream a run's endpoint serves (D180's ledger,
  [admission](../research/measurements/managed-output/admission.md)). ROOT's decision: count
  them, as the daemon does, with its code and its bound.
- *What each stream is charged.* The daemon's own account, now one function of each kind in
  daemon/managed.rs, which the daemon's reservation and the run host both call (R12). An output,
  `output_bytes`: its record twice (its VM process's capture worker's and its host's), what its
  endpoint sends of it unacknowledged and its control frame, each as its admission says, and its
  host's record of it; then `storage_excess`, what its record's allocation holds past that, once
  it is made. A stdin, `input_bytes`: its record, its taken frames, what its endpoint holds of its
  owner's stream (a record's head, the record and an end) and its host's record of it. The TLS
  handshake and datagrams of the connection it rides are its endpoint's, charged once per
  connection (the amendment below; this one charged them per stream). Its
  admission is what its endpoint admits it (`member_output`, `member_input`: `exec_admissions`);
  its host's record is its entry in the run host's map of them, as the daemon's is its `Output`
  or `Input`. Each is held by the daemon's guard (`execs::Held`, now generic over how it holds
  the budget: a borrow, or a share where it outlives one), against the daemon's bound: the
  host's available memory (`Charge::grow`).
- *When.* As each stream is made: its first generation's as its endpoint binds, before its
  members start (since the amendment "a first generation charged before its members start",
  below; before it, as its run host started serving them, its members already running), and
  before its endpoint's driver serves a lane, so that no lane reaches one its budget has no room
  for before it is let go; each next generation's as its restart joins it (D270). Held while its
  stream is; a past generation's streams that are over (an output finished or let go, a stdin
  ended or let go: none of their buffers held) give theirs back as their member's next generation
  joins, and the rest go at the run's end. Never less than what is held: a stream not yet over
  keeps its charge, as the daemon's ledger is conservative.
- *No room, refused typed* (R04). A stream its budget has no room for is let go before any lane
  reaches it (shards-remote: `managed::Control::no_room` and `input::Control::no_room`, explicit
  states `Ending::NoRoom` and `Slot::NoRoom`, observed as let go), its record or its buffer with
  it, and each lane to it is refused `Capacity`: D251's reason, close code 6, which a controller
  reads as `Fault::Refused(Reason::Capacity)`, never queued. Revoked after (its run's end, a
  sealed or failed generation), a lane to it is refused `Closed`, as any revoked stream's. Its
  guest is credited none of that output; its stdin's relay finds it gone and ends its member's
  input connection, so its member reads its end. The run, its other streams and their lanes go
  on. The daemon refuses its run whole where its streams have no room (`Admission::Insufficient`
  as it starts); a run host's streams come and go with its members' generations: a first
  generation's were refused each alone here, and are now refused whole with their run before its
  members start, and a restart's next generation whole before it starts (the amendments below).
  This amendment changed no wire: the image channel stayed at version 44.
- *Literals.* None new (R03): the daemon's bound and derivation apply.
- *Not counted* (owed to ROOT, R14). The run host's capture reader reads each record into a
  buffer of its own and copies it into its lane's: a third record while one is in flight, where
  the daemon reads into its lane's own, so its account has two. Each stream's thread, where the
  daemon serves its streams on one credit worker. And its endpoint's own socket queues, which
  the daemon charges a run's endpoint (`kernel_buffer_bytes`) and the run host's endpoint holds
  with or without stdio, uncharged before this amendment too (charged since, below).
- *Counted past what is held* (resolved by the amendment below). Each stream was charged a TLS
  handshake's crypto (RFC 8446's bound, 16 MiB) and a datagram each way, as each of step 5's
  endpoints of one stream had a connection of its own, where an agent-control endpoint's streams
  share its connection, whose transport admits the most any stream does
  (`control::Endpoint::bind`), not their sum.
- *Tested* (unit, written, not run: the person's rule of 2026-11-16).
  `daemon::managed::terminal_tests::a_streams_charge_is_what_its_admission_holds_and_its_hosts_record`
  (each account's parts, and none past a u64); shards-remote
  `control::tests::a_stream_its_host_has_no_room_for_refuses_its_lanes_capacity` (an output's
  and a stdin's lanes refused `Capacity`, the other lanes served, `Closed` once revoked);
  `api_run::hosted::tests::an_orchestrators_stdio_lanes_are_charged_to_its_budget_or_refused_capacity`
  (a first generation served with its budget full refused `Capacity` and charged nothing, its
  member's stdin reading its end; each next generation charged exactly the daemon's bytes for
  its two outputs; a past generation given back as the next joins; the budget whole after the
  run).
- *Owed* (ROOT): those suites (`cargo test --profile test-release -p shards-remote --lib --
  control:: managed::`; `cargo test --profile test-release -p shards --lib -- daemon::managed::
  api_run::`), clippy on the seven targets;
  a real-VM run of a harness's stdio under a budget with no room (its lanes refused `Capacity`)
  and with room (charged, and given back across a restart), on HVF, KVM and WHP.

**Amended: a link charged once per connection, a restart with no room refused** (2026-11-16,
ROOT's two decisions; lane lane-charge).
- *Why.* The account above charged every stream a TLS handshake's crypto, 16,777,219 bytes, and
  a datagram each way, 65,527 bytes each, as each of step 5's endpoints of one stream was a
  connection of its own. An agent-control endpoint's lanes share its connection, whose transport
  admits the largest handshake and datagram any of its streams admits, not their sum
  (`control::Endpoint::bind`). So N lanes reserved N × 16,908,273 bytes of link, where their
  endpoint holds two connections' at most, and a small host could refuse lanes it had room for.
  And a restart whose
  next generation had no room still started it: that generation's lanes were refused `Capacity`,
  none credited its output, and its member blocked once its pipe filled.
- *Decided (ROOT).*
  1. A handshake is charged once per connection, as the connection's place is made: as its
     endpoint binds, before its driver makes any connection. Each lane is charged its own buffers
     alone. The basis is unchanged: D180's and D238's ceiling, RFC 8446 §4's largest handshake
     message, now charged per connection (R03: no new number). The daemon's runs and the run
     host are charged alike, by the same functions (R12).
  2. A restart whose next generation's lanes cannot be charged is refused, typed `Capacity`,
     before that generation starts.
- *A link's charge* (`link_bytes`, daemon/managed.rs). It has two parts, each as the endpoint's
  link admits it (`control::Endpoint::link`: the most its streams admitted, or the cited link
  where it serves no stream):
  - a handshake's crypto for each connection the endpoint holds at once;
  - a datagram each way: its driver's send queue (`DriverLimits::queued_datagram_bytes`) and its
    receive buffer, one of each per driver, not per lane.

  The connections an endpoint holds at once:
  - an agent-control endpoint: `control::CONNECTIONS`, two (D238: the one it serves, and the one
    that replaces it, each with its own TLS state while both are open). Now public.
  - an endpoint of one stream: `managed::CONNECTIONS`, one (`max_incoming(1)`). Now named where
    its driver's limits use it.

  A lane, `output_bytes` or `input_bytes`, is charged its records, its window, its control frame
  and its host's record of it, nothing of its link. On one agent-control endpoint, N lanes cost
  N lane charges and one link: 2 × 16,777,219 + 2 × 65,527 = 33,685,492 bytes. Under the account
  above, the same N lanes cost N × 16,908,273 bytes on top of their lane charges.
- *Where it is charged.*
  - The daemon, as its run starts: each stream's own buffers in its reservation; its agent-control
    endpoint's link with its kernel queues as `bind_agent` returns; each of step 5's endpoints'
    link with its kernel queues as it binds, one connection each. A stream the daemon drains
    itself has no endpoint, and is charged no link.
  - The run host: its endpoint's link as `bind_control` returns, before its driver runs
    (`charge_link`), held while the run is served. With no room, the run does not start: its
    endpoint could not be made (`Cause::Boot`; `Cause::Capacity`, and before its members start,
    since the amendment below), as with any endpoint that could not be bound.
    The link is charged whatever its endpoint serves: socket lanes, execs, MCP connections and
    stdio alike. Before this, the run host charged no link unless it served stdio.
- *A restart with no room* (R04). `Stdio::join` charges each of the next generation's streams as
  it makes them. A stream with no room is let go (`no_room`, its lanes refused `Capacity`), and
  the join is refused `RestartRefusal::Capacity` before `MEMBER_START` is sent, so the generation
  never starts. Every stream of that generation is made first, so all its lanes answer alike.
  The restart's refusal then runs as any refused restart's does:
  - its hold is let go, so the end its last generation had ends its member whole;
  - the next generation's streams are revoked (`abort_generation`), and what any of them held of
    the budget is given back at once, as their buffers go with them.

  The image channel's version 48 appends the refusal (tag 7), so a side that reads none refuses
  the run as it is asked. shards-api surfaces it as
  `ImageRefusal::Restart(RestartRefusal::Capacity, _)`. A swap that restarts its member now
  (`SwapWhen::Now`) maps it to `SwapRefusal::Failed`, with its words, as it maps every restart
  refusal but `Running`. A first generation's streams were made while its members already ran, so
  each kept the per-stream refusal above (charged before its members start since, below).
- *Literals.* None new (R03): RFC 8446 §4's bound (D180, D238); D238's `CONNECTIONS`; one
  connection for an endpoint of one stream; D180's datagram. The refusal's tag is the next free
  one.
- *Tested* (unit, written, not run: the person's rule of 2026-11-16).
  - `daemon::managed::terminal_tests::a_streams_charge_is_what_its_admission_holds_and_its_hosts_record`:
    each lane's charge has none of its link, and a larger handshake or datagram charges a lane no
    more; a link's charge is one handshake per connection and a datagram each way; none past a
    u64.
  - shards-remote `control::tests::lanes::its_windows_are_its_streams_own_summed`: an endpoint
    tells the link it was bound with, the cited one where it serves no stream, the most its
    streams admitted otherwise.
  - `api_run::hosted::tests::an_orchestrators_endpoint_is_charged_its_link_once_whatever_lanes_it_carries`:
    the same charge with three member streams or none, given back whole.
  - `api_run::hosted::tests::a_restart_whose_next_generation_has_no_room_is_refused_capacity_before_it_starts`:
    the restart refused `Capacity`; its VM asked to hold the member, then to let it go, and never
    asked to start its next generation; the first generation's charge given back as the next
    joined; the next generation's never held; the budget whole after the run.
  - shards-api `image::wire::tests::a_restart_round_trips_and_its_malformed_answers_are_refused`:
    `Capacity` round-trips, and tag 8 is refused.
- *Not counted* (owed to ROOT, R14), as the amendment above left it: the run host's endpoint's
  socket queues, which the daemon charges with its link (`kernel_buffer_bytes`). Charged since
  (below).
- *Owed* (ROOT).
  - The suites: `cargo test --profile test-release -p shards-remote --lib -- control:: managed::`,
    `cargo test --profile test-release -p shards-api --lib -- image::wire::`, and
    `cargo test --profile test-release -p shards --lib -- daemon::managed:: api_run::`.
  - Clippy on the seven targets.
  - A real-VM restart of a harness whose next generation has no room (refused `Capacity`, its
    member ended, nothing of its next generation started), and a daemon's agent-control run's
    budget with several owned streams (one link), on HVF, KVM and WHP.

**Amended: a first generation charged before its members start, and the endpoint's sockets'
queues charged** (2026-11-16, ROOT's decisions 1 and 2; lane charge-2).
- *Why.*
  1. The run host made and charged its members' first stdio streams as it started serving them,
     after `hand_over` had handed its VM the run, so its members were already running. A stream
     its budget had no room for was let go alone (`no_room`), and its member blocked once its
     pipe filled, as a restart's next generation did before the amendment above.
  2. The run host's endpoint's socket queues were charged nowhere, where the daemon charges its
     runs' endpoints' (`kernel_buffer_bytes`). And the daemon counted its endpoint's waker only
     through its first owned output's control, so an endpoint serving no owned output went
     without it.
- *Decided (ROOT).*
  1. A first generation's lanes are charged before its members start, as a restart's are. With
     no room, the run is refused, typed, before its members start.
  2. The endpoint's socket queues are charged with the shared lane accounting, from the
     sockets' own buffer sizes as the OS reports them (R03: no chosen number), once per
     endpoint.
- *The run host's start* (`serve_launched`), in its order:
  1. Its endpoint is bound, as before past its VM's start (its key's rule is unchanged).
  2. Its link and its sockets' queues are charged (`charge_link`, through `endpoint_bytes`).
  3. Each first-generation stream is charged (`charge_first`), by the functions `Stdio::join`
     charges a next generation with (`output_charge`, `input_charge`).
  4. Only then does `hand_over` hand its VM the run, which starts its members.

  A run its budget has no room for is refused `Cause::Capacity` at 2 or 3, its VM never handed
  the run, so none of its members starts. What it held is given back as it is refused, and its
  VM ended as any refused run's is (`end`). Its endpoint's driver still starts only as the run
  is served, after `STARTED`. A first generation's stream is now charged or its run refused:
  `Stdio::output` and `input` let a stream with no room go (`no_room`) only for a restart's next
  generation, which `join` refuses whole.
- *The sockets' queues* (`control::Endpoint::kernel_buffer_bytes`, shards-remote). Each socket
  the endpoint holds, its send and receive buffers as `getsockopt(SO_SNDBUF)` and
  `getsockopt(SO_RCVBUF)` report them (net.rs `socket_buffers`):
  - its served socket and its wake, its driver's, as before;
  - its waker, which its `Revoke` and every stream's control share: read as it is bound, and
    now counted whatever streams it serves.

  `endpoint_bytes` (daemon/managed.rs) is the endpoint's whole charge, its link (`link_bytes`)
  and its queues, once per endpoint (R12). Both the daemon's agent-control endpoint and the run
  host's are charged by it. The daemon no longer adds its first owned output's waker beside it,
  which would count the one waker twice.
- *Typed* (R04).
  - `Cause::Capacity` (tag 7), the image channel's version 51, so that a side that reads no such
    cause refuses the run as it is asked. shards-api surfaces it as `ImageRefusal::Capacity`,
    in the run host's words.
  - The link's no room, refused `Cause::Boot` by the amendment above, is `Capacity` now: the
    same budget, at the same step of the start. A queue that could not be read, or a charge
    that overflows, stays `Boot`: its endpoint could not be made.
- *Literals.* None new (R03): the buffers the OS reports, the amendment above's link, the next
  free tag and version.
- *Tested* (unit, written, not run: the person's rule of 2026-11-16).
  - shards-remote `control::tests::lanes::its_windows_are_its_streams_own_summed`: an endpoint's
    queues are its driver's and its waker's, the one its streams' controls share; an endpoint of
    no stream counts its waker too.
  - `api_run::hosted::tests::an_orchestrators_endpoint_is_charged_its_link_once_whatever_lanes_it_carries`:
    each endpoint charged its link and its own sockets' queues, given back whole.
  - `api_run::hosted::tests::an_orchestrators_stdio_lanes_are_charged_to_its_budget_or_refused_capacity`:
    a first generation charged with its budget full refused, nothing held; streams served with no
    room, as a next generation's may be, let go, their lanes refused `Capacity`, its stdin's relay
    ending its member's input connection.
  - `api_run::hosted::tests::an_orchestrators_run_serves_its_members_stdio_on_its_endpoint_by_generation`
    and `a_restart_whose_next_generation_has_no_room_is_refused_capacity_before_it_starts`: their
    first generations charged by `charge_first` before they are served.
  - shards-api `image::wire::tests::messages_round_trip`: `Capacity` round-trips, and tag 8 is
    refused. `image::session::tests::refusals_come_typed_in_their_hosts_words`: `Capacity` read
    as `ImageRefusal::Capacity`.
- *Owed* (ROOT).
  - The suites: `cargo test --profile test-release -p shards-remote --lib -- control::`,
    `cargo test --profile test-release -p shards-api --lib -- image::`, and
    `cargo test --profile test-release -p shards --lib -- daemon::managed:: api_run::`.
  - Clippy on the seven targets.
  - Real VM, on HVF, KVM and WHP: a run with stdio lanes whose budget has no room for its first
    generation, refused `Capacity`, its VM never handed the run (no member output, no
    `STARTED`); and a daemon's agent-control run, its endpoint's waker charged once. Both
    written since (the amendment below).

**Amended: the host's available memory told, and the charges' two real-VM tests written**
(2026-11-16, ROOT's decision; lane charge-seam).
- *Why.* The two real-VM tests the amendment above owes could not be written (lane
  phase6-v). Both charges are held to the host's available memory, which no test can set, and
  a host with room shows no charge's size. ROOT's decision: a test seam on D188's told channel
  (R12), read by the same reader in the daemon and in the run host; and a charge made
  observable only where a test cannot otherwise see that it is charged once.
- *The seam* (D188's amendment of this date). A told line `available BYTES` sets what
  `Charge::grow` measures against (`pressure::available`): the told bytes where a line has
  told some, else the kernel's count.
  - The daemon hears the line on its watcher while a microVM runs, and logs it.
  - A run host reads the first line of what its `SHARDS_PRESSURE` names before its run is
    made.

  No wire changed: the image channel stays at version 51.
- *Nothing new made observable.* Each refusal already says what its charge asked:
  - the daemon's, typed `Admission::Insufficient { requested, available }`, which its client
    is told as `managed output admission: N bytes requested, M available`;
  - the run host's link's, typed `Cause::Capacity`, which names the link's bytes.

  A test that tells a size reads what the refused step asked, so no field was added.
- *The tests* (written, not run: the person's rule of 2026-11-16).
  1. api_image.rs
     `a_run_with_no_room_for_its_first_lanes_is_refused_capacity_before_its_members_start`: an
     image whose harness sleeps, its stdio as its endpoint's lanes (`ControlAsk::stdio`), its
     run host told through a file.
     - Told 0: refused `ImageRefusal::Capacity` at its link, which names the link's bytes, L.
     - Told L, room for its link alone: refused `Capacity` at its harness's first lane
       (`member N's first Stdout lane`), by `charge_first` before `hand_over`, so its VM is
       never handed the run and none of its members starts.
     - Told `u64::MAX`: it starts.
  2. managed_output
     `endpoint_charge::a_daemon_runs_agent_control_endpoint_is_charged_its_waker_once_whatever_it_owns`:
     log_lanes's image of agents `a` and `b` (its `Home`, now shared and given a told pipe),
     with a plain microVM kept running so that the daemon's watcher listens.
     - Told 0: a run asking `shards.control=true` and owning `a`'s output is refused at its
       reservation, which says its bytes, R.
     - Told R: that run, and one owning no output, are each refused at their endpoint with
       nothing left, and each says the same charge. It is the link (`HANDSHAKE_BYTES` ×
       `control::CONNECTIONS`, and a datagram each way) and the kernel queues of three
       sockets. The test reads those queues from an endpoint of one stream it binds itself
       (step 5's: its driver's served socket and wake, and its control's waker, all bound on
       loopback by the same `net::Driver::bind_bounded`).
     - A waker charged twice where an output is owned, or not at all where none is (as before
       lane charge-2), makes one of the two charges differ by one socket's queues.
     - Told `u64::MAX`: the run starts.
- *Literals* (R03). Every number the tests use is D252's own or read on the host:
  - RFC 8446 §4's largest handshake message (`HANDSHAKE_BYTES`, 16,777,219), D238's two
    connections (`control::CONNECTIONS`) and D180's datagram (`DATAGRAM_BYTES`, 65,527), one
    each way (`link_bytes`);
  - the sockets' queues, as the OS where the test runs reports them (`getsockopt`);
  - every other size is what a refusal said;
  - 0 is no room at all, and `u64::MAX` the most a told word can say, room for any charge.
- *On Windows.* The daemon's told pipe is a named pipe (`common::Told`). The run host's told
  word is a file, read the same way on every OS.
- *Owed* (ROOT), on HVF (macOS arm64), KVM (Linux amd64) and WHP (Windows), with
  `SHARDS_REQUIRE_VMS=1`:
  - `cargo test --profile test-release -p shards --bin shards -- pressure:: daemon::managed:: api_run::`
  - `cargo test --profile test-release -p shards --test api_image -- --exact
    a_run_with_no_room_for_its_first_lanes_is_refused_capacity_before_its_members_start`
  - `cargo test --profile test-release -p shards --test managed_output -- --exact
    endpoint_charge::a_daemon_runs_agent_control_endpoint_is_charged_its_waker_once_whatever_it_owns`
  - `cargo test --profile test-release -p shards --test managed_output log_lanes` (its `Home`
    changed)
  - `scripts/lint` (the seven targets).

### D253. An orchestrator's run restores its image's template and takes a warm VM from its pool, as the daemon's runs do (built: templates and pools; their real-VM tests passing on HVF and KVM x86-64, PM M605; the 2026-11-16 writable-layer amendment kept on its A/Bs on HVF at p50, p90 and p99, PM M593; on WHP and KVM arm64, a daemon run and restore on each OS, and that amendment's mutation, real-VM tests and A/B on KVM owed)

**Why.** An orchestrator's run (D231) booted its microVM cold every time, where a daemon's run
restores its image's template (D25) and takes a warm VM from its pool (D26). Hex boots its node
through it (Hex step 39), so every one of Hex's starts paid a boot.

**Decided.**
- *One shape.* Every microVM a run boots has one shape beside its guest, the daemon's and a run
  host's alike, so that a template's name (`run::template`) means one machine whichever
  process saved it:
  - `run::Shape::give` is the daemon's composition, moved out of `warm_for`: size, CPU
    baseline, memory to plug and its swap window, reporting, the in-VM server's and the
    emulator's devices, shares and their DAX windows, PCI slots, bridge;
  - `run::boot_args` is `cold`'s words;
  - `run::restore_args` (with `run::Backings`) is `plan_refill`'s;
  - `run::gpu_guest` is the GPU's guest, with the GPU kernel (D144);
  - the share window's setting is `daemon::share_window_mib`, out of `settings`.

  The daemon calls each of them, its words unchanged. The run host calls them too, so its
  microVM now has what a daemon run's has and it had not: a join disk and share, a writable
  layer's file (D190), swap and share windows, memory to plug, the CPU baseline and another
  CPU's emulator (D179). Its own `vm_args` is gone. Its memory to plug is there and none of it
  is plugged: its request asks no most past what it boots with (`RunHead::plug` none), so an
  orchestrator's memory ask stays the run's whole, as before.
- *The GPUs a run names* (D232) are in its template's key where it names any, as its snapshot
  keeps the selection and its restores rejoin it (format 29): a template saved on one
  selection is none of another's. The keys of those that name none are as they were.
  `boot_args` gives each in `--gpu-device`'s grammar after `--gpu`.
- *How a run starts* (`api_run.rs`, `started`), as the daemon's `warm_for` starts one:
  - **Restored**, where its template is saved. Its files are held open as its VM restores it,
    and for the run's life (`snapshot::hold`).
  - **Saved**, where none is. It boots with `--snapshot-dir` at a name of its process's alone;
    once its VM is ready its record is written (`run::Origin`) and the save becomes the
    template, unless another run's got there first (`run::settle`). A save whose VM is never
    ready makes no template, whatever it wrote: it is removed (`run::settle_boot`, the daemon's
    `warm_for` too, which until then settled whatever its `cold` left, ready or not: a VM that
    saved its snapshot and then failed before `READY` became the template, recordless;
    `only_a_ready_boots_save_becomes_the_template`, red first). What is at the template's name
    and is no snapshot (a removal cut short) is removed first, or it would keep every save from
    becoming the template.
  - **Replaced**, where its template does not restore: its VM ends, or says anything else,
    before it is ready, or its template cannot be read. The template is removed with its
    record, and the run boots saving another.
  - A VM that cannot be launched at all is the host's failure. Saving again would not mend
    it, so the template stays and the run fails.
  - **Booted**, where it has no template: a guest its caller gave (as the daemon's runs of one
    have none), or a host whose hypervisor restores no snapshot (`vm::restores_here`, PM
    M345).

  Its orchestrator hears which (`ImageGuest::started_from`, `wire::StartedFrom`, image channel
  version 19). The run's per-run secrets, its agent-control key above all (D252), are made
  after its VM is ready, so no template carries them.
- *The preparation lease ends at readiness* (runs-05). Once launch has completed
  readiness and template settlement, the VM owns its open rootfs and snapshot files
  (D26). A warm host lets go of `Prepared::lease` before WARMED and before awaiting
  CREATE; every served run does so before handoff/STARTED. The lease protects
  preparation, not an idle spare's or workload's life, so unrelated collection can
  acquire the store afterward. Its live collection/progress proof is owed to ROOT;
  unit shaping tests do not prove a running VM's file ownership.
- *One demand rule.* D26's rule for how many warm VMs a pool keeps (the largest burst within an
  RFC 6298 refill window, within the keep-alive) is `shards_api::demand`, moved from the daemon,
  never copied. The daemon's pools keep theirs by it, and an orchestrator's will too.

**Literals.** None of its own. The rule removes a template at one failed restore: a run host
makes one VM, and a wrong removal costs that run's boot alone. The daemon's pools, which
removed one at three failures of any kind (`MAX_FAILURES`, gone), now remove one at its first
failure of its own and at no other (D26 amended, ROOT's ruling of 2026-11-17).

**Tested** (unit, stand-ins, no VM):

- `an_orchestrators_runs_microvm_is_the_daemons_for_the_same_inputs`: the run host's words and

- `how_a_run_started_reads_back_as_its_host_said_it`: the channel.

**Owed** (ROOT, real VMs): `api_image.rs`'s
`an_images_next_run_restores_the_template_its_first_saved` (Saved, Restored, Replaced after its

**Decided: pools** (`shards_api::image::ImagePools`, plan step 5). The orchestrator owns each
microVM's life (D231), so its pools live in its process, with shards-api:
- *A warm run host* is `shards api-run` started with `WARM` (image channel version 21: `WARM`
  14, `WARMED` 32, `Cause::Unfit` 5, `StartedFrom::Warm` 4) and a run's exemplar
  (`wire::Request::exemplar`): the request with its members' stages, its deadline and its
  control ask taken out, so it carries none of a run's secrets. It makes the microVM's part of
  a run (`shape`: the image prepared, the network chosen, the volumes open, the microVM
  composed), restores or saves its template and starts its VM, then says `WARMED`. When its run
  comes (`CREATE`), it makes the run's own part (`plan`: the members' stages, the ports bound,
  the nesting grant, the setup) and serves it as any run, said `Warm` (`StartedFrom::Warm`).
- A run whose exemplar is not the host's is refused `Unfit` (`Cause::Unfit`), and its
  orchestrator's pool gives it a host of its own. The split follows the daemon's warm path:
  what the VM is before its run, what the run is with its `RUN`. Per-run identity, the
  agent-control key (D252), is made after the take.
- *A pool* is the runs of one microVM: one exemplar, one run host program and environment.
  `boot` takes a ready warm host of its run's pool, else starts a host of its own, as
  `ImageShards` does; either way the pool counts the run, and its end as its guest drops.
- *A spare already ended before CREATE* (runs-04) is `Taken::Untaken`: its watcher or
  its process's terminal state proves it never received this run, and the pool starts a
  fresh host. This check is at the take boundary, without periodic probes or another
  lifetime manager. Once CREATE is attempted, a transport failure remains `Refused`:
  there is no proof the run was not received, so it is never replayed. `Unfit` remains
  the host's explicit refusal of a run for another microVM.
- *Its size* is D26's, by the one rule (`shards_api::demand`, moved from the daemon). That is
  the largest burst of its runs within one refill window, an RFC 6298 retransmission timeout
  of its warm hosts' starts as timed from spawn to `WARMED`, at least one while in use, and
  none once idle past the keep-alive. Each host is charged to the orchestrator's room before
  it starts (*Amended: the room*, below); no count of hosts bounds the pools.
- *The keep-alive* is the orchestrator's, `ImagePools::KEEP` D26's cited one (moved to
  `shards_api::demand::KEEP`, the daemon's `DEFAULT_KEEP` too).
- *Cold start:* nothing is warm until a pool's first run, which starts a host of its own while
  its pool starts one ahead. The first window is RFC 6298's initial RTO, as the daemon's
  pools' is.
- *A warm start that fails* is no warm host: its pool starts no more until its next run.
- *The pools' thread* hands out warm hosts, starts more, each start awaited on a thread of its
  own, and ends those past a pool's target or keep-alive. Dropping the pools ends every warm
  host and kills every starting one.

**Tested** (unit, a simulated run host): `a_pools_first_run_starts_its_own_host_and_the_next_takes_a_warm_one`,
`a_warm_host_that_does_not_fit_or_start_leaves_its_run_a_host_of_its_own`,
`a_pool_keeps_its_burst_within_its_room_and_its_owner_ends_them_all`,
`a_pools_warm_hosts_end_past_its_keep_alive`; the channel's warm words
(`a_warm_hosts_exemplar_keeps_all_but_a_runs_own`); the daemon's pools by the moved rule, their
tests unchanged.

**Owed** (ROOT, real VMs): `api_image.rs`'s `an_images_next_run_takes_a_warm_host_of_its_pool`
on HVF, KVM x86_64 and WHP; R14's start of a warm run against a restored one, the warm host's

**Amended: the room** (2026-11-14, with Hex's lead; `ImagePools::new(room, keep)` replaces
`new(most, keep)`, which is deleted with no legacy path). Hex serves image boxes from these
pools, so its node must charge every warm host to the room it admits boxes from, and make
warm hosts yield before it refuses or evicts a real box.
- *Why a count was wrong.* `most` counted hosts. But a host's cost is its microVM's size, and
  sizes differ from pool to pool: two hosts of 8 GiB and two of 512 MiB were the same "2". A
  count also lives apart from the node's admission, so the pools' refill raced the node's own
  starts. The node's room could be taken between its check and the warm host's start, and a
  snapshot of the count was stale as it was read. Now the room is the node's own, and every
  host is claimed of it before it starts.
- *The contract* (`shards_api::image::{WarmRoom, WarmHost, Gave, Released, PoolHeld, PoolId}`):
  - every warm host start (refill, a first run's follow-up, a reserved host put back) first
    calls `WarmRoom::claim` with its spec's memory (bytes) and vCPUs. A refusal starts nothing:
    the pool's target is unmet, and nothing errs;
  - each successful claim is given back exactly once: `Taken` as a run takes the host or a
    box reserves it (its room is the box's; the guest gives nothing as it drops), `Ended` once
    its processes have ended (past its target or keep-alive, released, or with the pools),
    `Failed` where its start fails;
  - the room decides alone. A claim should be refused only where the host does not fit the room
    free now, with no headroom rule: a box wins its room back through `release`.
- *A size left to `shards run`* (`vcpus` or `memory_mib` 0) is resolved before the pool's key
  and its claim, as its run host would give it: every CPU this process may run on, and the
  memory that holds what one vCPU's default may allocate, at most the host's. That is
  `shards_ipc::size::unsized_run`, the very functions `run::sizes_for` sizes with (`host_cpus`,
  `memory_mib`, `overhead_kib`, `MEMORY_MIB`), moved from the `shards` crate into shards-ipc
  so that both call one source. So a default-sized box pools with one that names that size,
  and claims its real room. Its run's request carries the resolved size, which its warm
  host's exemplar check matches. A run that asks its GPU report (D233) is still no pool's.
- *`release(memory)`* ends the coldest hosts until at least `memory` bytes are freed, or none
  is left. Warm hosts go first: those of the pools whose demand target is lowest, then the
  longest idle. Starting hosts go after them. It returns once every one's processes have
  ended, each followed to its end and never timed, as a stopped run's are (D215, D217:
  `Hosts::end`, the watcher's word that the host and its process group have ended). Each
  room is given before it returns, with exact bytes. An end that could not be followed is
  refused typed (`ImageRefusal::Os`), every room given all the same.
- *`reserve(spec)` / `WarmTicket::boot`*: one warm host held for one box, at once, gives
  `Taken` within `reserve`, so the node moves the charge to the box in the same step. A
  second reserve of the same host is impossible, and `release` never ends a reserved host,
  since it is out of its pool. A ticket dropped unused goes back under a claim of its own,
  or ends where that claim is refused, never giving for its first claim again. A ticket
  booted with another pool's spec is refused, typed: `ImageRefusal::OtherPool`. A
  ticketless `Images::boot` still takes a warm host itself, also giving `Taken` once.
- *`held()`* is each pool's claimed room (warm and starting hosts, at their spec's whole size)
  and `footprints`, one reading per warm host whose reading is in. A warm host answers `USE`
  (image channel version 32: `to_host::USE` 40, `to_client::USED` 41) with its VM process's
  use while it waits for its run. That is `process_usage(vm)` (`api_run.rs` `host_use`), the
  one reader a running run's stats use, so the number is theirs. `held()` never waits: each
  warm host's last told footprint is given, and a `USE` is asked for the next unless one is
  unanswered. So a host's first `held()` lists none for it, and a later one lists its
  reading. Any frame other than `CREATE` and `USE` still ends a warm host.
- *No deadlock, by construction.* The pools' thread, their state's one owner, never calls the
  room. Claims, and the `Failed` gives, go in order on a room thread of their own, which
  answers each claim back to the pools. `release`, `reserve`, `held` and a boot's take are
  answered without waiting on it. A `Taken` give, and the refill after it, which is asked
  only once the give has returned so that its claims see the room given back, run on the
  caller's thread. So do `release`'s `Ended` gives. The rule both ways: `claim` and `give`
  must not block on a lock that their owner holds across a call of the pools, dropping them
  included. An atomic room counter meets it. A node that holds its room lock across
  `release` while the room thread waits in `claim` for that lock does not hang: its release
  is answered, and the claim goes on once the lock is let go.
- *Orphans.* A warm host ends with its holder by any death. `api-run`'s `warm` reads its
  orchestrator's channel for `CREATE`, and the channel's end (the holder gone) ends its
  microVM (`Ok(None)` → `end`). A host still starting meets that end as it says `WARMED`.
  It is the same tie as D231's run hosts; no parent-death signal is added.
- *Literals.* None. A pool's demand target takes no count of ours (`UNCOUNTED`, `usize::MAX`:
  no bound but the room's), and its demand's held claims are those of one refill window.
  `PoolId` is the SHA-256 of the pool's key (its run host's program and environment, its
  runs' exemplar), length-prefixed per field: the same while the pool lives.

- `release_ends_the_coldest_first_and_says_what_it_freed`: the lowest target before the

- `a_taken_host_gives_taken_once_and_its_guest_nothing_more`: ticketless and reserved;
- `a_warm_host_that_does_not_fit_or_start_leaves_its_run_a_host_of_its_own`: `Failed`;

- `a_room_waiting_on_its_owners_lock_holds_up_no_answer`: a claim blocked on a mutex the test

- `a_run_asking_its_gpu_report_or_no_size_gets_a_host_of_its_own_and_no_pool`.

**Decided: a run host's layers end with it** (plan step 17, #73). A run host makes its
microVM's writable layer's file in its home's `layers` (D190, layers.rs `fresh`), unlinked as
its handle goes once the microVM is ready or has failed. A host that ends before that, stopped
mid-boot (D231's `BootStop`: its process group killed on Unix, its job on Windows) or failing,
never lets go of it: the file stayed, sparse, up to the run's 10 GiB, its written blocks
counted, until a daemon next started in that home cleared `layers`, and an orchestrator's home
may never run one. Found from source by the boot-stop test's implementer; reproduced by the
stand-in host tests below, red before the change.
- *Considered: no name to outlive its holders.* Unlink as the VM process opens the file, or
  hand it a descriptor of an unlinked file. Rejected for this slice: the VM process takes
  `--layer PATH` and opens it by path (`platform::open_input`, through its grants on macOS and
  Windows), a restore's file is a clone made by name (`for_restore`), and a daemon's run that
  stays needs the name until its microVM has gone, when it renames it into its directory
  (`keep_at`). A descriptor-only layer means a new grant kind on three platforms and a
  `keep_at` that links an open file back to a name (Linux's `linkat` of `/proc/self/fd`, none
  on macOS or Windows): a larger redesign, and the window between `fresh` and the hand-off
  stays either way.
- *Decided: the orchestrator removes them.* Only the process that makes a layer's file names it,
  by its own pid (`shards_ipc::layer_name`, now shared by `fresh` and the sweep;
  `layer_maker` reads it back). The orchestrator's watcher of each host (`session.rs`
  `watch`) waits for the host's end without reaping it (`Child::ended`, waitid `WNOWAIT`), then
  removes every `layers/<hostpid>-*` file (`clear_layers`), then reaps it. Ended, the host
  makes no more; unreaped (on Windows, its handle held by the watcher), its pid is no other
  process's, so no live host of the same pid in the same home can exist and lose its file to
  the sweep. Which home is the host's is found as the host finds it, from the environment it is
  given over the orchestrator's (`shards_ipc::home_in`, `home`'s rule with the lookup passed
  in). A file its microVM still holds as it is killed goes as the one its host let go of at
  readiness does: the name now, the blocks with the microVM.
- *Unchanged:* a run that stays keeps its layer. A kept layer is renamed out of `layers` into
  its run's directory (`keep_at`) or never was in it (`in_place`), and an orchestrator's run host
  keeps none. A host that ends after its run started has let go of its file already, and the
  sweep finds nothing. The daemon's `clear` at start stays for a daemon's own.
- *Literals:* none. Removal failures are not refusals: the watcher has no caller to tell, a
  name left is what the drop leaves on the same failure, and the next daemon clears it.

**Tested** (unit, stand-in hosts, no VM): `a_stop_mid_boot_ends_the_boot_its_host_and_all_its_host_started`

whose hosts now make a layer's file as the real one names it and are stopped mid-boot;
`a_run_host_that_ends_before_its_run_starts_leaves_no_layer` (Unix), whose host makes two
and exits. Each expects the host's gone and another pid's kept. `a_layers_name_says_its_maker`
