**Amended (lane xnet-v, 2026-11-16, ROOT's decisions on slice 6's three questions).**
- *Who gives an ended run's leases back* (accepted as built): its host, as it ends, by their
  drop or the kernel's; the network process holds none (it opens no path, D31). shards-api then
  tells the network's other runs their members without it (`links::host_gone`).
- *A dead run's names put back in a guest* (closed): in the window from a run's VM's end to its
  host's, another change's `Rejoin`, reading the leases, told the dead run's names to the
  other runs' guests again; its host now withdraws them first as its VM ends (*States*, *A run's
  names*: `api_run`'s `Names`, `withdraw_names` at the head of `follow`'s end), no change refused
  meanwhile but one of its own run's. Test (light): `api_run::hosted::tests::
  a_runs_names_are_withdrawn_first_as_its_vm_ends` (a change holding the run's places all
  along; the name gone once the VM's end is followed, its address and pairing held, a name
  asked after refused `Network`).
- *Which member holds a contested UDP port* (the real-VM test, rewritten): learned from the
  members' own word, the holder alone being sent the datagrams of a client of the port
  published on the host. D122's ports reader cannot say it: `shards read ports` names every
  candidate ("the one listening of …", daemon/commands.rs `read_ports`), as `wire::Bound::to`
  does ("several alike where several claim it"), and the chooser tells no host its choice. The
  test grants one member at a time: as written it granted both in from a on the port, which
  the run's one address on the network does not tell apart (`shared-in` has a translation for
  each member's grant, init's `outside_batch`, the first that matches taking each new flow, so
  a's datagrams to c would reach b and c's wait never end; read in the code, its live run in
  the lane's report, and refused from now on, below). ROOT's second assertion, that a grant to
  the member not holding the port gets no flow, is not this design's: the chooser chooses for
  eth0's own address alone (D122's amendment of this day, ROOT's decision on slice 5's open
  item: "a network shared by runs, eth0's second address, is its members' grants'",
  chooser.rs), so a flow to the run's address on a shared network goes to the member its grant
  names, holder or not. "No flow" would take the chooser's choice at that address too:
  `shared-in` leaving a contested port to the chooser's chains, which would match the shared
  addresses again, zoning the holder's answers there both ways, and the forward chain telling
  a peer's flow from eth0's, whose ingress rule takes any source: slice 5 and D122's amendment
  redesigned, ROOT's to decide. The test holds the design as recorded: the
  holder granted alone is reached, the other not; the other granted alone is reached, the
  holder not; the holder answers eth0's own clients throughout.
- *Two members granted in on one port of the run's address* (item 5's "each port of its run's
  address one member's", which the run host did not hold): both were told, and the first
  translation took every flow. The run host now refuses the second `Unheld` before anything is
  told (`port_taken`: another member's grant in of that protocol meeting its ports, whatever its
  peer, as a host's port is one socket's whatever sends to it), D278's refusal of members "the
  microVM cannot hold apart", with no wire change. Tests: light,
  `api_run::hosted::tests::a_port_coming_in_to_a_runs_address_on_a_shared_network_is_one_members`;
  real VMs, the contested test's holder granted in beside the other, refused `Unheld`.

## 4. Start path (≤ 5 ms budget)

The target: a user's `shards run IMAGE COMMAND` to its command executing in its microVM
(usable), under 5 ms, boot included. A pooled run's VM restored its image's template,
resumed and connected before the request (D25, D26): what a restore costs is paid ahead
(restore below). Measured from the user's side: the client's spawn to the guest's
WORKLOAD_STARTED marker, on one clock across every process (`docs/research/measurements/
start-path`, PM M470), and by the image bench's `template_usable` (benches/image.rs).

Each step of a pooled run, Fedora (KVM, Intel Core i9-14900HX, 32 CPUs, a vCPU per host
CPU, Linux 6.19), alpine `true`, n 100, after PM M470, the host at load 20 to 30 from other
work (p50):

| Step | Cost | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| The client's launch: spawn to `main` of the 160 MB PIE `shards` (0.57 for `/usr/bin/true`; 180 more page faults, 125 of them its relocated read-only data, about 1.8 µs a page at load 2; its size costs nothing, and RELR takes the relocations' table but not the pages they write, PM M514) | 1.5–1.6 ms | [PM M470, M514] |
| The client: its request written to its slot | 0.37 ms | [PM M470] |
| The daemon's slot thread reads it, bridges it to its handling | 0.18 ms | [PM M470, D185] |
| The daemon prepares the run (image, spec), makes its container, keeps its request, sets it up; the host's CPUs read once for all of it (`Prepared::cpus`; on Linux each read walks the daemon's cgroups, and the start read them six times; the cut unmeasured) | 1.1 ms (0.55, 0.19, 0.13, 0.20) | [PM M470] |
| Its network process told (E1) | 0.07 ms | [PM M470] |
| The hand-over to the warm VM, TAKEN (13.5 ms before its descriptor room, M470) | 0.14–0.17 ms | [PM M470] |
| The guest starts the command: init takes the request 0.49, its names' files 0.48, the standby woken and set up 0.55, the exec until init hears it 1.67 | 2.5–3.5 ms | [PM M470, M292, M440] |
| **Spawn to usable** | **5.8 ms at load 20–26 (p90 7.3); 7.2 at load 30** | [PM M470, M471] |

Before the request, off its path: the restore itself (`to_beat`, a fresh VM process to its
guest running again: 9.1 ms on Fedora at load 15, against Firecracker's 10.4, PM M471),
and on HVF:

| Step | Cost | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `hv_vm_create` + `hv_gic_create` + sequential vCPU creation | ~11 + 2 + 7·n µs | [PM M2] |
| `mmap` snapshot memory `MAP_PRIVATE` + `hv_vm_map` | ~1–10 µs | [PM M3] |
| GIC restore (`hv_gic_set_state`; its registers alone, 20–30 µs, lose interrupts in flight) | ~1.2–1.3 ms | [PM M14, M45] |
| vCPU register restore | ~0.5 µs per vCPU | [PM M14] |
| Resume; guest faults in its working set | ~64 µs per MiB (1 vCPU), ~2.2× less with prefetch vCPUs; prefetched | [PM M5, M6, M30] |

Not met yet on Fedora: the guest's start of the command and the client's launch are most
of what is left.

Clone correctness hazards (RNG reseed via vmgenid, clock via vtimer offset, network
identity) are **pending** the snapshot research.

## 5. Phased plan with exit criteria

Each phase ends with committed E2E tests and benchmarks that run real VMs.

1. **VMM core on HVF (arm64).**
   - Scope: memory, Image loader, FDT, in-kernel GIC, PSCI (incl. CPU_ON), vtimer,
     UART console, virtio-mmio plus blk/console/rng/vsock, boot timer.
   - Exit: the bootstrap kernel (Linux 6.18 from Firecracker CI) boots to a shell
     from a real rootfs, SMP.
   - Exit: boot-time and VMM-RSS benchmarks run in the suite.
2. **Snapshot/restore plus warm pool.**
   - Scope: register-level GIC/vCPU/device state, lazy file-backed memory, clone
     identity fixes.
   - Exit: measured request → guest-running ≤ 1 ms p50 on the M5 Max.
3. **Guest stack v0.**
   - Scope: `shards-init`; tuned kernel built in a shards builder VM; OCI pull →
     rootfs image; `shards run vm IMAGE CMD`.
   - Built: our kernel (CI releases); virtio-pmem; the EROFS writer; layers → one EROFS
     image (D15); booting into an image to run a command (D16); the image store (D18);
     registry TLS, HTTP and auth (D19–D21); pulls (D22); `shards pull image` (D23); `shards run vm
     IMAGE` (D24); terminals (D16, D27); the kernel and shards-init shipped with shards
     (D28).
4. **In-VM engine.**
   - Scope: Docker Engine API subset → full; the rootless runtime (compatible, not
     containers underneath); networks, volumes, build; compose.
   - Proven by running the official Docker CLI/Compose conformance suites against
     it. Built since: domains for agents and harnesses (D59), the in-VM server (D60), the
     run's command apart from them (D115), the Engine API (D170) and Compose against it
     (D173).
5. **Host CLI/daemon parity and networking.**
   - Scope: userspace network stack, port publishing, per-VM and per-container
     isolation policy. Pending: networking research.
6. **KVM backend.**
   - Scope: x86_64 first, since hosted CI runners expose `/dev/kvm` (booting since
     4dd2799). Then arm64, tested inside an EL2-enabled shards VM on this host.
     virtio-pci plus VFIO.
7. **GPU classes** [GPU R1–R6]: Linux VFIO warm pools; macOS virtio-gpu/Venus plus
   a remoting broker.
8. **Hardening.**
   - Scope: seccomp/sandbox profiles, virtio fuzzing, stress-to-failure.
   - Pending: rootless-security research.

## 6. Testing and benchmarking rules

- **E2E means real VMs.** Tests boot real guests on the host hypervisor. Mocks are
  allowed only for pure parsers and state machines.
- **Every performance claim is backed by a committed benchmark.**
  - Report n, p50, p90, p99 and max.
  - Record host, OS and git revision.
  - Compare against Firecracker's published targets and methodology
    (boot-timer MMIO write, RSS excluding guest memory) [VIO §2.6–2.7].
- **Stress to failure.** Also: VM density until OOM, concurrent starts, fuzzing of
  device register and descriptor inputs, and fault injection on host I/O.
